    <div class="container">
      <h1 id="error-prone">Error Prone</h1>

<p>It’s common for even the best programmers to make simple mistakes. And
sometimes a refactoring which seems safe can leave behind code which will never
do what’s intended.</p>

<p>We’re used to getting help from the compiler, but it doesn’t do much beyond
static type checking. Using Error Prone to augment the compiler’s type
analysis, you can catch more mistakes before they cost you time, or end up as
bugs in production. We use Error Prone in Google’s Java build system to
eliminate classes of serious bugs from entering our code, and we’ve
open-sourced it, so you can too!</p>

<p><strong>Error Prone …</strong></p>

<ul>
  <li><strong>hooks into your standard build, so all developers run it without thinking</strong></li>
  <li><strong>tells you about mistakes immediately after they’re made</strong></li>
  <li><strong>produces suggested fixes, allowing you to build tooling on it</strong></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="how-it-works">How it works</h2>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">java.util.Set</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">java.util.HashSet</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">ShortSet</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">main</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">Set</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Short</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">s</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">HashSet</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">short</span> <span class="n">i</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="n">i</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span> <span class="mi">100</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="n">i</span><span class="o">++)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">);</span>
      <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">i</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">size</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>$ bazel build :hello
ERROR: example/myproject/BUILD:29:1: Java compilation in rule '//example/myproject:hello'
ShortSet.java:6: error: [CollectionIncompatibleType] Argument 'i - 1' should not be passed to this method;
its type int is not compatible with its collection's type argument Short
      s.remove(i - 1);
              ^
    (see https://errorprone.info/bugpattern/CollectionIncompatibleType)
1 error
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="testimonials">Testimonials</h2>

<p>Doug Lea, on learning of <a href="https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8176402">a bug we discovered in
ConcurrentHashMap</a>:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Definitely embarrassing. I guess I’m back to liking Error Prone even though
it sometimes annoys me :-)</p>
</blockquote>

sometimes a refactoring which seems safe can leave behind code which will never
do what’s intended.</p>

<p>We’re used to getting help from the compiler, but it doesn’t do much beyond

</ul>

    <div class="container">
      <h1 id="bug-patterns">Bug patterns</h1>

<p>This list is auto-generated from our sources.</p>

<p>Patterns which are marked <strong>Experimental</strong> will not be evaluated against your
code, unless you specifically configure Error Prone. The default checks are
marked <strong>On by default</strong>, and each release promotes some experimental checks
after we’ve vetted them against Google’s codebase.</p>

<h2 id="on-by-default--error">On by default : ERROR</h2>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AlwaysThrows">AlwaysThrows</a></strong><br />
Statically detects calls that will always fail at runtime.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AndroidInjectionBeforeSuper">AndroidInjectionBeforeSuper</a></strong><br />
AndroidInjection.inject() should always be invoked before calling super.lifecycleMethod()</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ArrayEquals">ArrayEquals</a></strong><br />
Reference equality used to compare arrays</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ArrayFillIncompatibleType">ArrayFillIncompatibleType</a></strong><br />
Arrays.fill(Object[], Object) called with incompatible types.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ArrayHashCode">ArrayHashCode</a></strong><br />
hashcode method on array does not hash array contents</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ArrayToString">ArrayToString</a></strong><br />
Calling toString on an array does not provide useful information</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ArraysAsListPrimitiveArray">ArraysAsListPrimitiveArray</a></strong><br />
Arrays.asList does not autobox primitive arrays, as one might expect.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AsyncCallableReturnsNull">AsyncCallableReturnsNull</a></strong><br />
AsyncCallable should not return a null Future, only a Future whose result is null.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AsyncFunctionReturnsNull">AsyncFunctionReturnsNull</a></strong><br />
AsyncFunction should not return a null Future, only a Future whose result is null.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AutoValueBuilderDefaultsInConstructor">AutoValueBuilderDefaultsInConstructor</a></strong><br />
Defaults for AutoValue Builders should be set in the factory method returning Builder instances, not the constructor</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AutoValueConstructorOrderChecker">AutoValueConstructorOrderChecker</a></strong><br />
Arguments to AutoValue constructor are in the wrong order</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BadAnnotationImplementation">BadAnnotationImplementation</a></strong><br />
Classes that implement Annotation must override equals and hashCode. Consider using AutoAnnotation instead of implementing Annotation by hand.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BadShiftAmount">BadShiftAmount</a></strong><br />
Shift by an amount that is out of range</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BanJNDI">BanJNDI</a></strong><br />
Using JNDI may deserialize user input via the `Serializable` API which is extremely dangerous</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BoxedPrimitiveEquality">BoxedPrimitiveEquality</a></strong><br />
Comparison using reference equality instead of value equality. Reference equality of boxed primitive types is usually not useful, as they are value objects, and it is bug-prone, as instances are cached for some values but not others.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BundleDeserializationCast">BundleDeserializationCast</a></strong><br />
Object serialized in Bundle may have been flattened to base type.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ChainingConstructorIgnoresParameter">ChainingConstructorIgnoresParameter</a></strong><br />
The called constructor accepts a parameter with the same name and type as one of its caller's parameters, but its caller doesn't pass that parameter to it.  It's likely that it was intended to.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CheckNotNullMultipleTimes">CheckNotNullMultipleTimes</a></strong><br />
A variable was checkNotNulled multiple times. Did you mean to check something else?</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CheckReturnValue">CheckReturnValue</a></strong><br />
The result of this call must be used</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CollectionIncompatibleType">CollectionIncompatibleType</a></strong><br />
Incompatible type as argument to Object-accepting Java collections method</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CollectionToArraySafeParameter">CollectionToArraySafeParameter</a></strong><br />
The type of the array parameter of Collection.toArray needs to be compatible with the array type</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComparableType">ComparableType</a></strong><br />
Implementing 'Comparable&lt;T&gt;' where T is not the same as the implementing class is incorrect, since it violates the symmetry contract of compareTo.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComparingThisWithNull">ComparingThisWithNull</a></strong><br />
this == null is always false, this != null is always true</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComparisonOutOfRange">ComparisonOutOfRange</a></strong><br />
Comparison to value that is out of range for the compared type</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CompatibleWithAnnotationMisuse">CompatibleWithAnnotationMisuse</a></strong><br />
@CompatibleWith's value is not a type argument.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CompileTimeConstant">CompileTimeConstant</a></strong><br />
Non-compile-time constant expression passed to parameter with @CompileTimeConstant type annotation.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComputeIfAbsentAmbiguousReference">ComputeIfAbsentAmbiguousReference</a></strong><br />
computeIfAbsent passes the map key to the provided class's constructor</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ConditionalExpressionNumericPromotion">ConditionalExpressionNumericPromotion</a></strong><br />
A conditional expression with numeric operands of differing types will perform binary numeric promotion of the operands; when these operands are of reference types, the expression's result may not be of the expected type.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ConstantOverflow">ConstantOverflow</a></strong><br />
Compile-time constant expression overflows</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DaggerProvidesNull">DaggerProvidesNull</a></strong><br />
Dagger @Provides methods may not return null unless annotated with @Nullable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DangerousLiteralNull">DangerousLiteralNull</a></strong><br />
This method is null-hostile: passing a null literal to it is always wrong</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DeadException">DeadException</a></strong><br />
Exception created but not thrown</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DeadThread">DeadThread</a></strong><br />
Thread created but not started</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DereferenceWithNullBranch">DereferenceWithNullBranch</a></strong><br />
Dereference of an expression with a null branch</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DiscardedPostfixExpression">DiscardedPostfixExpression</a></strong><br />
The result of this unary operation on a lambda parameter is discarded</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DoNotCall">DoNotCall</a></strong><br />
This method should not be called.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DoNotMock">DoNotMock</a></strong><br />
Identifies undesirable mocks.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DoubleBraceInitialization">DoubleBraceInitialization</a></strong><br />
Prefer collection factory methods or builders to the double-brace initialization pattern.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DuplicateMapKeys">DuplicateMapKeys</a></strong><br />
Map#ofEntries will throw an IllegalArgumentException if there are any duplicate keys</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DurationFrom">DurationFrom</a></strong><br />
Duration.from(Duration) returns itself; from(Period) throws a runtime exception.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DurationGetTemporalUnit">DurationGetTemporalUnit</a></strong><br />
Duration.get() only works with SECONDS or NANOS.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DurationTemporalUnit">DurationTemporalUnit</a></strong><br />
Duration APIs only work for DAYS or exact durations.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DurationToLongTimeUnit">DurationToLongTimeUnit</a></strong><br />
Unit mismatch when decomposing a Duration or Instant to call a &lt;long, TimeUnit&gt; API</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsHashCode">EqualsHashCode</a></strong><br />
Classes that override equals should also override hashCode.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsNaN">EqualsNaN</a></strong><br />
== NaN always returns false; use the isNaN methods instead</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsNull">EqualsNull</a></strong><br />
The contract of Object.equals() states that for any non-null reference value x, x.equals(null) should return false. If x is null, a NullPointerException is thrown. Consider replacing equals() with the == operator.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsReference">EqualsReference</a></strong><br />
== must be used in equals method to check equality to itself or an infinite loop will occur.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsWrongThing">EqualsWrongThing</a></strong><br />
Comparing different pairs of fields/getters in an equals implementation is probably a mistake.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerFormatString">FloggerFormatString</a></strong><br />
Invalid printf-style format string</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerLogString">FloggerLogString</a></strong><br />
Arguments to log(String) must be compile-time constants or parameters annotated with @CompileTimeConstant. If possible, use Flogger's formatting log methods instead.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerLogVarargs">FloggerLogVarargs</a></strong><br />
logVarargs should be used to pass through format strings and arguments.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerSplitLogStatement">FloggerSplitLogStatement</a></strong><br />
Splitting log statements and using Api instances directly breaks logging.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ForOverride">ForOverride</a></strong><br />
Method annotated @ForOverride must be protected or package-private and only invoked from declaring class, or from an override of the method</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FormatString">FormatString</a></strong><br />
Invalid printf-style format string</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FormatStringAnnotation">FormatStringAnnotation</a></strong><br />
Invalid format string passed to formatting method.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FromTemporalAccessor">FromTemporalAccessor</a></strong><br />
Certain combinations of javaTimeType.from(TemporalAccessor) will always throw a DateTimeException or return the parameter directly.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FunctionalInterfaceMethodChanged">FunctionalInterfaceMethodChanged</a></strong><br />
Casting a lambda to this @FunctionalInterface can cause a behavior change from casting to a functional superinterface, which is surprising to users.  Prefer decorator methods to this surprising behavior.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FuturesGetCheckedIllegalExceptionType">FuturesGetCheckedIllegalExceptionType</a></strong><br />
Futures.getChecked requires a checked exception type with a standard constructor.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FuzzyEqualsShouldNotBeUsedInEqualsMethod">FuzzyEqualsShouldNotBeUsedInEqualsMethod</a></strong><br />
DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals should never be used in an Object.equals() method</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/GetClassOnAnnotation">GetClassOnAnnotation</a></strong><br />
Calling getClass() on an annotation may return a proxy class</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/GetClassOnClass">GetClassOnClass</a></strong><br />
Calling getClass() on an object of type Class returns the Class object for java.lang.Class; you probably meant to operate on the object directly</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/GuardedBy">GuardedBy</a></strong><br />
Checks for unguarded accesses to fields and methods with @GuardedBy annotations</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/GuiceAssistedInjectScoping">GuiceAssistedInjectScoping</a></strong><br />
Scope annotation on implementation class of AssistedInject factory is not allowed</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BadImport">BadImport</a></strong><br />
Importing nested classes/static methods/static fields with commonly-used names can make code harder to read, because it may not be clear from the context exactly which type is being referred to. Qualifying the name with that of the containing class can make the code clearer.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BadInstanceof">BadInstanceof</a></strong><br />
instanceof used in a way that is equivalent to a null check.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BareDotMetacharacter">BareDotMetacharacter</a></strong><br />
"." is rarely useful as a regex, as it matches any character. To match a literal '.' character, instead write "\.".</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BigDecimalEquals">BigDecimalEquals</a></strong><br />
BigDecimal#equals has surprising behavior: it also compares scale.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BigDecimalLiteralDouble">BigDecimalLiteralDouble</a></strong><br />
new BigDecimal(double) loses precision in this case.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BooleanLiteral">BooleanLiteral</a></strong><br />
This expression can be written more clearly with a boolean literal.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BoxedPrimitiveConstructor">BoxedPrimitiveConstructor</a></strong><br />
valueOf or autoboxing provides better time and space performance</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BoxingComparator">BoxingComparator</a></strong><br />
Comparator.comparing() unnecessarily boxes numerical primitives; please use the primitive-specific method instead (e.g., comparingInt()).</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BugPatternNaming">BugPatternNaming</a></strong><br />
Giving BugPatterns a name different to the enclosing class can be confusing</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ByteBufferBackingArray">ByteBufferBackingArray</a></strong><br />
ByteBuffer.array() shouldn't be called unless ByteBuffer.arrayOffset() is used or if the ByteBuffer was initialized using ByteBuffer.wrap() or ByteBuffer.allocate().</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CacheLoaderNull">CacheLoaderNull</a></strong><br />
The result of CacheLoader#load must be non-null.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CanonicalDuration">CanonicalDuration</a></strong><br />
Duration can be expressed more clearly with different units</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CatchAndPrintStackTrace">CatchAndPrintStackTrace</a></strong><br />
Logging or rethrowing exceptions should usually be preferred to catching and calling printStackTrace</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CatchFail">CatchFail</a></strong><br />
Ignoring exceptions and calling fail() is unnecessary, and makes test output less useful</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ChainedAssertionLosesContext">ChainedAssertionLosesContext</a></strong><br />
Inside a Subject, use check(…) instead of assert*() to preserve user-supplied messages and other settings.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CharacterGetNumericValue">CharacterGetNumericValue</a></strong><br />
getNumericValue has unexpected behaviour: it interprets A-Z as base-36 digits with values 10-35, but also supports non-arabic numerals and miscellaneous numeric unicode characters like ㊷; consider using Character.digit or UCharacter.getUnicodeNumericValue instead</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ClassCanBeStatic">ClassCanBeStatic</a></strong><br />
Inner class is non-static but does not reference enclosing class</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ClassInitializationDeadlock">ClassInitializationDeadlock</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ClassNewInstance">ClassNewInstance</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CloseableProvides">CloseableProvides</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ClosingStandardOutputStreams">ClosingStandardOutputStreams</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CollectionUndefinedEquality">CollectionUndefinedEquality</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComparableAndComparator">ComparableAndComparator</a></strong><br />
Class should not implement both `Comparable` and `Comparator`</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CompareToZero">CompareToZero</a></strong><br />
The result of #compareTo or #compare should only be compared to 0. It is an implementation detail whether a given type returns strictly the values {-1, 0, +1} or others.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComplexBooleanConstant">ComplexBooleanConstant</a></strong><br />
Non-trivial compile time constant boolean expressions shouldn't be used.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EmptyBlockTag">EmptyBlockTag</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ComparisonContractViolated">ComparisonContractViolated</a></strong><br />
This comparison method violates the contract</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DeduplicateConstants">DeduplicateConstants</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DepAnn">DepAnn</a></strong><br />
Item documented with a @deprecated javadoc note is not annotated with @Deprecated</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EmptyIf">EmptyIf</a></strong><br />
Empty statement after if</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ExtendsAutoValue">ExtendsAutoValue</a></strong><br />

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/Java8ApiChecker">Java8ApiChecker</a></strong><br />
Use of class, field, or method that is not compatible with JDK 8</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/LongLiteralLowerCaseSuffix">LongLiteralLowerCaseSuffix</a></strong><br />
Prefer 'L' to 'l' for the suffix to long literals</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MissingRuntimeRetention">MissingRuntimeRetention</a></strong><br />
Scoping and qualifier annotations must have runtime retention.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MoreThanOneQualifier">MoreThanOneQualifier</a></strong><br />
Using more than one qualifier annotation on the same element is not allowed.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/NoAllocation">NoAllocation</a></strong><br />
@NoAllocation was specified on this method, but something was found that would trigger an allocation</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RefersToDaggerCodegen">RefersToDaggerCodegen</a></strong><br />
Don't refer to Dagger's internal or generated code</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/StaticOrDefaultInterfaceMethod">StaticOrDefaultInterfaceMethod</a></strong><br />
Static and default interface methods are not natively supported on older Android devices.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/StaticQualifiedUsingExpression">StaticQualifiedUsingExpression</a></strong><br />
A static variable or method should be qualified with a class name, not expression</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/SystemExitOutsideMain">SystemExitOutsideMain</a></strong><br />
Code that contains System.exit() is untestable.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TestExceptionChecker">TestExceptionChecker</a></strong><br />
Using @Test(expected=…) is discouraged, since the test will pass if <em>any</em> statement in the test method throws the expected exception</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ThreadSafe">ThreadSafe</a></strong><br />
Type declaration annotated with @ThreadSafe is not thread safe</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UseCorrectAssertInTests">UseCorrectAssertInTests</a></strong><br />
Java assert is used in testing code. For testing purposes, prefer using Truth-based assertions.</p>

<h2 id="experimental--warning">Experimental : WARNING</h2>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AnnotationPosition">AnnotationPosition</a></strong><br />
Annotations should be positioned after Javadocs, but before modifiers.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AssertFalse">AssertFalse</a></strong><br />
Assertions may be disabled at runtime and do not guarantee that execution will halt here; consider throwing an exception instead</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AssistedInjectAndInjectOnConstructors">AssistedInjectAndInjectOnConstructors</a></strong><br />
@AssistedInject and @Inject should not be used on different constructors in the same class.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AvoidObjectArrays">AvoidObjectArrays</a></strong><br />
Object arrays are inferior to collections in almost every way. Prefer immutable collections (e.g., ImmutableSet, ImmutableList, etc.) over an object array whenever possible.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BinderIdentityRestoredDangerously">BinderIdentityRestoredDangerously</a></strong><br />
A call to Binder.clearCallingIdentity() should be followed by Binder.restoreCallingIdentity() in a finally block. Otherwise the wrong Binder identity may be used by subsequent code.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BindingToUnqualifiedCommonType">BindingToUnqualifiedCommonType</a></strong><br />
This code declares a binding for a common value type without a Qualifier annotation.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BuilderReturnThis">BuilderReturnThis</a></strong><br />
Builder instance method does not return 'this'</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CanIgnoreReturnValueSuggester">CanIgnoreReturnValueSuggester</a></strong><br />
Methods that always return 'this' (or return an input parameter) should be annotated with @com.google.errorprone.annotations.CanIgnoreReturnValue</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CannotMockFinalClass">CannotMockFinalClass</a></strong><br />
Mockito cannot mock final classes</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CannotMockMethod">CannotMockMethod</a></strong><br />
Mockito cannot mock final or static methods, and can't detect this at runtime</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CatchingUnchecked">CatchingUnchecked</a></strong><br />
This catch block catches `Exception`, but can only catch unchecked exceptions. Consider catching RuntimeException (or something more specific) instead so it is more apparent that no checked exceptions are being handled.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/CheckedExceptionNotThrown">CheckedExceptionNotThrown</a></strong><br />
This method cannot throw a checked exception that it claims to. This may cause consumers of the API to incorrectly attempt to handle, or propagate, this exception.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ConstantPatternCompile">ConstantPatternCompile</a></strong><br />
Variables initialized with Pattern#compile calls on constants can be constants</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DefaultLocale">DefaultLocale</a></strong><br />
Implicit use of the JVM default locale, which can result in differing behaviour between JVM executions.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/DifferentNameButSame">DifferentNameButSame</a></strong><br />
This type is referred to in different ways within this file, which may be confusing.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsBrokenForNull">EqualsBrokenForNull</a></strong><br />
equals() implementation may throw NullPointerException when given null</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ExpectedExceptionChecker">ExpectedExceptionChecker</a></strong><br />
Prefer assertThrows to ExpectedException</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ExplicitArrayForVarargs">ExplicitArrayForVarargs</a></strong><br />
Avoid explicit array creation for varargs</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerLogWithCause">FloggerLogWithCause</a></strong><br />
Setting the caught exception as the cause of the log message may provide more context for anyone debugging errors.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerMessageFormat">FloggerMessageFormat</a></strong><br />
Invalid message format-style format specifier ({0}), expected printf-style (%s)</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerRedundantIsEnabled">FloggerRedundantIsEnabled</a></strong><br />
Logger level check is already implied in the log() call. An explicit atLEVEL().isEnabled() check is redundant.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerRequiredModifiers">FloggerRequiredModifiers</a></strong><br />
FluentLogger.forEnclosingClass should always be saved to a private static final field.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerWithCause">FloggerWithCause</a></strong><br />
Calling withCause(Throwable) with an inline allocated Throwable is discouraged. Consider using withStackTrace(StackSize) instead, and specifying a reduced stack size (e.g. SMALL, MEDIUM or LARGE) instead of FULL, to improve performance.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FloggerWithoutCause">FloggerWithoutCause</a></strong><br />
Use withCause to associate Exceptions with log statements</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FunctionalInterfaceClash">FunctionalInterfaceClash</a></strong><br />
Overloads will be ambiguous when passing lambda arguments.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/HardCodedSdCardPath">HardCodedSdCardPath</a></strong><br />
Hardcoded reference to /sdcard</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/IdentifierName">IdentifierName</a></strong><br />
Methods and non-static variables should be named in lowerCamelCase</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/InconsistentOverloads">InconsistentOverloads</a></strong><br />
The ordering of parameters in overloaded methods should be as consistent as possible (when viewed from left to right)</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/InitializeInline">InitializeInline</a></strong><br />
Initializing variables in their declaring statement is clearer, where possible.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/InterfaceWithOnlyStatics">InterfaceWithOnlyStatics</a></strong><br />
This interface only contains static fields and methods; consider making it a final class instead to prevent subclassing.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/InterruptedExceptionSwallowed">InterruptedExceptionSwallowed</a></strong><br />
This catch block appears to be catching an explicitly declared InterruptedException as an Exception/Throwable and not handling the interruption separately.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/Interruption">Interruption</a></strong><br />
Always pass 'false' to 'Future.cancel()', unless you are propagating a cancellation-with-interrupt from another caller</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MissingDefault">MissingDefault</a></strong><br />
The Google Java Style Guide requires that each switch statement includes a default statement group (even if it contains no code) unless the switch statement covers all values of an enum.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MissingJavadoc">MissingJavadoc</a></strong><br />
Public types must have Javadoc comments.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MockitoDoSetup">MockitoDoSetup</a></strong><br />
Prefer using when/thenReturn over doReturn/when for additional type safety.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MutableGuiceModule">MutableGuiceModule</a></strong><br />
Fields in Guice modules should be final</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/NegativeBoolean">NegativeBoolean</a></strong><br />
Prefer positive boolean names</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/NonCanonicalStaticMemberImport">NonCanonicalStaticMemberImport</a></strong><br />
Static import of member uses non-canonical name</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/NonFinalStaticField">NonFinalStaticField</a></strong><br />
Static fields should almost always be final.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PreferJavaTimeOverload">PreferJavaTimeOverload</a></strong><br />
Prefer using java.time-based APIs when available. Note that this checker does not and cannot guarantee that the overloads have equivalent semantics, but that is generally the case with overloaded methods.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PreferPreconditions">PreferPreconditions</a></strong><br />
Consider using Preconditions instead of explicit if-throw for parameter validation.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PreferredInterfaceType">PreferredInterfaceType</a></strong><br />
This type can be more specific.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PrimitiveArrayPassedToVarargsMethod">PrimitiveArrayPassedToVarargsMethod</a></strong><br />
Passing a primitive array to a varargs method is usually wrong</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/QualifierWithTypeUse">QualifierWithTypeUse</a></strong><br />
Injection frameworks currently don't understand Qualifiers in TYPE_PARAMETER or TYPE_USE contexts.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RecordComponentAccessorAnnotationConflict">RecordComponentAccessorAnnotationConflict</a></strong><br />
Annotation on record component is ignored.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RedundantNullCheck">RedundantNullCheck</a></strong><br />
Null check on an expression that is statically determined to be non-null according to language semantics or nullness annotations.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RedundantOverride">RedundantOverride</a></strong><br />
This overriding method is redundant, and can be removed.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RedundantThrows">RedundantThrows</a></strong><br />
Thrown exception is a subtype of another</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/StringFormatWithLiteral">StringFormatWithLiteral</a></strong><br />
There is no need to use String.format() when all the arguments are literals.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/StronglyTypeByteString">StronglyTypeByteString</a></strong><br />
This primitive byte array is only used to construct ByteStrings. It would be clearer to strongly type the field instead.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/StronglyTypeTime">StronglyTypeTime</a></strong><br />
This primitive integral type is only used to construct time types. It would be clearer to strongly type the field instead.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/SunApi">SunApi</a></strong><br />
Usage of internal proprietary API which may be removed in a future release</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/SuppressWarningsWithoutExplanation">SuppressWarningsWithoutExplanation</a></strong><br />
Use of @SuppressWarnings should be accompanied by a comment describing why the warning is safe to ignore.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/SystemOut">SystemOut</a></strong><br />
Production code should not print to standard out or standard error. Standard out and standard error should only be used for debugging.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ThrowSpecificExceptions">ThrowSpecificExceptions</a></strong><br />
Base exception classes should be treated as abstract. If the exception is intended to be caught, throw a domain-specific exception. Otherwise, prefer a more specific exception for clarity. Common alternatives include: AssertionError, IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, and (Guava's) VerifyException.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TimeUnitMismatch">TimeUnitMismatch</a></strong><br />
An value that appears to be represented in one unit is used where another appears to be required (e.g., seconds where nanos are needed)</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TooManyParameters">TooManyParameters</a></strong><br />
A large number of parameters on public APIs should be avoided.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TransientMisuse">TransientMisuse</a></strong><br />
Static fields are implicitly transient, so the explicit modifier is unnecessary</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TruthContainsExactlyElementsInUsage">TruthContainsExactlyElementsInUsage</a></strong><br />
containsExactly is preferred over containsExactlyElementsIn when creating new iterables.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TryWithResourcesVariable">TryWithResourcesVariable</a></strong><br />
This variable is unnecessary, the try-with-resources resource can be a reference to a final or effectively final variable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnescapedEntity">UnescapedEntity</a></strong><br />
Javadoc is interpreted as HTML, so HTML entities such as &amp;, &lt;, &gt; must be escaped. If this finding seems wrong (e.g. is within a @code or @literal tag), check whether the tag could be malformed and not recognised by the compiler.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessarilyFullyQualified">UnnecessarilyFullyQualified</a></strong><br />
This fully qualified name is unambiguous to the compiler if imported.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessarilyUsedValue">UnnecessarilyUsedValue</a></strong><br />
The result of this API is ignorable, so it does not need to be captured / assigned into an `unused` variable.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessarilyVisible">UnnecessarilyVisible</a></strong><br />
Some methods (such as those annotated with @Inject or @Provides) are only intended to be called by a framework, and so should have default visibility.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryAnonymousClass">UnnecessaryAnonymousClass</a></strong><br />
Implementing a functional interface is unnecessary; prefer to implement the functional interface method directly and use a method reference instead.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryDefaultInEnumSwitch">UnnecessaryDefaultInEnumSwitch</a></strong><br />
Switch handles all enum values: an explicit default case is unnecessary and defeats error checking for non-exhaustive switches.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryFinal">UnnecessaryFinal</a></strong><br />
Since Java 8, it's been unnecessary to make local variables and parameters `final` for use in lambdas or anonymous classes. Marking them as `final` is weakly discouraged, as it adds a fair amount of noise for minimal benefit.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryOptionalGet">UnnecessaryOptionalGet</a></strong><br />
This code can be simplified by directly using the lambda parameters instead of calling get..() on optional.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessarySemicolon">UnnecessarySemicolon</a></strong><br />
Unnecessary semicolons should be omitted. For empty block statements, prefer {}.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryTestMethodPrefix">UnnecessaryTestMethodPrefix</a></strong><br />
A `test` prefix for a JUnit4 test is redundant, and a holdover from JUnit3. The `@Test` annotation makes it clear it's a test.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnsafeLocaleUsage">UnsafeLocaleUsage</a></strong><br />
Possible unsafe operation related to the java.util.Locale class.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnusedException">UnusedException</a></strong><br />
This catch block catches an exception and re-throws another, but swallows the caught exception rather than setting it as a cause. This can make debugging harder.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UrlInSee">UrlInSee</a></strong><br />
URLs should not be used in @see tags; they are designed for Java elements which could be used with @link.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UsingJsr305CheckReturnValue">UsingJsr305CheckReturnValue</a></strong><br />
Prefer ErrorProne's @CheckReturnValue over JSR305's version.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/Var">Var</a></strong><br />
Non-constant variable missing @Var annotation</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/Varifier">Varifier</a></strong><br />
Consider using `var` here to avoid boilerplate.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/YodaCondition">YodaCondition</a></strong><br />
The non-constant portion of a comparison generally comes first. For equality, prefer e.equals(CONSTANT) if e is non-null or Objects.equals(e, CONSTANT) if e may be null. For standard operators, prefer e &lt;OPERATION&gt; CONSTANT.</p>

<h2 id="experimental--suggestion">Experimental : SUGGESTION</h2>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AddNullMarkedToClass">AddNullMarkedToClass</a></strong><br />
Apply @NullMarked to this class</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AddNullMarkedToPackageInfo">AddNullMarkedToPackageInfo</a></strong><br />
Apply @NullMarked to this package</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AnnotationMirrorToString">AnnotationMirrorToString</a></strong><br />
AnnotationMirror#toString doesn't use fully qualified type names, prefer auto-common's AnnotationMirrors#toString</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/AnnotationValueToString">AnnotationValueToString</a></strong><br />
AnnotationValue#toString doesn't use fully qualified type names, prefer auto-common's AnnotationValues#toString</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/BooleanParameter">BooleanParameter</a></strong><br />
Use parameter comments to document ambiguous literals</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ClassNamedLikeTypeParameter">ClassNamedLikeTypeParameter</a></strong><br />
This class's name looks like a Type Parameter.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ConstantField">ConstantField</a></strong><br />
Fields with CONSTANT_CASE names should be both static and final</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/EqualsMissingNullable">EqualsMissingNullable</a></strong><br />
Method overrides Object.equals but does not have @Nullable on its parameter</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FieldCanBeFinal">FieldCanBeFinal</a></strong><br />
This field is only assigned during initialization; consider making it final</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FieldCanBeLocal">FieldCanBeLocal</a></strong><br />
This field can be replaced with a local variable in the methods that use it.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FieldCanBeStatic">FieldCanBeStatic</a></strong><br />
A final field initialized at compile-time with an instance of an immutable type can be static.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/FieldMissingNullable">FieldMissingNullable</a></strong><br />
Field is assigned (or compared against) a definitely null value but is not annotated @Nullable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ForEachIterable">ForEachIterable</a></strong><br />
This loop can be replaced with an enhanced for loop.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ImmutableMemberCollection">ImmutableMemberCollection</a></strong><br />
If you don't intend to mutate a member collection prefer using Immutable types.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ImmutableRefactoring">ImmutableRefactoring</a></strong><br />
Refactors uses of the JSR 305 @Immutable to Error Prone's annotation</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ImmutableSetForContains">ImmutableSetForContains</a></strong><br />
This private static ImmutableList is only used for contains, containsAll or isEmpty checks; prefer ImmutableSet.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ImplementAssertionWithChaining">ImplementAssertionWithChaining</a></strong><br />
Prefer check(…), which usually generates more readable failure messages.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/LambdaFunctionalInterface">LambdaFunctionalInterface</a></strong><br />
Use Java's utility functional interfaces instead of Function&lt;A, B&gt; for primitive types.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MethodCanBeStatic">MethodCanBeStatic</a></strong><br />
This method does not reference the enclosing instance and can be static</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MissingBraces">MissingBraces</a></strong><br />
The Google Java Style Guide requires braces to be used with if, else, for, do and while statements, even when the body is empty or contains only a single statement.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MixedArrayDimensions">MixedArrayDimensions</a></strong><br />
C-style array declarations should not be used</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MultiVariableDeclaration">MultiVariableDeclaration</a></strong><br />
Variable declarations should declare only one variable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/MultipleTopLevelClasses">MultipleTopLevelClasses</a></strong><br />
Source files should not contain multiple top-level class declarations</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PackageLocation">PackageLocation</a></strong><br />
Package names should match the directory they are declared in</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ParameterComment">ParameterComment</a></strong><br />
Non-standard parameter comment; prefer `/* paramName= */ arg`</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ParameterMissingNullable">ParameterMissingNullable</a></strong><br />
Parameter has handling for null but is not annotated @Nullable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PrivateConstructorForNoninstantiableModule">PrivateConstructorForNoninstantiableModule</a></strong><br />
Add a private constructor to modules that will not be instantiated by Dagger.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PrivateConstructorForUtilityClass">PrivateConstructorForUtilityClass</a></strong><br />
Classes which are not intended to be instantiated should be made non-instantiable with a private constructor. This includes utility classes (classes with only static members), and the main class.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/PublicApiNamedStreamShouldReturnStream">PublicApiNamedStreamShouldReturnStream</a></strong><br />
Public methods named stream() are generally expected to return a type whose name ends with Stream. Consider choosing a different method name instead.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RemoveUnusedImports">RemoveUnusedImports</a></strong><br />
Unused imports</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/RequireNonNullRefactoring">RequireNonNullRefactoring</a></strong><br />
Refactor explicit null checks to Objects.requireNonNull</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ReturnMissingNullable">ReturnMissingNullable</a></strong><br />
Method returns a definitely null value but is not annotated @Nullable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ReturnsNullCollection">ReturnsNullCollection</a></strong><br />
Method has a collection return type and returns {@code null} in some cases but does not annotate the method as @Nullable. See Effective Java 3rd Edition Item 54.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ScopeOnModule">ScopeOnModule</a></strong><br />
Scopes on modules have no function and will soon be an error.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/SwitchDefault">SwitchDefault</a></strong><br />
The default case of a switch should appear at the end of the last statement group</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/SymbolToString">SymbolToString</a></strong><br />
Element#toString shouldn't be used for comparison as it is expensive and fragile.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/ThrowsUncheckedException">ThrowsUncheckedException</a></strong><br />
Unchecked exceptions do not need to be declared in the method signature.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TraditionalJavadocToMarkdown">TraditionalJavadocToMarkdown</a></strong><br />
Converts traditional Javadoc comments into Markdown Javadoc comments</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TryFailRefactoring">TryFailRefactoring</a></strong><br />
Prefer assertThrows to try/fail</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TypeParameterNaming">TypeParameterNaming</a></strong><br />
Type parameters must be a single letter with an optional numeric suffix, or an UpperCamelCase name followed by the letter 'T'.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/TypeToString">TypeToString</a></strong><br />
TypeMirror#toString shouldn't be used for comparison as it is expensive and fragile.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UngroupedOverloads">UngroupedOverloads</a></strong><br />
Constructors and methods with the same name should appear sequentially with no other code in between, even when modifiers such as static or private differ between the methods. Please re-order or re-name methods.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryBoxedAssignment">UnnecessaryBoxedAssignment</a></strong><br />
This expression can be implicitly boxed.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryBoxedVariable">UnnecessaryBoxedVariable</a></strong><br />
It is unnecessary for this variable to be boxed. Use the primitive instead.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessarySetDefault">UnnecessarySetDefault</a></strong><br />
Unnecessary call to NullPointerTester#setDefault</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UnnecessaryStaticImport">UnnecessaryStaticImport</a></strong><br />
Using static imports for types is unnecessary</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/UseEnumSwitch">UseEnumSwitch</a></strong><br />
Prefer using a switch instead of a chained if-else for enums</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/VarWithPrimitive">VarWithPrimitive</a></strong><br />
Avoid using `var` with primitive types. Explicit primitive type names are short and clear, and `var` provides no benefit in readability while potentially hiding the type.</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/VoidMissingNullable">VoidMissingNullable</a></strong><br />
The type Void is not annotated @Nullable</p>

<p><strong><a href="bugpattern/WildcardImport">WildcardImport</a></strong><br />
Wildcard imports, static or otherwise, should not be used</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-9 col-sm-9">
          <h1>Installation</h1>
          <p>Our goal is to make it simple to add Error Prone checks to your existing Java
compilation. Please note that Error Prone must be run on JDK 21 or newer. (It
can still be used to build Java 8 code by setting the appropriate <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-source</code> /
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-target</code> / <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-bootclasspath</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--release</code> flags.) If you still have to build
with an older JDK version you can use
<a href="#running-error-prone-on-earlier-jdk-versions">older unmaintained Error Prone versions</a>.</p>

<p>Please join our
<a href="https://groups.google.com/group/error-prone-announce">mailing list</a> to know
when a new version is released!</p>

<h2 id="bazel">Bazel</h2>

<p>Error Prone works out of the box with <a href="https://bazel.build">Bazel</a>.</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>java_library(
    name = "hello",
    srcs = ["Hello.java"],
)
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>$ bazel build :hello
ERROR: example/myproject/BUILD:29:1: Java compilation in rule '//example/myproject:hello'
examples/maven/error_prone_should_flag/src/main/java/Main.java:20: error: [DeadException] Exception created but not thrown
    new Exception();
    ^
    (see https://errorprone.info/bugpattern/DeadException)
  Did you mean 'throw new Exception();'?
1 error
BazelJavaBuilder threw exception: java compilation returned status ERROR
INFO: Elapsed time: 1.989s, Critical Path: 1.69s
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="maven">Maven</h2>

<p>Edit your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">pom.xml</code> file to add settings to the maven-compiler-plugin:</p>

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nt">&lt;build&gt;</span>
    <span class="nt">&lt;plugins&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;plugin&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;groupId&gt;</span>org.apache.maven.plugins<span class="nt">&lt;/groupId&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;artifactId&gt;</span>maven-compiler-plugin<span class="nt">&lt;/artifactId&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;version&gt;</span>3.11.0<span class="nt">&lt;/version&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;configuration&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;source&gt;</span>17<span class="nt">&lt;/source&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;target&gt;</span>8<span class="nt">&lt;/target&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;encoding&gt;</span>UTF-8<span class="nt">&lt;/encoding&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;compilerArgs&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-XDcompilePolicy=simple<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>--should-stop=ifError=FLOW<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-Xplugin:ErrorProne<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="c">&lt;!-- necessary only if building with JDK21: https://github.com/google/error-prone/issues/5426 --&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-XDaddTypeAnnotationsToSymbol=true<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;/compilerArgs&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;annotationProcessorPaths&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;path&gt;</span>
              <span class="nt">&lt;groupId&gt;</span>com.google.errorprone<span class="nt">&lt;/groupId&gt;</span>
              <span class="nt">&lt;artifactId&gt;</span>error_prone_core<span class="nt">&lt;/artifactId&gt;</span>
              <span class="nt">&lt;version&gt;</span>${error-prone.version}<span class="nt">&lt;/version&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;/path&gt;</span>
            <span class="c">&lt;!-- Other annotation processors go here.

            If 'annotationProcessorPaths' is set, processors will no longer be
            discovered on the regular -classpath; see also 'Using Error Prone
            together with other annotation processors' below. --&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;/annotationProcessorPaths&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;/configuration&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;/plugin&gt;</span>
    <span class="nt">&lt;/plugins&gt;</span>
  <span class="nt">&lt;/build&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Additional flags are required due to
<a href="https://openjdk.java.net/jeps/396">JEP 396: Strongly Encapsulate JDK Internals by Default</a>.</p>

<p>If your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">maven-compiler-plugin</code> uses an external executable, e.g. because
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;fork&gt;</code> is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">true</code> or because the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">maven-toolchains-plugin</code> is enabled, add the
following under <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">compilerArgs</code> in the configuration above:</p>

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.file=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.model=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.parser=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.processing=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.tree=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.util=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-opens=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.code=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-J--add-opens=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.comp=ALL-UNNAMED<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Otherwise, add the following to the
<a href="https://maven.apache.org/configure.html#mvn-jvm-config-file">.mvn/jvm.config</a>
file:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.file=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.model=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.parser=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.processing=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.tree=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-exports jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.util=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.code=ALL-UNNAMED
--add-opens jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.comp=ALL-UNNAMED
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>See the <a href="https://errorprone.info/docs/flags#maven">flags documentation</a> for
details on how to customize the plugin’s behavior.</p>

<h2 id="gradle">Gradle</h2>

<p>The gradle plugin is an external contribution. The documentation and code is at
<a href="https://github.com/tbroyer/gradle-errorprone-plugin">tbroyer/gradle-errorprone-plugin</a>.</p>

<h2 id="ant">Ant</h2>

<p>Download the following artifacts from maven:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">error_prone_core-${EP_VERSION?}-with-dependencies.jar</code> from
<a href="https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/google/errorprone/error_prone_core/">https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/google/errorprone/error_prone_core/</a></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">dataflow-errorprone-${DATAFLOW_VERSION?}.jar</code> from
<a href="https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/eisop/dataflow-errorprone/">https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/eisop/dataflow-errorprone/</a></li>
</ul>

<p>and add the following javac task to your project’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">build.xml</code> file:</p>

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>    <span class="nt">&lt;path</span> <span class="na">id=</span><span class="s">"processorpath.ref"</span><span class="nt">&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;pathelement</span> <span class="na">location=</span><span class="s">"${user.home}/.m2/repository/com/google/errorprone/error_prone_core/${error-prone.version}/error_prone_core-${error-prone.version}-with-dependencies.jar"</span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;pathelement</span> <span class="na">location=</span><span class="s">"${user.home}/.m2/repository/io/github/eisop/dataflow-errorprone/${dataflow.version}/dataflow-errorprone-${dataflow.version}.jar"</span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
    <span class="nt">&lt;/path&gt;</span>

    <span class="nt">&lt;javac</span> <span class="na">srcdir=</span><span class="s">"src"</span> <span class="na">destdir=</span><span class="s">"build"</span> <span class="na">fork=</span><span class="s">"yes"</span> <span class="na">includeantruntime=</span><span class="s">"no"</span><span class="nt">&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-XDcompilePolicy=simple"</span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"--should-stop=ifError=FLOW"</span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-processorpath"</span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">pathref=</span><span class="s">"processorpath.ref"</span><span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-Xplugin:ErrorProne -Xep:DeadException:ERROR"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.file=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.model=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.parser=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.processing=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.tree=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-exports=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.util=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-opens=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.code=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;compilerarg</span> <span class="na">value=</span><span class="s">"-J--add-opens=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.comp=ALL-UNNAMED"</span> <span class="nt">/&gt;</span>
    <span class="nt">&lt;/javac&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Setting the following <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--add-exports=</code> flags is required on JDK 16 and newer due
to
<a href="https://openjdk.java.net/jeps/396">JEP 396: Strongly Encapsulate JDK Internals by Default</a>:</p>

<h2 id="intellij-idea">IntelliJ IDEA</h2>

<p>To add the plugin, start the IDE and find the Plugins dialog. Browse
Repositories, choose Category: Build, and find the Error-prone plugin.
Right-click and choose “Download and install”. The IDE will restart after you’ve
exited these dialogs.</p>

<p>To enable Error Prone, choose <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Settings | Compiler | Java Compiler | Use
compiler: Javac with error-prone</code> and also make sure <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Settings | Compiler | Use
external build</code> is NOT selected.</p>

<h2 id="eclipse">Eclipse</h2>

<p>Ideally, you should find out about failed Error Prone checks as you code in
eclipse, thanks to the continuous compilation by ECJ (eclipse compiler for
Java). But this is an architectural challenge, as Error Prone currently relies
heavily on the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.sun.*</code> APIs for accessing the AST and symbol table.</p>

<p>For now, Eclipse users should use the Findbugs eclipse plugin instead, as it
catches many of the same issues.</p>

<h2 id="command-line">Command Line</h2>

<p>Error Prone supports the
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/jdk/api/javac/tree/com/sun/source/util/Plugin.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.sun.source.util.Plugin</code></a>
API, which can be used by adding Error Prone to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-processorpath</code> and setting
the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Xplugin</code> flag.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>wget https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/google/errorprone/error_prone_core/<span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">EP_VERSION</span><span class="p">?</span><span class="k">}</span>/error_prone_core-<span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">EP_VERSION</span><span class="p">?</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="nt">-with-dependencies</span>.jar
wget https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/eisop/dataflow-errorprone/<span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">DATAFLOW_VERSION</span><span class="p">?</span><span class="k">}</span>/dataflow-errorprone-<span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">DATAFLOW_VERSION</span><span class="p">?</span><span class="k">}</span>.jar
javac <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.file<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.main<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.model<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.parser<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.processing<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.tree<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-exports</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.util<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-opens</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.code<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-J--add-opens</span><span class="o">=</span>jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.comp<span class="o">=</span>ALL-UNNAMED <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-XDcompilePolicy</span><span class="o">=</span>simple <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">--should-stop</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="nv">ifError</span><span class="o">=</span>FLOW <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="nt">-processorpath</span> error_prone_core-<span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">EP_VERSION</span><span class="p">?</span><span class="k">}</span><span class="nt">-with-dependencies</span>.jar:dataflow-errorprone-<span class="k">${</span><span class="nv">DATAFLOW_VERSION</span><span class="p">?</span><span class="k">}</span>.jar <span class="se">\</span>
  <span class="s1">'-Xplugin:ErrorProne -XepDisableAllChecks -Xep:CollectionIncompatibleType:ERROR'</span> <span class="se">\</span>
  ShortSet.java
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>ShortSet.java:8: error: [CollectionIncompatibleType] Argument 'i - 1' should not be passed to this method; its type int is not compatible with its collection's type argument Short
      s.remove(i - 1);
              ^
    (see https://errorprone.info/bugpattern/CollectionIncompatibleType)
1 error
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--add-exports</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--add-opens</code> flags are required due to
<a href="https://openjdk.java.net/jeps/396">JEP 396: Strongly Encapsulate JDK Internals by Default</a>:</p>

<h2 id="my-build-system-isnt-listed-here">My build system isn’t listed here</h2>

<p>If you’re an end-user of the build system, you can
<a href="https://github.com/google/error-prone/issues">file a bug to request integration</a>.</p>

<p>If you develop a build system, you should create an integration for your users!
Here are some basics to get you started:</p>

<p>Error-prone is implemented as a compiler hook, using an internal mechanism in
javac. To install our hook, we override the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">main()</code> method in
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.sun.tools.javac.main.Main</code>.</p>

<p>Find the spot in your build system where javac’s main method is called. This is
assuming you call javac in-process, rather than shell’ing out to the javac
executable on the machine (which would be pretty lame since it’s hard to know
where that’s located).</p>

<p>First, add Error Prone’s core library to the right classpath. It will need to be
visible to the classloader which currently locates the javac Main class. Then
replace the call of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javac.main.Main.main()</code> with the Error Prone compiler:</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">return new ErrorProneCompiler.Builder().build().compile(args) == 0</code></p>

<h2 id="using-error-prone-together-with-other-annotation-processors">Using Error Prone together with other annotation processors</h2>

<p>All of the above instructions use the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javac</code> option <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-processorpath</code> which has
side-effect of causing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javac</code> to no longer scan the compile classpath for
annotation processors. If you are using other annotation processors in addition
to Error Prone, such as
<a href="https://github.com/google/auto/tree/master/value">AutoValue</a>, then you will
need to add their JARs to your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-processorpath</code> argument. The mechanics of this
will vary according to the build tool you are using.</p>

<h2 id="running-error-prone-on-earlier-jdk-versions">Running Error Prone on earlier JDK versions</h2>

<ul>
  <li>Error Prone 2.10.0 is the latest version to support running on JDK 8.</li>
  <li>Error Prone 2.31.0 is the latest version to support running on JDK 11.</li>
  <li>Error Prone 2.42.0 is the latest version to support running on JDK 17.</li>
</ul>

<p>(Compiling the Java 8 language level is still supported by using a javac from a
newer JDK, and setting the appropriate <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-source</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-target</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-bootclasspath</code> or
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">--release</code> flags).</p>

<p>For instructions on using Error Prone 2.10.0 with JDK 8, see
<a href="https://github.com/google/error-prone/blob/f8e33bc460be82ab22256a7ef8b979d7a2cacaba/docs/installation.md">this older version of the installation instructions</a>.</p>

          <h1>
            AndroidInjectionBeforeSuper<br>
            <small>AndroidInjection.inject() should always be invoked before calling super.lifecycleMethod()</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Members injection should always be called as early as possible to avoid
uninitialized @Inject members. This is also crucial to protect against bugs
during configuration changes and reattached Fragments to make sure that each
framework type is injected in the appropriate order.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AndroidInjectionBeforeSuper")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ArrayEquals<br>
            <small>Reference equality used to compare arrays</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Generally when comparing arrays for equality, the programmer intends to check
that the contents of the arrays are equal rather than that they are actually the
same object. But many commonly used equals methods compare arrays for reference
equality rather than content equality. These include the instance <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.equals()</code>
method, Guava’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.common.base.Objects#equal()</code>, JDK’s
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Objects#equals()</code>, and Android’s
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">androidx.core.ObjectsCompat#equals()</code>.</p>

<p>If reference equality is needed, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">==</code> should be used instead for clarity.
Otherwise, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Arrays#equals()</code> to compare the contents of the
arrays.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ArrayEquals")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ArrayFillIncompatibleType<br>
            <small>Arrays.fill(Object[], Object) called with incompatible types.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arrays.fill(Object[], Object)</code> is used to copy a reference into every slot of
an array.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">];</span>
<span class="nc">Arrays</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">fill</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"life"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="c1">// 42 references to the same String instance of "life" in the foo array</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>However, because of Array covariance (e.g.: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String[]</code> is assignable to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object[]</code>), and the signature of Arrays.fill is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arrays.fill(Object[],
Object)</code>, this also allows you to do the following:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">];</span>
<span class="nc">Arrays</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">fill</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// ArrayStoreException! Integer can't be put into a String[]</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This check detects the above circumstances, and won’t let you attempt to put
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer</code>s into a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String[]</code>.</p>

<h2 id="what-about-lists">What about Lists?</h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List&lt;T&gt;</code> doesn’t have the same issue, since generic types are <em>not</em> covariant.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>
<span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Compile time error: Integer is not assignable to String</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ArrayFillIncompatibleType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ArrayHashCode<br>
            <small>hashcode method on array does not hash array contents</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Computing a hashcode for an array is tricky. Typically you want a hashcode that
depends on the value of each element in the array, but many of the common ways
to do this actually return a hashcode based on the <em>identity</em> of the array
rather than its contents.</p>

<p>This check flags attempts to compute a hashcode from an array that do not take
the contents of the array into account. There are several ways to mess this up:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p>Call the instance <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.hashCode()</code> method on an array.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Call the JDK method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Objects#hashCode()</code> with an argument of array
type.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Call the JDK method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Objects#hash()</code> or the Guava method
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.common.base.Objects#hashCode()</code> with multiple arguments, at
least one of which is an array.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Call the JDK method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Objects#hash()</code> or the Guava method
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.common.base.Objects#hashCode()</code> with a single argument of
<em>primitive</em> array type. Because these are varags methods that take
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object...</code>, the primitive array is autoboxed into a single-element Object
array, and these methods use the identity hashcode of the primitive array
rather than examining its contents. Note that calling these methods on an
argument of <em>Object</em> array type actually does the right thing because no
boxing is needed.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<p>Please use either <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Arrays#hashCode()</code> (for single-dimensional arrays)
or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Arrays#deepHashCode()</code> (for multidimensional arrays) to compute a
hash value that depends on the contents of the array. If you really intended to
compute the identity hash code, consider using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.lang.System#identityHashCode()</code> instead for clarity.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ArrayHashCode")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>
