    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            EqualsNull<br>
            <small>The contract of Object.equals() states that for any non-null reference value x, x.equals(null) should return false. If x is null, a NullPointerException is thrown. Consider replacing equals() with the == operator.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The contract of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.equals()</code> states that for any non-null reference value
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x.equals(null)</code> should return <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code>. Thus code such as</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>if (x.equals(null)) {
  ...
}
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>either returns <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code>, or throws a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NullPointerException</code> if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x</code> is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code>. The
nested block may never execute.</p>

<p>This check replaces <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x.equals(null)</code> with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x == null</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">!x.equals(null)</code>
with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x != null</code>. If the author intended for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x.equals(null)</code> to return <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">true</code>,
consider this as fragile code as it breaks the contract of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.equals()</code>.</p>

<p>See <a href="https://books.google.com/books?id=BIpDDwAAQBAJ">Effective Java 3rd Edition §10: Objey the general contract when overriding
equals</a> for more details.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsNull")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            EqualsReference<br>
            <small>== must be used in equals method to check equality to itself or an infinite loop will occur.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>.equals() to the same object will result in infinite recursion</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsReference")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

      <li><a href="https://github.com/google/error-prone">GitHub</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
</nav>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            EqualsWrongThing<br>
            <small>Comparing different pairs of fields/getters in an equals implementation is probably a mistake.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>An equals method compares non-corresponding fields from itself and the other
instance:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Frobnicator</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="nd">@Override</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@Nullable</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!(</span><span class="n">other</span> <span class="k">instanceof</span> <span class="nc">Frobnicator</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="nc">Frobnicator</span> <span class="n">that</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Frobnicator</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">a</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">that</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">a</span> <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">b</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">that</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">a</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// BUG: should be b == that.b</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsWrongThing")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ForOverride<br>
            <small>Method annotated @ForOverride must be protected or package-private and only invoked from declaring class, or from an override of the method</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A method that overrides a @ForOverride method should not be invoked directly.
Instead, it should be invoked only from the class in which it was declared. For
example, if overriding Converter.doForward, you should invoke it through
Converter.convert. For testing, factor out the code you want to run to a
separate method.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ForOverride")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            FormatString<br>
            <small>Invalid printf-style format string</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Format strings for the printf family of functions must follow the specification
in the documentation for <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Formatter.html">java.util.Formatter</a>.</p>

<p>The syntax for format specifiers is:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>%[argument_index$][flags][width][.precision]conversion
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Format strings can have the following errors:</p>

<h2 id="duplicateformatflags">DuplicateFormatFlags</h2>

<p>Duplicate flags are provided in the format specifier:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"e = %++10.4f"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">E</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="formatflagsconversionmismatch">FormatFlagsConversionMismatch</h2>

<p>A conversion and flag are incompatible:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%#b"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">E</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="illegalformatcodepoint">IllegalFormatCodePoint</h2>

<p>The argument is a character with an invalid Unicode code point.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%c"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mh">0x110000</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="illegalformatconversion">IllegalFormatConversion</h2>

<p>The argument corresponding to the format specifier is of an incompatible type:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%f"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="illegalformatflags">IllegalFormatFlags</h2>

<p>An illegal combination of flags is given:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%-010d"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mi">5</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="illegalformatprecision">IllegalFormatPrecision</h2>

<p>The conversion does not support a precision:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%.c"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="sc">'c'</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="illegalformatwidth">IllegalFormatWidth</h2>

<p>The conversion does not support a width:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%1n"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="missingformatargument">MissingFormatArgument</h2>

<p>There is a format specifier which does not have a corresponding argument or if
an argument index refers to an argument that does not exist:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%&lt;s"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"test"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="missingformatwidth">MissingFormatWidth</h2>

<p>The format width is required:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"e = %-f"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">E</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="unknownformatconversion">UnknownFormatConversion</h2>

<p>An unknown conversion is given:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%r"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FormatString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            FormatStringAnnotation<br>
            <small>Invalid format string passed to formatting method.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Methods can be annotated with Error Prone’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatMethod</code> annotation to
indicate that calls to this function should be treated similarly to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String.format</code>: One of the parameters is a ‘format string’ (the first String
parameter or the only parameter annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatString</code>), and the
subsequent parameters are used as format arguments to that format string.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@FormatMethod</span>
<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">myLogMethod</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@FormatString</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">fmt</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

<span class="c1">// ERROR: 2nd format argument isn't a number</span>
<span class="n">myLogMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"My log message: %d and %d"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"has a message"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>In order to avoid complex runtime issues when the format string part is
dynamically constructed, leading to a mismatch between the arguments and format
strings, we require that the ‘format string’ argument in calls to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatMethod</code>-annotated methods be one of:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Another <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatString</code>-annotated variable</li>
  <li>A compile time constant string</li>
  <li>A final or effectively final variable assigned to a compile time constant
string</li>
  <li>A string literal</li>
</ul>

<p>We will then check that the format string and format arguments match.</p>

<p>For more information on possible format string errors, see the documentation on
the <a href="FormatString">FormatString check</a>.</p>

<p>The import for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatMethod</code> is:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">com.google.errorprone.annotations.FormatMethod</span><span class="o">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation
@SuppressWarnings(“FormatStringAnnotation”) to the enclosing element.</p>

<h2 id="suppression-1">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FormatStringAnnotation")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            FromTemporalAccessor<br>
            <small>Certain combinations of javaTimeType.from(TemporalAccessor) will always throw a DateTimeException or return the parameter directly.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Not all java.time types can be created via from(TemporalAccessor). For example, you can create a Month from a LocalDate (Month.from(localDate)) because a LocalDate consists of a year, month, and day. However, you cannot create a LocalDate from a Month (since it doesn’t have the year or day information). Instead of throwing a DateTimeException at runtime, this checker validates the type transformations at compile time using static type information.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FromTemporalAccessor")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            FunctionalInterfaceMethodChanged<br>
            <small>Casting a lambda to this @FunctionalInterface can cause a behavior change from casting to a functional superinterface, which is surprising to users.  Prefer decorator methods to this surprising behavior.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>There are only two correct ways to have one <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FunctionalInterface</code></a> extend
another <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FunctionalInterface</code></a>—the way where you leave the abstract method
alone, and the way where you make a different abstract method but a default
method for the original abstract method simply delegates to the new name.</p>

<p>If you do anything else, you create a situation where what looks like a “cast”
actually changes behavior. That is really quite bad for understandability.</p>

<p>For example, if the method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">bar()</code> changes the behaviour of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">qux()</code>, then the
same lambda cast to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">B</code> could have completely different behaviour.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@FunctionalInterface</span>
<span class="kd">interface</span> <span class="nc">A</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="nf">bar</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="nd">@FunctionalInterface</span>
<span class="kd">interface</span> <span class="nc">B</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="no">A</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="nf">qux</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="nd">@Override</span>
  <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="nf">bar</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// anything here but exactly `return qux();` or perhaps `return (SomeType) qux();`</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you need to change the behaviour of an existing lambda, prefer an explicit
decorator method, e.g.:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Runnable</span> <span class="nf">crashTerminating</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Runnable</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">...</span><span class="na">wrapping</span> <span class="n">behavior</span> <span class="n">goes</span> <span class="n">here</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FunctionalInterfaceMethodChanged")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            FuturesGetCheckedIllegalExceptionType<br>
            <small>Futures.getChecked requires a checked exception type with a standard constructor.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The passed exception type must not be a RuntimeException, and it must expose a
public constructor whose only parameters are of type String or Throwable.
getChecked will reject any other type with an IllegalArgumentException.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FuturesGetCheckedIllegalExceptionType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            FuzzyEqualsShouldNotBeUsedInEqualsMethod<br>
            <small>DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals should never be used in an Object.equals() method</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>From documentation: DoubleMath.fuzzyEquals is not transitive, so it is not
suitable for use in Object#equals implementations.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FuzzyEqualsShouldNotBeUsedInEqualsMethod")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            GetClassOnAnnotation<br>
            <small>Calling getClass() on an annotation may return a proxy class</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Instances of an annotation interface generally return a random proxy class when
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass()</code> is called on them; to get the actual annotation type use
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">annotationType()</code>.</p>

<p>In the following example, calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass()</code> on the annotation instance
returns a proxy class like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.sun.proxy.$Proxy1</code>, while <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">annotationType()</code>
returns <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deprecated</code>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Deprecated</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Test</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">printAnnotationClass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Annotation</span> <span class="n">annotation</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">err</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">annotation</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getClass</span><span class="o">());</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">err</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">annotation</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">annotationType</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">printAnnotationClass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Test</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getAnnotation</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Deprecated</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">));</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prints:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>class com.sun.proxy.$Proxy1
interface java.lang.Deprecated
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GetClassOnAnnotation")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            GetClassOnClass<br>
            <small>Calling getClass() on an object of type Class returns the Class object for java.lang.Class; you probably meant to operate on the object directly</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass()</code> on an object of type Class returns the Class object for
java.lang.Class. Usually this is a mistake, and people intend to operate on the
object itself (for example, to print an error message). If you really did intend
to operate on the Class object for java.lang.Class, please use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class.class</code>
instead for clarity.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GetClassOnClass")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            GuardedBy<br>
            <small>Checks for unguarded accesses to fields and methods with @GuardedBy annotations</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: GuardedByChecker</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The GuardedBy analysis checks that fields or methods annotated with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@GuardedBy(lock)</code> are only accessed when the specified lock is held.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">com.google.errorprone.annotations.concurrent.GuardedBy</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Account</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@GuardedBy</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"this"</span><span class="o">)</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">balance</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">getBalance</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">balance</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// OK: implicit 'this' lock is held.</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">withdraw</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">setBalance</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">balance</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// OK: implicit 'this' lock is held.</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">deposit</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">setBalance</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">balance</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// ERROR: access to 'balance' not guarded by 'this'.</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="nd">@GuardedBy</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"this"</span><span class="o">)</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">setBalance</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">newBalance</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">checkState</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">newBalance</span> <span class="o">&gt;=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"Balance cannot be negative."</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="n">balance</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">newBalance</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// OK: 'this' must be held by caller of 'setBalance'.</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This above example uses implicit locks (via the ‘synchronized’ modifier). The
analysis also supports synchronized statements and java.util.concurrent locks.</p>

<h2 id="basic-concepts">Basic Concepts</h2>

<p>The analysis provides a way of associating members with locks. A member is a
field or a method. A lock can be the implicit lock of an object, or a
java.util.concurrent Lock.</p>

<p>An implicit lock is acquired using the built in synchronization features of the
language. Adding the ‘synchronized’ modifier to an instance method causes the
implicit lock of the enclosing instance to be acquired for the duration of the
method. Adding the ‘synchronized’ modifier to a static method is similar, except
the implicit lock of the Class object is acquired instead.</p>

<p>The Locks defined in java.util.concurrent are acquired with explicit
lock()/unlock() methods. The use of these methods in Java should always
correspond to a try/finally block, to ensure that the locks are released on all
execution paths.</p>

<h2 id="reference">Reference</h2>

<h3 id="lock-expression-syntax">Lock expression syntax</h3>

<p>The following syntax can be used to describe a lock:</p>

<table><tr><td><code>

this
</code></td><td>
The implicit object lock of the enclosing class.
</td></tr><tr><td><code>

ClassName.this
</code></td><td>
The implicit object lock of the enclosing class specified by ClassName.
(For inner classes, the ClassName.this designation allows you to specify which
'this' reference is intended.)

</td></tr><tr><td><code>
fieldName <br />
this.fieldName <br />
ClassName.this.fieldName
</code></td><td>
The final instance field specified by fieldName.

</td></tr><tr><td><code>
methodName() <br />
this.methodName() <br />
ClassName.this.methodName()
</code></td><td>
The instance method specified by methodName(). Methods called to return
locks should be deterministic.

</td></tr><tr><td><code>
ClassName.class
</code></td><td>
The implicit lock of specified Class object.

</td></tr><tr><td><code>
ClassName.fieldName
</code></td><td>
The static final field specified by fieldName.

</td></tr><tr><td><code>
ClassName.methodName()
</code></td><td>
The static method specified by methodName(). Methods called to return locks
should be deterministic.

</td></tr><tr><td><code>
itself
</code></td><td>
The annotated field.

</td></tr></table>

<h3 id="annotations">Annotations</h3>

<h4 id="guardedby">@GuardedBy</h4>

<p>com.google.errorprone.annotations.concurrent.GuardedBy</p>

<p>The @GuardedBy annotation is used to document that a member (a field or a
method) can only be accessed when the specified lock is held.</p>

<p>@GuardedBy can be used with both implicit locks and java.util.concurrent Locks.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Lock</span> <span class="n">lock</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ReentrantLock</span><span class="o">();</span>

<span class="nd">@GuardedBy</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"lock"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">m</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">++;</span>  <span class="c1">// error: access of 'x' not guarded by 'lock'</span>
  <span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">lock</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">++;</span>  <span class="c1">// OK: guarded by 'lock'</span>
  <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">unlock</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Note: there are a couple more annotations called <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@GuardedBy</code>, including
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javax.annotation.concurrent.GuardedBy</code> and
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">org.checkerframework.checker.lock.qual.GuardedBy</code>. The check recognizes those
versions of the annotation, but we recommend using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.errorprone.annotations.concurrent.GuardedBy</code>.</p>

<h4 id="limitations">Limitations</h4>

<p>Anonymous classes and lambdas need to re-acquire locks that may be held by an
enclosing block. For example, consider:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Transaction</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@GuardedBy</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"this"</span><span class="o">)</span>
  <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">handle</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">doSomething</span><span class="o">(()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">++;</span>  <span class="c1">// Error: access of 'x' not guarded by 'Transaction.this'</span>
    <span class="o">});</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The analysis is intra-procedural, meaning it doesn’t consider the implementation
of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">doSomething</code>.</p>

<p>In general, the checker doesn’t know if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">doSomething</code> immediately calls the
provided lambda while the lock is still held by the enclosing method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">handle</code>,
for example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomething</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Runnable</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">r</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">run</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>… or whether the lambda could be called later after <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">handle</code> has released the
lock, for example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomething</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Runnable</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// runs `r` at some point in the future</span>
  <span class="n">someExecutor</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">execute</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">r</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>However, the check does special-case some method calls which are known to
immediately call the provided lambda or method reference.</p>

<h4 id="false-negatives-with-aliasing">False negatives with aliasing</h4>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Names</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@GuardedBy</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"this"</span><span class="o">)</span>
  <span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">names</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">addName</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">copyOfNames</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="k">this</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="n">copyOfNames</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">names</span><span class="o">;</span>  <span class="c1">// OK: access of 'names' guarded by 'this'</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="n">copyOfNames</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">);</span>  <span class="c1">// should be an error: this access is not thread-safe!</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The analysis does not track aliasing, so it’s possible to circumvent the safety
it provides by copying references to guarded members.</p>

<p>In the example, the guarded field ‘names’ can be accessed via a copy even if the
required lock is not held.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GuardedBy")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            GuiceAssistedInjectScoping<br>
            <small>Scope annotation on implementation class of AssistedInject factory is not allowed</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Classes that AssistedInject factories create may not be annotated with scope
annotations, such as @Singleton. This will cause a Guice error at runtime.</p>

<p>See
<a href="https://code.google.com/p/google-guice/issues/detail?id=742">this bug report</a>
for details.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GuiceAssistedInjectScoping")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            GuiceAssistedParameters<br>
            <small>A constructor cannot have two @Assisted parameters of the same type unless they are disambiguated with named @Assisted annotations.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>From the <a href="https://google.github.io/guice/api-docs/latest/javadoc/com/google/inject/assistedinject/FactoryModuleBuilder.html">javadoc of FactoryModuleBuilder</a>:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>The types of the factory method’s parameters must be distinct. To use multiple
parameters of the same type, use a named <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Assisted</code> annotation to
disambiguate the parameters. The names must be applied to the factory method’s
parameters:</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">interface</span> <span class="nc">PaymentFactory</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="nc">Payment</span> <span class="nf">create</span><span class="o">(</span>
        <span class="nd">@Assisted</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"startDate"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Date</span> <span class="n">startDate</span><span class="o">,</span>
        <span class="nd">@Assisted</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"dueDate"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Date</span> <span class="n">dueDate</span><span class="o">,</span>
       <span class="nc">Money</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="o">);</span>
 <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<blockquote>
  <p>…and to the concrete type’s constructor parameters:</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">RealPayment</span> <span class="kd">implements</span> <span class="nc">Payment</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nd">@Inject</span>
   <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nf">RealPayment</span><span class="o">(</span>
      <span class="nc">CreditService</span> <span class="n">creditService</span><span class="o">,</span>
      <span class="nc">AuthService</span> <span class="n">authService</span><span class="o">,</span>
       <span class="nd">@Assisted</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"startDate"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Date</span> <span class="n">startDate</span><span class="o">,</span>
       <span class="nd">@Assisted</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"dueDate"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Date</span> <span class="n">dueDate</span><span class="o">,</span>
       <span class="nd">@Assisted</span> <span class="nc">Money</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
     <span class="o">...</span>
   <span class="o">}</span>
 <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GuiceAssistedParameters")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            GuiceInjectOnFinalField<br>
            <small>Although Guice allows injecting final fields, doing so is disallowed because the injected value may not be visible to other threads.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>From the <a href="https://github.com/google/guice/wiki/InjectionPoints#how-guice-injects">Guice wiki</a>:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Injecting <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">final</code> fields is not recommended because the injected value may not
be visible to other threads.</p>
</blockquote>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GuiceInjectOnFinalField")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            HashtableContains<br>
            <small>contains() is a legacy method that is equivalent to containsValue()</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Hashtable.contains(Object)</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ConcurrentHashMap.contains(Object)</code> are legacy
methods for testing if the given object is a value in the hash table. They are
often mistaken for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">containsKey</code>, which checks whether the given object is a
<em>key</em> in the hash table.</p>

<p>If you intended to check whether the given object is a key in the hash table,
use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">containsKey</code> instead. If you really intended to check whether the given
object is a value in the hash table, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">containsValue</code> for clarity.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("HashtableContains")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            IdentityBinaryExpression<br>
            <small>A binary expression where both operands are the same is usually incorrect.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: SelfEquality</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using the same expressions as both arguments to the following binary expressions
is usually a mistake:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a &amp;&amp; a</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a || a</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a &amp; a</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a | a</code> is equivalent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a &lt;= a</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a &gt;= a</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a == a</code> is always <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">true</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a &lt; a</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a &gt; a</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a != a</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a ^ a</code> is always <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a / a</code> is always <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">1</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a % a</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a - a</code> is always <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code></li>
</ul>

<p>If the expression has side-effects, consider refactoring one of the expressions
with side effects into a local. For example, prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// check twice, just to be sure</span>
<span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="n">isTrue</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isTrue</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">isTrue</span> <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isTrue</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>to this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isTrue</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isTrue</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("IdentityBinaryExpression")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            IdentityHashMapBoxing<br>
            <small>Using IdentityHashMap with a boxed type as the key is risky since boxing may produce distinct instances</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Usage of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.IdentityHashMap</code> with a boxed primitive type as a key is
risky and can yield unexpected results because <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.IdentityHashMap</code> uses
reference-equality when comparing keys and reference equality for primitive
wrappers is particularly bug-prone: Primitive wrapper classes cache instances
for some (but usually not all) values, so == may be equivalent to equals() for
some values but not others. Additionally, not all versions of the runtime and
other libraries use the cache in the same cases, so upgrades may change
behavior.</p>

<p>Thus:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">map</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">IdentityHashMap</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>
  <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">n</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">randomInt</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">map</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">put</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">map</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">get</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">);</span>  <span class="c1">// This could be null since boxing happens twice and could produce distinct values.</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>But:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">map</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">IdentityHashMap</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>
  <span class="nc">Integer</span> <span class="n">n</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">randomInt</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">map</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">put</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">map</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">get</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">);</span>  <span class="c1">// This cannot be null because it's the same instance.</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("IdentityHashMapBoxing")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            Immutable<br>
            <small>Type declaration annotated with @Immutable is not immutable</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This check validates that all classes annotated with Error Prone’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code>
annotation (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.errorprone.annotations.Immutable</code>) are deeply immutable.
It also checks that any class extending an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code>-annotated class or
implementing an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code>-annotated interface are also immutable.</p>

<p>NOTE: Other versions of the annotation, such as
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javax.annotation.concurrent.Immutable</code>, are currently <em>not</em> enforced.</p>

<p>An object is immutable if its state cannot be observed to change after
construction. Immutable objects are inherently thread-safe.</p>

<p>A class is immutable if all instances of that class are immutable. The
immutability of a class can only be fully guaranteed if the class is final,
otherwise one must ensure all subclasses are also immutable.</p>

<p>A conservative definition of object immutability is:</p>

<ul>
  <li>All fields are final;</li>
  <li>All reference fields are of immutable type, or null;</li>
  <li>It is <em>properly constructed</em> (the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this</code> reference does not escape the
constructor).</li>
</ul>

<p>The requirement that all reference fields be immutable ensures <em>deep</em>
immutability, meaning all contained state is also immutable. A weaker property,
common with container classes, is <em>shallow</em> immutability, which allows some of
the object’s fields to point to mutable objects. One example of shallow
immutability is guava’s ImmutableList, which may contain mutable elements.</p>

<p>It is possible to implement immutable classes with some internal mutable state,
as long as callers can never observe changes to that state. For example, some
state may be lazily initialized to improve performance.</p>

<p>It is also technically possible to have an immutable object with non-final
fields (see the implementation of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String#hashCode()</code> for an example), but doing
this correctly requires subtle reasoning about safe data races and deep
knowledge of the Java Memory Model.</p>

<p>If you have an immutable class with mutable fields as described above, you can
mark it as such by <a href="#suppression">suppressing the Immutable check</a> on it. This
will allow your class to be included in other <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> classes.</p>

<p>For more information about immutability, see:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Java Concurrency in Practice §3.4</li>
  <li><a href="https://books.google.com/books?id=BIpDDwAAQBAJ">Effective Java 3rd Edition §17</a></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="type-parameters">Type Parameters</h2>

<p>When an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> class has type parameters that are used in the type of that
class’s fields, that class is called an immutable generic container. Usages of
immutable generic container classes, such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableList</code>, are only actually
deemed immutable if the arguments to all such type parameters are also deemed
immutable. For example, an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableList&lt;String&gt;</code> is deemed immutable since
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code>s are immutable. However, an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableList&lt;Object&gt;</code> is not deemed
immutable since <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object</code>s are not provably immutable.</p>

<p>When creating generic container classes, Error Prone requires that you declare
whether that container is allowed to be used with mutable, or only with
immutable type parameters.</p>

<h3 id="immutablecontainerof--"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable(containerOf = ...)</code></h3>

<p>If you want to allow your immutable generic container to possibly contain
mutable types, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code>’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">containerOf</code> method:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Immutable</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">containerOf</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"T"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableHolder</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">ref</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Error Prone will allow you to instantiate an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableHolder&lt;String&gt;</code> and use
it as a field in another <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> class. You may instantiate an
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableHolder&lt;Object&gt;</code>, but since it is mutable, Error Prone would report an
error if that was a field of another <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> class.</p>

<h3 id="immutabletypeparameter"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@ImmutableTypeParameter</code></h3>

<p>If you want to allow your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> generic container to only contain
immutable types, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@ImmutableTypeParameter</code>:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Immutable</span>
<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableContainer</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nd">@ImmutableTypeParameter</span> <span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">ref</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Error Prone will allow you to instantiate a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableContainer&lt;String&gt;</code> and use
it as a field in another <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> class. However, it is a compiler error to
instantiate an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableContainer&lt;Object&gt;</code>.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@ImmutableTypeParameter</code> can restrict generic parameters to immutable types
only but the generic itself may not be immutable.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MutableContainer</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nd">@ImmutableTypeParameter</span> <span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>You can also use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@ImmutableTypeParameter</code> to annotate a method’s type
parameters:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">SomeMutableClass</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nd">@ImmutableTypeParameter</span> <span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">putInImmutableList</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="type-parameters-not-used-in-fields">Type Parameters Not Used in Fields</h3>

<p>If your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Immutable</code> class has a type parameter that is not used in the type of
your class’s fields, then there is no need to use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">containerOf</code> or
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@ImmutableTypeParameter</code>:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Immutable</span>
<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">NonContainer</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="o">...</span> <span class="c1">// No fields whose type contains T</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">element</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// process 'element', which won't violate NonContainer's immutability.</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>Suppress false positives by adding an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("Immutable")</code>
annotation to the enclosing element, or the offending field.</p>

<p>To suppress warnings in AutoValue classes, add <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@AutoValue.CopyAnnotations</code> to
ensure the suppression is also applied to the generated sub-class:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@AutoValue</span>
<span class="nd">@AutoValue</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">CopyAnnotations</span>
<span class="nd">@Immutable</span>
<span class="nd">@SuppressWarnings</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Immutable"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyAutoValue</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>


    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ImpossibleNullComparison<br>
            <small>This value cannot be null, and comparing it to null may be misleading.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: ProtoFieldNullComparison</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This checker looks for comparisons of protocol buffer fields with null. If a
proto field is not specified, its field accessor will return a non-null default
value. Thus, the result of calling one of these accessors can never be null, and
comparisons like these often indicate a nearby error.</p>

<p>If you need to distinguish between an unset optional value and a default value,
you have two options. In most cases, you can simply use the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hasField()</code> method.
proto3 however does not generate <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hasField()</code> methods for primitive types
(including <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">string</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">bytes</code>). In those cases you will need to wrap your
field in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">google.protobuf.StringValue</code> or similar.</p>

<p>NOTE: This check applies to normal (server) protos and Lite protos. The
deprecated nano runtime does produce objects which use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code> values to indicate
field absence.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">test</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProto</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getField</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getRepeatedFieldList</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getRepeatedField</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">test</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProto</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hasField</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getRepeatedFieldList</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">isEmpty</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getRepeatedFieldCount</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If the presence of a field is required information in proto3, the field can be
wrapped. For example,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">message</span> <span class="nc">MyMessage</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">google</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">protobuf</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">StringValue</span> <span class="n">my_string</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Presence can then be tested using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myMessage.hasMyString()</code>, and the value
retrieved using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myMessage.getMyString().getValue()</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ImpossibleNullComparison")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            IncompatibleArgumentType<br>
            <small>Passing argument to a generic method with an incompatible type.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The called method is annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@CompatibleWith</code>, which enforces that the
parameter passed to the method can potentially be <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-5.html#jls-5.5.1">cast</a> to the appropriate
generic type. However, the type of the parameter passed can’t be cast to the
appropriate generic type.</p>

<p>This is useful when a method can’t just take a parameter of the generic type to
allow developers to safely operate with instances held with a wildcard type when
using an instance as both a <em>consumer</em> and <em>producer</em> of values. This should
<em>not</em> be the default, as most interfaces are either one or the other. Containers
and container-like class are the most likely places to use this tool.</p>

<p>TIP: More explanation can be found on the page for <a href="CollectionIncompatibleType">CollectionIncompatibleType</a></p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">interface</span> <span class="nc">Container</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">thing</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@CompatibleWith</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"T"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">thing</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">containsAsT</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">thing</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">containmentCheck</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Container</span><span class="o">&lt;?</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Number</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">container</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">container</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// OK, int can be cast to Number</span>
  <span class="n">container</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">2.0</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// OK, double can be cast to Number</span>
  <span class="n">container</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Not OK, String can't be cast to number</span>

  <span class="c1">// Does not compile, since, for example, container might be Container&lt;Double&gt;, and Integer</span>
  <span class="c1">// can't be cast to Double.</span>
  <span class="n">container</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">containsAsT</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">);</span>

  <span class="nc">Container</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">stringContainer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">...;</span>
  <span class="n">stringContainer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// OK</span>
  <span class="c1">// OK, since Object *could* be cast to String</span>
  <span class="n">stringContainer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{});</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("IncompatibleArgumentType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            IncompatibleModifiers<br>
            <small>This annotation has incompatible modifiers as specified by its @IncompatibleModifiers annotation</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>

*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The @IncompatibleModifiers annotation declares that the target annotation is
incompatible with a set of provided modifiers. This check ensures that all
annotations respect their @IncompatibleModifiers specifications.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("IncompatibleModifiers")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

      <span class="icon-bar"></span>
    </button>
    <a class="navbar-brand" href="/index">Error Prone</a>
  </div>
