    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            InexactVarargsConditional<br>
            <small>Conditional expression in varargs call contains array and non-array arguments</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When calling a varargs method, you can either pass an explicit array of
arguments, or individual arguments:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">err</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Arrays</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">deepToString</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">));</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Both of the following print <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">[1, 2]</code>:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>f(new Object[] {1, 2}) // prints "[1, 2]"
f(1, 2) // prints "[1, 2]"
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If the argument to the varargs method is a conditional expression, and either
branch is not an array, the result of the expression will be implicitly wrapped
in an array.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">flag</span> <span class="o">?</span> <span class="mi">1</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="c1">// prints [1] or [2]</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This means that if one branch is an array and the other branch is not, the array
branch will become a multi-dimensional array:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">flag</span> <span class="o">?</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="o">{</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">}</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// prints [[1, 2]] or [3]</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To avoid the implicit array creation, the other argument can be explicitly
wrapped in an array:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">flag</span> <span class="o">?</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="o">{</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">}</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="o">{</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="o">});</span> <span class="c1">// prints [1, 2] or [3]</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Or, if the multi-dimensional array was intentional, it can be written explicitly
as:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">flag</span> <span class="o">?</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">[][]</span> <span class="mi">1</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="o">{</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="o">});</span> <span class="c1">// prints [[1, 2]] or [3]</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("InexactVarargsConditional")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            InfiniteRecursion<br>
            <small>This method calls itself unconditionally; it will throw StackOverflowError</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A method that always calls itself will cause a StackOverflowError.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">oops</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nf">oops</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>Exception in thread "main" java.lang.StackOverflowError
  at Test.oops(X.java:3)
  at Test.oops(X.java:3)
  ...
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The fix may be to call another method with the same name:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// error</span>
  <span class="n">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="cm">/*verbose=*/</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// ok</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="n">verbose</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or to call the method on a different instance:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Delegate</span> <span class="kd">implements</span> <span class="nc">Processor</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Processor</span> <span class="n">delegate</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// error</span>
    <span class="n">delegate</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">process</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// ok</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("InfiniteRecursion")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            InjectMoreThanOneScopeAnnotationOnClass<br>
            <small>A class can be annotated with at most one scope annotation.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: MoreThanOneScopeAnnotationOnClass</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Annotating a class with more than one scope annotation is invalid according to
the JSR-330 specification.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("InjectMoreThanOneScopeAnnotationOnClass")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            InvalidPatternSyntax<br>
            <small>Invalid syntax used for a regular expression</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This error is triggered by calls to regex-accepting methods with invalid string
literals. These calls would cause a PatternSyntaxException at runtime.</p>

<p>We deliberately do not check <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.regex.Pattern#compile</code> as many of its
users are deliberately testing the regex compiler or using a vacuously true
regex.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">"."</code> is also discouraged, as it is a valid regex but is easy to mistake for
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">"\\."</code>. Instead of e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">str.replaceAll(".", "x")</code>, prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Strings.repeat("x",
str.length())</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CharMatcher.ANY.replaceFrom(str, "x")</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("InvalidPatternSyntax")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <a href="/docs/installation">Docs</a>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            IsInstanceOfClass<br>
            <small>The argument to Class#isInstance(Object) should not be a Class</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Passing an argument of type <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class#instanceOf(Class)</code> is usually a
mistake.</p>

<p>Calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">clazz.instanceOf(obj)</code> for some <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">clazz</code> with type <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class&lt;T&gt;</code> is
equivalent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">obj instanceof T</code>. The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceOf</code> method exists for cases where
the type <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">T</code> is not known statically.</p>

<p>When a class literal is passed as the argument of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceOf</code>, the result will
only be true if the class literal on left hand side is equal to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class.class</code>.</p>

<p>For example, the following code returns true if and only if the type <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A</code> is
equal to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class</code> (i.e. lhs is equal to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class.class</code>).</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">B</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Class</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">lhs</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Class</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">B</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">rhs</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">lhs</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">instanceOf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">rhs</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// equivalent to 'lhs == Class.class'</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To test if the type represented by a class literal is a subtype of the type
represented by some other class literal, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isAssignableFrom</code> should be used
instead:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">B</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Class</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">lhs</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Class</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">B</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">rhs</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">lhs</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isAssignableFrom</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">rhs</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// equivalent to 'B instanceof A'</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>JUnit 3 requires that test method names start with “<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">test</code>”. The method that
triggered this error looks like it is supposed to be a test, but misspells the
required prefix; has <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Test</code> annotation, but no prefix; or has the wrong method
signature. As a consequence, JUnit 3 will ignore it.</p>

<p>If you meant to disable this test on purpose, or this is a helper method, change
the name to something more descriptive, like “<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">disabledTestSomething()</code>”. You
don’t need an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Test</code> annotation, but if you want to keep it, add <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Ignore</code> too.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JUnit3TestNotRun")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            JUnit4ClassAnnotationNonStatic<br>
            <small>This method should be static</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>JUnit4 provides two annotations (<a href="https://junit.sourceforge.net/javadoc/org/junit/BeforeClass.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@BeforeClass</code></a> and
<a href="https://junit.sourceforge.net/javadoc/org/junit/AfterClass.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@AfterClass</code></a>) that are applied to methods that are run once per
<strong>test class</strong>. These complement the more-often used <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Before</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@After</code>
which are applied to methods that are run once per <strong>test method</strong>.</p>

<p>JUnit4 runs <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@BeforeClass</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@AfterClass</code> methods without making an instance
of the test class, meaning that the methods must be <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static</code>. JUnit4 will fail
to run any <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@BeforeClass</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@AfterClass</code> method that isn’t also <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JUnit4ClassAnnotationNonStatic")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            JUnit4SetUpNotRun<br>
            <small>setUp() method will not be run; please add JUnit's @Before annotation</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>JUnit 3 provides the method setUp(), to be overridden by subclasses when the
test needs to perform some pre-test initialization. In JUnit 4, this is
accomplished by annotating such a method with @Before.</p>

<p>The method that triggered this error matches the definition of setUp() from
JUnit3, but was not annotated with @Before and thus won’t be run by the JUnit4
runner.</p>

<p>If you intend for this setUp() method not to run by the JUnit4 runner, but
perhaps manually be invoked in certain test methods, please rename the method or
mark it private.</p>

<p>If the method is part of an abstract test class hierarchy where this class’s
setUp() is invoked by a superclass method that is annotated with @Before, then
please rename the abstract method or add @Before to the superclass’s definition
of setUp()</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JUnit4SetUpNotRun")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

The test method that triggered this error looks like it was meant to be a test,
but was not so annotated, so it will not be run. If you intend for this test
method not to run, please add both an @Test and an @Ignore annotation to make it
clear that you are purposely disabling it. If this is a helper method and not a
test, consider reducing its visibility to non-public, if possible.</p>

          <h1>
            JavaxInjectOnAbstractMethod<br>
            <small>Abstract and default methods are not injectable with javax.inject.Inject</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <a href="https://javax-inject.github.io/javax-inject/api/javax/inject/Inject.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Inject</code></a> annotation cannot be applied to abstract methods, per the JSR-330
spec, since injectors will only inject those methods if the concrete implementer
of the abstract method has the <a href="https://javax-inject.github.io/javax-inject/api/javax/inject/Inject.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Inject</code></a> annotation as well. See
<a href="OverridesJavaxInjectableMethod">OverridesJavaxInjectableMethod</a> for more examples of this interaction.</p>

<p>Currently, default methods in interfaces are not injected if they have
<a href="https://javax-inject.github.io/javax-inject/api/javax/inject/Inject.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Inject</code></a> for similar reasons, although future updates to dependency injection
frameworks may allow this, since the default methods are not abstract.</p>

<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/google/guice/wiki/JSR330">Guice wiki</a> page on JSR-330 for more.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JavaxInjectOnAbstractMethod")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            JodaToSelf<br>
            <small>Use of Joda-Time's DateTime.toDateTime(), Duration.toDuration(), Instant.toInstant(), Interval.toInterval(), and Period.toPeriod() are not allowed.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Joda-Time’s DateTime.toDateTime(), Duration.toDuration(), Instant.toInstant(), Interval.toInterval(), and Period.toPeriod() are always unnecessary, since they simply ‘return this’. There is no reason to ever call them.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JodaToSelf")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            LenientFormatStringValidation<br>
            <small>The number of arguments provided to lenient format methods should match the positional specifiers.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This check ensures that the number of arguments passed to ‘lenient’ formatting
methods like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Preconditions.checkArgument</code> match the number of format
specifiers.</p>

<p>WARNING: Only the exact two-character placeholder sequence <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">%s</code> is recognized by
these methods. Any others will be ignored, and not used for argument
substitution.</p>

<p>The APIs checked by this bugpattern include:</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot-jre/api/docs/com/google/common/base/Strings.html#lenientFormat\(java.lang.String,java.lang.Object...\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.common.base.Strings#lenientFormat</code></a></li>

          <h1>
            LiteByteStringUtf8<br>
            <small>This pattern will silently corrupt certain byte sequences from the serialized protocol message. Use ByteString or byte[] directly</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When serializing bytes from a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MessageLite</code>, one can use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">toByteString</code> to get a
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteString</code>, effectively an immutable wrapper over a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">byte[]</code>. This ByteString
can be passed around and deserialized into a message using
<a href="https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/java/com/google/protobuf/Message.Builder#mergeFrom-com.google.protobuf.ByteString-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MyMessage.Builder.mergeFrom(ByteString)</code></a>.</p>

<p><a href="https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/java/com/google/protobuf/ByteString#toStringUtf8--"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteString#toStringUtf8</code></a> copies UTF-8 encoded byte data living inside the
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteString</code> to a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.lang.String</code>, replacing any
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8#Invalid_byte_sequences">invalid UTF-8 byte sequences</a> with � (the Unicode
replacement character).</p>

<p>In this circumstance, a protocol message is being serialized to a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteString</code>,
then immediately turned into a Java <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code> using the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">toStringUtf8</code> method.
However, serialized protocol buffers are arbitrary binary data and not
UTF-8-encoded data. Thus, the resulting <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code> may not match the actual
serialized bytes from the protocol message.</p>

<p>Instead of holding the serialized protocol message in a Java <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code>, carry
around the actual bytes in a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteString</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">byte[]</code>, or some other equivalent
container for arbitrary binary data.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LiteByteStringUtf8")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            LockOnBoxedPrimitive<br>
            <small>It is dangerous to use a boxed primitive as a lock as it can unintentionally lead to sharing a lock with another piece of code.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Instances of boxed primitive types may be cached by the standard library
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">valueOf</code> method. This method is used for autoboxing. This means that using a
boxed primitive as a lock can result in unintentionally sharing a lock with
another piece of code.</p>

<p>Consider using an explicit lock <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object</code> instead of locking on a boxed
primitive. That is, prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">lock</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Object</span><span class="o">();</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomething</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// ...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>instead of this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Integer</span> <span class="n">lock</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomething</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// ...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LockOnBoxedPrimitive")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            LossyPrimitiveCompare<br>
            <small>Using an unnecessarily-wide comparison method can lead to lossy comparison</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Implicit widening conversions when comparing two primitives with methods like Float.compare can lead to lossy comparison. For example, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Float.compare(Integer.MAX_VALUE, Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1) == 0</code>. Use a compare method with non-lossy conversion, or ideally no conversion if possible.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LossyPrimitiveCompare")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            MathRoundIntLong<br>

          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Math.round() called with an integer or long type results in truncation because Math.round only accepts floats or doubles and some integers and longs can’t be represented with float.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

          <h1>
            MemorySegmentReferenceEquality<br>
            <small>Do not compare MemorySegments using reference equality.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MemorySegment</code> is a value-based class. Comparing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MemorySegment</code> instances
using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">==</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">!=</code> is bug-prone because <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MemorySegment</code> implementations may not
be unique for the same underlying memory. Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Objects.equals()</code> (or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.equals()</code>
if the receiver is known to be non-null) instead.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">MemorySegment</span> <span class="n">seg</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">...;</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">seg</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">NULL</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="c1">// reference equality</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>should be:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">MemorySegment</span> <span class="n">seg</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">...;</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Objects</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">seg</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">NULL</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="c1">// value equality</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Reference equality between any two <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MemorySegment</code> instances (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a == b</code>) is
flagged by this check, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Objects.equals(a, b)</code> is the preferred alternative.</p>

<p>See also https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8381012</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MemorySegmentReferenceEquality")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            MislabeledAndroidString<br>
            <small>Certain resources in `android.R.string` have names that do not match their content</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Certain resources in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">android.R.string</code> have names that do not match their
content: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">android.R.string.yes</code> is actually “OK” and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">android.R.string.no</code> is
“Cancel”. Avoid these string resources and prefer ones whose names <em>do</em> match
their content. If you need “Yes” or “No” you must create your own string
resources.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MislabeledAndroidString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            MisleadingEscapedSpace<br>
            <small>Using \s anywhere except at the end of a line in a text block is potentially misleading.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When Java introduced text blocks as a feature, it also introduced a new string
escape sequence <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\s</code>. This escape sequence is another way to write a normal
space, but it has the advantage that it can be used at the end of a line in a
text block, where a normal space would be stripped.</p>

<p>This new escape sequence can easily be confused with the regex <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\s</code>, which is a
metacharacter that matches any kind of whitespace character. To write that
metacharacter in a Java string, you must still write <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\\s</code>: an escaped backslash
followed by an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">s</code>.</p>

<p>There is little reason to ever write the Java escape <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\s</code> except at the end of a
line. Either use a normal space, or switch to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\\s</code> if you are trying to write
the regex metacharacter.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// Each line here is five characters long.</span>
<span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">colors</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"""
    one \s
    two \s
    three
    """</span><span class="o">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MisleadingEscapedSpace")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            MissingSuperCall<br>
            <small>Overriding method is missing a call to overridden super method</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>API providers may annotate a method with an annotation like
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">androidx.annotation.CallSuper</code> or
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javax.annotation.OverridingMethodsMustInvokeSuper</code> to require that overriding
methods invoke the super method. This check enforces those annotations.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MissingSuperCall")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            MissingTestCall<br>
            <small>A terminating method call is required for a test helper to have any effect.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Some test helpers such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EqualsTester</code> require a terminating method call to be
of any use.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nd">@Test</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">string</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">EqualsTester</span><span class="o">()</span>
        <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addEqualityGroup</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">))</span>
        <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addEqualityGroup</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"world"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"world"</span><span class="o">))</span>
        <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addEqualityGroup</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">valueOf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">));</span>
    <span class="c1">// Oops: forgot to call `testEquals()`</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MissingTestCall")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            MisusedWeekYear<br>
            <small>Use of "YYYY" (week year) in a date pattern without "ww" (week in year). You probably meant to use "yyyy" (year) instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>“YYYY” in a date pattern means “week year”. The week year is defined to begin at
the beginning of the week that contains the year’s first Thursday. For example,
the week year 2015 began on Monday, December 29, 2014, since January 1, 2015,
was on a Thursday.</p>

<p>“Week year” is intended to be used for week dates, e.g. “2015-W01-1”, but is
often mistakenly used for calendar dates, e.g. 2014-12-29, in which case the
year may be incorrect during the last week of the year. If you are formatting
anything other than a week date, you should use the year specifier “yyyy”
instead.</p>

<p>This isn’t an idle risk; Twitter had a
<a href="https://web.archive.org/web/20150711045621/http://tech.firstpost.com/news-analysis/twitter-suffers-massive-outage-on-all-online-platforms-back-now-247196.html">significant outage</a>
in <del>2015</del> 2014
<a href="https://xcancel.com/jmhodges/status/549430032616017921">due to this bug</a>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MisusedWeekYear")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            MixedDescriptors<br>
            <small>The field number passed into #findFieldByNumber belongs to a different proto to the Descriptor.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A field <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Descriptor</code> was created by mixing the message <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Descriptor</code> from one
proto message with the field number from another. For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getDescriptor</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">findFieldByNumber</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">ID_FIELD_NUMBER</span><span class="o">)</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This accesses the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Descriptor</code> of a field in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code> with a field number from
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code>. One of these was probably intended:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getDescriptor</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">findFieldByNumber</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">ID_FIELD_NUMBER</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getDescriptor</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">findFieldByNumber</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">ID_FIELD_NUMBER</span><span class="o">)</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MixedDescriptors")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            MockitoUsage<br>
            <small>Missing method call for verify(mock) here</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Calls to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Mockito.when</code> should always be accompanied by a call to a method like
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">thenReturn</code>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">when</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">mock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">get</span><span class="o">()).</span><span class="na">thenReturn</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">answer</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// correct</span>
<span class="n">when</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">mock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">get</span><span class="o">())</span>                     <span class="c1">// oops!</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Similarly, calls to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Mockito.verify</code> should call the verified method <em>outside</em>
the call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">verify</code>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">verify</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">mock</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">execute</span><span class="o">();</span> <span class="c1">// correct</span>
<span class="n">verify</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">mock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">execute</span><span class="o">());</span> <span class="c1">// oops!</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>For more information, see the <a href="https://github.com/mockito/mockito/wiki/FAQ#what-are-unfinished-verificationstubbing-errors">Mockito documentation</a>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MockitoUsage")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ModifyingCollectionWithItself<br>
            <small>Using a collection function with itself as the argument.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Invoking a collection method with the same collection as the argument is likely
incorrect.</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">collection.addAll(collection)</code> may cause an infinite loop, duplicate the
elements, or do nothing, depending on the type of Collection and
implementation class.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">collection.retainAll(collection)</code> is a no-op.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">collection.removeAll(collection)</code> is the same as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">collection.clear()</code>.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">collection.containsAll(collection)</code> is always true.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ModifyingCollectionWithItself")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            MoreThanOneInjectableConstructor<br>
            <small>This class has more than one @Inject-annotated constructor. Please remove the @Inject annotation from all but one of them.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: inject-constructors, InjectMultipleAtInjectConstructors</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Injection frameworks may use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Inject</code> to determine how to construct an object
in the absence of other instructions. Annotating <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Inject</code> on a constructor
tells the injection framework to use that constructor. However, if multiple
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Inject</code> constructors exist, injection frameworks can’t reliably choose between
them.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MoreThanOneInjectableConstructor")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            MustBeClosedChecker<br>
            <small>This method returns a resource which must be managed carefully, not just left for garbage collection. If it is a constant that will persist for the lifetime of your program, move it to a private static final field. Otherwise, you should use it in a try-with-resources.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: MustBeClosed</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Methods or constructors annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@MustBeClosed</code> require that the returned
resource is closed. This is enforced by checking that invocations occur within
the resource variable initializer of a try-with-resources statement:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span> <span class="n">resource</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">createTheResource</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">doSomething</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">resource</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">return</code> statement of another method annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@MustBeClosed</code>:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@MustBeClosed</span>
<span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span> <span class="nf">createMyResource</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nf">createTheResource</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To support legacy code, the following pattern is also supported:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span> <span class="n">resource</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">createTheResource</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">doSomething</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">resource</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">resource</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">close</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MustBeClosedChecker")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            NonCanonicalStaticImport<br>
            <small>Static import of type uses non-canonical name</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Types should always be imported by their canonical name. The canonical name of a
top-level class is the fully-qualified name of the package, followed by a ‘.’,
followed by the name of the class. The canonical name of a member class is the
canonical name of its declaring class, followed by a ‘.’, followed by the name
of the member class.</p>

<p>Fully-qualified member class names are not guaranteed to be canonical. Consider
some member class M declared in a class C. There may be another class D that
extends C and inherits M. Therefore M can be accessed using the fully-qualified
name of D, followed by a ‘.’, followed by ‘M’. Since M is not declared in D,
this name is not canonical.</p>

<p>The JLS §7.5.3 requires all single static imports to <em>start</em> with a canonical
type name, but the fully-qualified name of the imported member is not required
to be canonical.</p>

<p>Importing types using non-canonical names is unnecessary and unclear, and should
be avoided.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">package</span> <span class="nn">a</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">One</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Inner</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">package</span> <span class="nn">a</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Two</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">One</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>An import of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Inner</code> should always refer to it using the canonical name
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a.One.Inner</code>, not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">a.Two.Inner</code>.</p>


    </div>
    <footer class="footer">

    <div class="container">

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            NonFinalCompileTimeConstant<br>
            <small>@CompileTimeConstant parameters should be final or effectively final</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>If a method’s formal parameter is annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@CompileTimeConstant</code>, the
method will always be invoked with an argument that is a static constant. If the
parameter itself is non-final, then it is a mutable reference to immutable data.
This is rarely useful, and can be confusing when trying to use the parameter in
a context that requires an compile-time constant. For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@CompileTimeConstant</span> <span class="n">y</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">g</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@CompileTimeConstant</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// x is not a constant</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("NonFinalCompileTimeConstant")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            NonRuntimeAnnotation<br>
            <small>Calling getAnnotation on an annotation that is not retained at runtime</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Calling getAnnotation on an annotation that does not have its Retention set to
RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME will always return null.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("NonRuntimeAnnotation")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            NullTernary<br>
            <small>This conditional expression may evaluate to null, which will result in an NPE when the result is unboxed.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>If a conditional expression evaluates to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code>, unboxing it will result in a
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NullPointerException</code>.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">flag</span> <span class="o">?</span> <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">flag</code> is false, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code> will be auto-unboxed from an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">int</code>,
resulting in a NullPointerException.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("NullTernary")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            NullableOnContainingClass<br>
            <small>Type-use nullability annotations should annotate the inner class, not the outer class (e.g., write `A.@Nullable B` instead of `@Nullable A.B`).</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The correct syntax to apply a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TYPE_USE</code> annotation to an inner class is
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A.@Nullable B</code>.</p>

<p>For a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TYPE_USE</code> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Nullable</code> annotation, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Nullable A.B</code> is legal Java if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">B</code> is
a non-static inner class:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">A</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@Target</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">TYPE_USE</span><span class="o">)</span>
  <span class="nd">@interface</span> <span class="nc">Nullable</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

  <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">B</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">C</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">test</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="nd">@Nullable</span> <span class="no">B</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span> <span class="c1">// B is annotated ('A' is the enclosing instance type)</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">test</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="nd">@Nullable</span> <span class="no">C</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span> <span class="c1">// C is annotated ('A' is a 'scoping construct' here)</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">test</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@Nullable</span> <span class="no">A</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">B</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span> <span class="c1">// compiles, but likely incorrect: annotates the enclosing instance type 'A', which can never be null</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">test</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@Nullable</span> <span class="no">A</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">C</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span> <span class="c1">// compile error: 'A' cannot be annotated</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>However, for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Nullable</code> (and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@NonNull</code>, and friends), annotating the outer
class is meaningless. The reference to the outer class (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A.this</code>) can never be
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code>, so any nullability annotations are redundant.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("NullableOnContainingClass")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="col-lg-12">

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            OverlappingQualifierAndScopeAnnotation<br>
            <small>Annotations cannot be both Scope annotations and Qualifier annotations: this causes confusion when trying to use them.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Qualifiers and Scoping annotations have different semantic meanings and a single
annotation should not be both a qualifier and a scoping annotation.</p>

<p>If an annotation is both a scoping annotation and a qualifier, unless great care
is taken with its application and usage, the semantics of objects annotated with
the annotation are unclear.</p>

<p>Take a look at this example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Retention</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">RetentionPolicy</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">RUNTIME</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nd">@Scope</span>
<span class="nd">@Qualifier</span>
<span class="nd">@interface</span> <span class="nc">DayScoped</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

<span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Allowance</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">DailyAllowance</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Allowance</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Spender</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@Inject</span>
  <span class="nc">Spender</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Allowance</span> <span class="n">allowance</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">BindingModule</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">AbstractModule</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="nd">@Provides</span>
  <span class="nd">@DayScoped</span>
  <span class="nc">Allowance</span> <span class="nf">providesAllowance</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">DailyAllowance</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Here, the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Allowance</code> instance used by Spender isn’t actually scoped to a single
day, as the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Provides</code> method applies the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DayScoped</code> scoping only to the
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@DayScoped Allowance</code>. Instead, the default constructor of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Allowance</code> is used
to create a new instance every time a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Spender</code> is created.</p>

<p>If <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@DayScope</code> wasn’t a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Qualifier</code>, the provider method would do the right
thing: the un-annotated <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Allowance</code> binding would be scoped to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DayScope</code>,
implemented by a single <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">DailyAllowance</code> instance per day.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("OverlappingQualifierAndScopeAnnotation")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            OverridesJavaxInjectableMethod<br>
            <small>This method is not annotated with @Inject, but it overrides a method that is  annotated with @javax.inject.Inject. The method will not be Injected.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When classes declare that they have an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@javax.inject.Inject</code>ed method,
dependency injection tools must call those methods after first calling any
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@javax.inject.Inject</code> constructor, and performing any field injection. These
methods are part of the initialization contract for the object.</p>

<p>When subclasses override methods annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@javax.inject.Inject</code> and
<em>don’t</em> also annotate themselves with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@javax.inject.Inject</code>, the injector will
not call those methods as part of the subclass’s initialization. This may
unexpectedly cause assumptions taken in the superclass (e.g.: this
post-initialization routine is finished, meaning that I can safely use this
field) to no longer hold.</p>

<p>This compile error is intended to prevent this unintentional breaking of
assumptions. Possible resolutions to this error include:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Inject</code> the overridden method, calling the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">super</code> method to maintain the
initialization contract.</li>
  <li>Make the superclass’ method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">final</code> to avoid subclasses unintentionally
masking the injected method.</li>
  <li>Move the initialization work performed by the superclass method into the
constructor.</li>
  <li>Suppress this error, and very carefully inspect the initialization routine
performed by the superclass, making sure that any work that needs to be done
there is done in an @Inject method in the subclass. You may want to refactor
portions of the body of the superclass method into a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">protected</code> method for
this subclass to use.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("OverridesJavaxInjectableMethod")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            PackageInfo<br>
            <small>Declaring types inside package-info.java files is very bad form</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Classes should not be declared inside <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">package-info.java</code> files.</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Typically package-info.java contains only a package declaration, preceded
immediately by the annotations on the package. While the file could
technically contain the source code for one or more classes with package
access, it would be very bad form.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>– <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-7.html#jls-7.4">JLS 7.4</a></p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("PackageInfo")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          </h1>
        </div>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>

            PeriodGetTemporalUnit<br>
            <small>Period.get() only works with YEARS, MONTHS, or DAYS.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Period.get(TemporalUnit)</code> only works when passed <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ChronoUnit.YEARS</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ChronoUnit.MONTHS</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ChronoUnit.DAYS</code>. All other values are guaranteed to throw an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">UnsupportedTemporalTypeException</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("PeriodGetTemporalUnit")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            PreconditionsInvalidPlaceholder<br>
            <small>Preconditions only accepts the %s placeholder in error message strings</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>LikelyError</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The Guava Preconditions checks take error message template strings that look
similar to format strings, but only accept the %s format (not %d, %f, etc.).
This check points out places where a Preconditions error message template string
has a non-%s format, or where the number of arguments does not match the number
of %s formats in the string.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("PreconditionsInvalidPlaceholder")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ProtoStringFieldReferenceEquality<br>
            <small>Comparing protobuf fields of type String using reference equality</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Comparing strings with == is almost always an error, but it is an error 100% of
the time when one of the strings is a protobuf field. Additionally, protobuf
fields cannot be null, so Object.equals(Object) is always more correct.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ProtoStringFieldReferenceEquality")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>
