          <h1>
            ProtoTruthMixedDescriptors<br>
            <small>The arguments passed to `ignoringFields` are inconsistent with the proto which is the subject of the assertion.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>ProtoTruth’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#ignoringFields</code> method accepts integer field numbers, so
supplying field numbers from the wrong protocol buffers is possible. For
example:</p>

<div class="language-proto highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">message</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="k">optional</span> <span class="kt">string</span> <span class="na">name</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
<span class="kd">message</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="p">{</span>
  <span class="k">optional</span> <span class="kt">string</span> <span class="na">name</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">;</span>
  <span class="k">optional</span> <span class="n">Bar</span> <span class="na">bar</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">;</span>
<span class="p">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">assertOnFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">ignoringFields</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">NAME_FIELD_NUMBER</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isEqualTo</span><span class="o">(...);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This will ignore the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo#name</code> field rather than <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar#name</code>. The field number
can be turned into a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Descriptor</code> object to resolve the correct nested field to
ignore:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">assertOnFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span>
      <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">ignoringFieldDescriptors</span><span class="o">(</span>
          <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getDescriptor</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">findFieldByNumber</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">NAME_FIELD_NUMBER</span><span class="o">))</span>
      <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isEqualTo</span><span class="o">(...);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ProtoTruthMixedDescriptors")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ProtocolBufferOrdinal<br>
            <small>To get the tag number of a protocol buffer enum, use getNumber() instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The generated Java source files for Protocol Buffer enums have <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getNumber()</code> as
accessors for the tag number in the protobuf file.</p>

<p>In addition, since it’s a java enum, it also has the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ordinal()</code> method,
returning its positional index within the generated java enum.</p>

<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ordinal()</code> order of the generated Java enums isn’t guaranteed, and can
change when a new enum value is inserted into a proto enum. The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getNumber()</code>
value won’t change for an enum value (since making that change is a
backwards-incompatible change for the protocol buffer).</p>

<p>You should very likely use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getNumber()</code> in preference to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ordinal()</code> in all
circumstances since it’s a more stable value.</p>

<p>Note: If you’re changing code that was already using ordinal(), it’s likely that
getNumber() will return a different real value. Tread carefully to avoid
mismatches if the ordinal was persisted elsewhere.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ProtocolBufferOrdinal")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ProvidesMethodOutsideOfModule<br>
            <small>@Provides methods need to be declared in a Module to have any effect.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Guice <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Provides</code> methods annotate methods that are used as a means of declaring
bindings. However, this is only helpful inside of a module. Methods outside of
these modules are not used for binding declaration.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ProvidesMethodOutsideOfModule")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            RandomCast<br>
            <small>Casting a random number in the range [0.0, 1.0) to an integer or long always results in 0.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Math.random()</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Random#nextFloat</code>, and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Random#nextDouble</code> return results in
the range <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">[0.0, 1.0)</code>. Therefore, casting the result to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">(int)</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">(long)</code>
<em>always</em> results in the value of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("RandomCast")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            RandomModInteger<br>
            <small>Use Random.nextInt(int).  Random.nextInt() % n can have negative results</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Random.nextInt() % n</code> has</p>

<ul>
  <li>a 1/n chance of being 0</li>
  <li>a 1/2n chance of being each number from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">1</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">n-1</code> inclusive</li>
  <li>a 1/2n chance of being each number from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-1</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-(n-1)</code> inclusive</li>
</ul>

<p>Many users expect a uniformly distributed random integer between <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">n-1</code>
inclusive, but you must use random.nextInt(n) to get that behavior. If the
original behavior is truly desired, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">(random.nextBoolean() ? 1 : -1) *
random.nextInt(n)</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("RandomModInteger")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            RecordAccessorInCompactConstructor<br>
            <small>Record accessors read uninitialized fields inside a compact constructor. Use the component parameter instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>In a Java <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">record</code>, using the accessor method (like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">d()</code>) inside a <strong>compact
constructor</strong> (the one without arguments, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo { ... }</code>) reads the record’s
underlying field before it has been set. This means the method will always
return <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code> (for objects) or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> (for primitives), regardless of what
arguments were passed to the constructor.</p>

<h2 id="examples">Examples</h2>

<h3 id="bad-using-the-accessor-method">Bad: Using the accessor method</h3>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">record</span> <span class="nf">User</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">User</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// BUG: name() reads the uninitialized field 'this.name', which is currently</span>
    <span class="c1">// null. This throws a NullPointerException immediately.</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">isEmpty</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">IllegalArgumentException</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Name cannot be empty"</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="good-using-the-parameter-name-directly">Good: Using the parameter name directly</h3>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">record</span> <span class="nf">User</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">User</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// CORRECT: Reads the constructor parameter 'name'.</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isEmpty</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">IllegalArgumentException</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Name cannot be empty"</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="explanation">Explanation</h2>

<p>The <strong>Compact Constructor</strong> in Java is a special initialization block that runs
<em>before</em> the record’s fields are automatically assigned.</p>

<ol>
  <li><strong>Code Execution:</strong> The code inside your compact constructor <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">User { ... }</code>
runs first.</li>
  <li><strong>Field Assignment:</strong> The compiler automatically assigns the parameters to
the fields (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this.name = name;</code>) only <em>after</em> your code block finishes
(<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-8.html#jls-8.10.4.2">JLS §8.10.4.2</a>).</li>
</ol>

<p>When you call <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">name()</code>, it attempts to read <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this.name</code>. Since the assignment
hasn’t happened yet, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this.name</code> still holds its default value, which is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code>
(<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-4.html#jls-4.12.5">JLS §4.12.5</a>).</p>

<p>To fix this, refer to the component by its name (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">name</code>). This accesses
the <strong>parameter</strong> passed to the constructor, which holds the correct value.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("RecordAccessorInCompactConstructor")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            RectIntersectReturnValueIgnored<br>
            <small>Return value of android.graphics.Rect.intersect() must be checked</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">android.graphics.Rect.intersect(Rect r)</code> and
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">android.graphics.Rect.intersect(int, int, int, int)</code> do not always modify the
rectangle to the intersected result. If the rectangles do not intersect, no
change is made and the original rectangle is not modified. These methods return
false to indicate that this has happened.</p>

<p>If you don’t check the return value of these methods, you may end up drawing the
wrong rectangle.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("RectIntersectReturnValueIgnored")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            RedundantSetterCall<br>
            <small>A field was set twice in the same chained expression.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: ProtoRedundantSet</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Proto and AutoValue builders provide a fluent interface for constructing
instances. Unlike argument lists, however, they do not prevent the user from
providing multiple values for the same field.</p>

<p>Setting the same field multiple times in the same chained expression is
pointless (as the intermediate value will be overwritten), and can easily mask a
bug, especially if the setter is called with <em>different</em> arguments.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">MyProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">newBuilder</span><span class="o">()</span>
    <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">copy</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getFoo</span><span class="o">())</span>
    <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">copy</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getBar</span><span class="o">())</span>
    <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">build</span><span class="o">();</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("RedundantSetterCall")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            RequiredModifiers<br>
            <small>This annotation is missing required modifiers as specified by its @RequiredModifiers annotation</small>
          </h1>
        </div>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This annotation is itself annotated with @RequiredModifiers and can only be used
when the specified modifiers are present. You are attempting to use it on an
element that is missing one or more required modifiers.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

          <h1>
            RestrictedApi<br>
            <small>Check for non-allowlisted callers to RestrictedApiChecker.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Calls to APIs marked <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@RestrictedApi</code> are prohibited without a corresponding
allowlist annotation.</p>

<p>The intended use-case for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@RestrictedApi</code> is to restrict calls to annotated
methods so that each usage of those APIs must be reviewed separately. For
example, an API might lead to security bugs unless the programmer uses it
correctly.</p>

<p>See the
<a href="https://errorprone.info/api/latest/com/google/errorprone/annotations/RestrictedApi.html">javadoc for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@RestrictedApi</code></a>
for more details.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("RestrictedApi")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ReturnValueIgnored<br>
            <small>Return value of this method must be used</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: ResultOfMethodCallIgnored, CheckReturnValue</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Certain library methods do nothing useful if their return value is ignored. For
example, String.trim() has no side effects, and you must store the return value
of String.intern() to access the interned string. This check encodes a list of
methods in the JDK whose return value must be used and issues an error if they
are not.</p>

<h2 id="orElseThrow"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Optional.orElseThrow</code></h2>

<p>Don’t call <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">orElseThrow</code> just for its side-effects. When the result of a call to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">orElseThrow</code> is discarded, it may be unclear to future readers whether the
result is being discarded deliberately or accidentally. That is, avoid:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// return value of orElseThrow() is silently ignored here</span>
<span class="n">optional</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">orElseThrow</span><span class="o">(()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">AssertionError</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"something has gone terribly wrong"</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Instead of calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">orElseThrow</code> for its side-effects, prefer an explicit call
to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isPresent()</code>, or use one of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">checkState</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">checkArgument</code> from
<a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot-jre/api/docs/com/google/common/base/Preconditions.html">Guava’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Preconditions</code> class</a>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="n">optional</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isPresent</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">AssertionError</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"something has gone terribly wrong"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<pre><code class="language-{.good}">checkState(optional.isPresent(), "something has gone terribly wrong");
</code></pre>

<pre><code class="language-{.good}">checkArgument(optional.isPresent(), "something has gone terribly wrong");
</code></pre>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ReturnValueIgnored")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            SelfAssertion<br>
            <small>This assertion will always fail or succeed.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: TruthSelfEquals</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When using Truth, if a test subject and the argument to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isEqualTo</code> are the same
instance (for example <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat(x).isEqualTo(x)</code>), then the assertion will
always pass. Truth implements <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isEqualTo</code> using [<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Objects#equal</code>] , which tests
its arguments for reference equality and returns true without calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals()</code>
if both arguments are the same instance.</p>

<p>JUnit’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertEquals</code> (and similar) methods are implemented in terms of
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object#equals</code>. However, this is not explicitly documented, so isn’t a
contractual guarantee of the assertion methods.</p>

<p>To test the implementation of an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> method, use
<a href="https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.guava/guava-testlib/latest/com/google/common/testing/EqualsTester.html">Guava’s EqualsTester</a>, or explicitly call <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> as part of the
test.</p>

<p>In our experience, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat(x).isEqualTo(x)</code> and similar are <em>more likely to
be typos</em> than assertions about an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> method. This alone is sufficient
motivation to choose a dedicated approach for testing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> implementations.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("SelfAssertion")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            SelfAssignment<br>
            <small>Variable assigned to itself</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The left-hand side and right-hand side of this assignment are the same. It has
no effect.</p>

<p>This also handles assignments in which the right-hand side is a call to
Preconditions.checkNotNull(), which returns the variable that was checked for
non-nullity. If you just intended to check that the variable is non-null, please
don’t assign the result to the checked variable; just call
Preconditions.checkNotNull() as a bare statement.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("SelfAssignment")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            SelfEquals<br>
            <small>Testing an object for equality with itself will always be true.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The arguments to equals method are the same object, so it always returns true.
Either change the arguments to point to different objects or substitute true.</p>

<p>For test cases, instead of explicitly testing equals, use
<a href="https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.guava/guava-testlib/latest/com/google/common/testing/EqualsTester.html">EqualsTester from Guava</a>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("SelfEquals")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            SizeGreaterThanOrEqualsZero<br>
            <small>Comparison of a size >= 0 is always true, did you intend to check for non-emptiness?</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A standard means of checking non-emptiness of an array or collection is to test
if the size of that collection is greater than 0. However, one may accidentally
check if the size is greater than or equal to 0, which is always true.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("SizeGreaterThanOrEqualsZero")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">toString</code> method on a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Stream</code> will print its identity, such as
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.stream.ReferencePipeline$Head@6d06d69c</code>. This is rarely what was
intended.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("StreamToString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>String.substring(int) gives you the substring from the index to the end, inclusive. Calling that method with an index of 0 will return the same String.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("SubstringOfZero")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>To suppress warnings to deprecated methods, you should add the annotation
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")</code> and not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("deprecated")</code></p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>TemporalAccessor.get(ChronoField) only works for certain values of ChronoField. E.g., DayOfWeek only supports DAY_OF_WEEK. All other values are guaranteed to throw an UnsupportedTemporalTypeException.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TemporalAccessorGetChronoField")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>

<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ThrowNull")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            TreeToString<br>
            <small>Tree#toString shouldn't be used for Trees deriving from the code being compiled, as it discards whitespace and comments.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Tree#toString</code> shouldn’t be used for Trees deriving from the code being
compiled, as it discards whitespace and comments.</p>

<p>This check only runs inside Error Prone code. Suggested replacements include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">VisitorState#getConstantExpression</code> for escaping constants in
generated code.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">VisitorState#getSourceForNode</code> : it will give you the original source text.
Note that for synthetic trees (e.g.: implicit constructors), that source may
be <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code>.</li>
  <li>If the string representation was being used for comparison with keywords
like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">super</code>, try <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">tree.getName().contentEquals("this")</code></li>
  <li>One can also get the symbol name and use it for comparison :
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ASTHelpers.getSymbol(tree).getSimpleName().toString()</code></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TreeToString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            TryFailThrowable<br>
            <small>Catching Throwable/Error masks failures from fail() or assert*() in the try block</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When testing that a line of code throws an expected exception, it is typical to
execute that line in a try block with a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code> on the line
following. The expectation is that the expected exception will be thrown, and
execution will continue in the catch block, and the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code> will
not be executed.</p>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code> throw AssertionErrors, which are a subtype of
Throwable. That means that if the catch block catches Throwable, then execution
will always jump to the catch block, and the test will always pass.</p>

<p>To fix this, you usually want to catch Exception rather than Throwable. If you
need to catch throwable (e.g., the expected exception is an AssertionError),
then add logic in your catch block to ensure that the AssertionError that was
caught is not the same one thrown by the call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TryFailThrowable")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            TypeParameterQualifier<br>
            <small>Type parameter used as type qualifier</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using a type parameter as a qualifier in the name of a type or expression is
equivalent to referencing the type parameter’s upper bound directly.</p>

<p>For example, this signature:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">static</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Message</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">populate</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Builder</span> <span class="n">builder</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Is identical to the following:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">static</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Message</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">populate</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Message</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Builder</span> <span class="n">builder</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The use of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">T.Builder</code> is unnecessary and misleading. Always refer to the type
by its canonical name <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Message.Builder</code> instead.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>This check may not be suppressed.</p>

          <h1>
            UnicodeInCode<br>
            <small>Avoid using non-ASCII Unicode characters outside of comments and literals, as they can be confusing.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using non-ASCII Unicode characters in code can be confusing, and potentially
unsafe.</p>

<p>For example, homoglyphs can result in a different method to the one that was
expected being invoked.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">static</span> <span class="n">com</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">google</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">common</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">base</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Objects</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equal</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">isAuthenticated</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">password</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// The "l" here is not what it seems.</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">equaⅼ</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">password</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="k">this</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">password</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="c1">// ...</span>

<span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="n">equaⅼ</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnicodeInCode")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            UnnecessaryTypeArgument<br>
            <small>Non-generic methods should not be invoked with type arguments</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.12.2.1">JLS §15.12.2.1</a> allows non-generic methods to be invoked with type arguments:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>a non-generic method may be potentially applicable to an invocation that
supplies explicit type arguments. Indeed, it may turn out to be applicable. In
such a case, the type arguments will simply be ignored.</p>

  <p>This rule stems from issues of compatibility and principles of
substitutability. Since interfaces or superclasses may be generified
independently of their subtypes, we may override a generic method with a
non-generic one. However, the overriding (non-generic) method must be
applicable to calls to the generic method, including calls that explicitly
pass type arguments. Otherwise the subtype would not be substitutable for its
generified supertype.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>There is no reason to do this in cases where the method being called is not an
override of a generic method.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryTypeArgument")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            UnusedAnonymousClass<br>
            <small>Instance created but never used</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Creating a side-effect-free anonymous class and never using it is usually a
mistake.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">Thread</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Runnable</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nd">@Override</span> <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">run</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="n">preventMissionCriticalDisasters</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">});</span> <span class="c1">// did you mean to call Thread#start()?</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnusedAnonymousClass")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            UnusedCollectionModifiedInPlace<br>
            <small>Collection is modified in place, but the result is not used</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Several of the methods in <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Collections</code>, such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">sort</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">shuffle</code>,
modify collections in place. If you call one of these methods on a
newly-allocated collection and don’t use it later, you are doing unnecessary
work. You probably meant to keep a reference to the newly-allocated copy of your
collection and use that in the rest of your code.</p>

<p>For example, this code sorts a new <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayList</code> and then throws away the result,
returning the unsorted original collection:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nc">Collection</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">sort</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Collection</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Collections</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">sort</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;(</span><span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">));</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The author probably meant:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nc">Collection</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">sort</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Collection</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">sortedFoos</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;(</span><span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="nc">Collections</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">sort</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">sortedFoos</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">sortedFoos</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnusedCollectionModifiedInPlace")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            VarTypeName<br>
            <small>`var` should not be used as a type name.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>As of JDK 10 <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">var</code> is a restricted local variable type and cannot be used for
type declarations (see <a href="https://openjdk.java.net/jeps/286">JEP 286</a>).</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("VarTypeName")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            WrongOneof<br>
            <small>This field is guaranteed not to be set given it's within a switch over a one_of.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When switching over a proto <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">one_of</code>, getters that don’t match the current case
are guaranteed to be return a default instance:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">switch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getBlahCase</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">FOO:</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getFoo</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">BAR:</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getFoo</span><span class="o">();</span> <span class="c1">// should be foo.getBar()</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("WrongOneof")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            XorPower<br>
            <small>The `^` operator is binary XOR, not a power operator.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>ERROR</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">^</code> binary XOR operator is sometimes mistaken for a power operator, but e.g.
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">2 ^ 2</code> evaluates to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code>, not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">4</code>.</p>

<p>Consider expressing powers of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">2</code> using a bit shift instead.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("XorPower")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AddressSelection<br>
            <small>Prefer InetAddress.getAllByName to APIs that convert a hostname to a single IP address</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Avoid APIs that convert a hostname to a single IP address:</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/net/Socket.html#%3Cinit%3E\(java.lang.String,int,boolean\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.net.Socket(String,int)</code></a></li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/net/InetSocketAddress.html#%3Cinit%3E\(java.lang.String,int\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.net.InetSocketAddress(String,int)</code></a></li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/net/InetAddress.html#getByName\(java.lang.String\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.net.InetAddress.html#getByName(String)</code></a></li>
</ul>

<p>Depending on the value of the
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/net/doc-files/net-properties.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true</code></a>
system property, those APIs will return an IPv4 or IPv6 address. If a client
only has IPv4 connectivity, it will fail to connect with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true</code>. If a client only has IPv6 connectivity,
it will fail to connect with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=false</code>.</p>

<p>The preferred alternative is for clients to consider all addresses returned by
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/net/InetAddress.html#getAllByName\(java.lang.String\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.net.InetAddress.html#getAllByName(String)</code></a>,
and try to connect to each one until a successful connection is made.</p>

<p>TIP: To resolve a loopback address, prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress()</code>
over hard-coding an IPv4 or IPv6 loopback address with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1")</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InetAddress.getByName("::1")</code>.</p>

<p>This is, prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nc">Socket</span> <span class="nf">doConnect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">exception</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">InetAddress</span> <span class="n">address</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="nc">InetAddress</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getAllByName</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">Socket</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">address</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">);</span>
      <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">exception</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
          <span class="n">exception</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">;</span>
        <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="o">{</span>
          <span class="n">exception</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addSuppressed</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span>
        <span class="o">}</span>
      <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="n">exception</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nc">Socket</span> <span class="nf">doConnect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">exception</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="k">for</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">InetAddress</span> <span class="n">address</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="nc">InetAddress</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getAllByName</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="nc">Socket</span> <span class="n">s</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Socket</span><span class="o">();</span>
        <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">connect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">InetSocketAddress</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">address</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">));</span>
        <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">;</span>
      <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">exception</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
          <span class="n">exception</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">;</span>
        <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="o">{</span>
          <span class="n">exception</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addSuppressed</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span>
        <span class="o">}</span>
      <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="n">exception</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>instead of this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nc">Socket</span> <span class="nf">doConnect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">Socket</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doConnect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">Socket</span> <span class="n">s</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Socket</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">connect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">InetSocketAddress</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">));</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doConnect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">Socket</span> <span class="n">s</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Socket</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">connect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">InetSocketAddress</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">InetAddress</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getByName</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hostname</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="o">));</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AddressSelection")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            AlreadyChecked<br>
            <small>This condition has already been checked.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Checking a provably-identical condition twice can be a sign of a logic error.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">first</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isPresent</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isPresent</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="c1">// Oops--should be checking `b`.</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">empty</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>It can also be a sign of redundancy, which can just be removed.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">act</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">enabled</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">frobnicate</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="n">enabled</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="c1">// !enabled is guaranteed to be true here, so the check can be removed</span>
    <span class="n">doSomethingElse</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AlreadyChecked")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            AmbiguousMethodReference<br>
            <small>Method reference is ambiguous</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The following code is fine in Java 7, but poses a problem in Java 8.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">A</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="no">B</span> <span class="nf">c</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">D</span> <span class="n">d</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="no">B</span> <span class="nf">c</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">A</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">D</span> <span class="n">d</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The method reference <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A::c</code> of the instance method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">c</code> has an implicit first
parameter for the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this</code> pointer. So both methods that <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A::c</code> could resolve to
are compatible with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">BiFunction&lt;A, D, B&gt;</code>, and the method reference is
ambiguous.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">BiFunction</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">A</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">D</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">B</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">f</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">...</span> <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>error: incompatible types: invalid method reference
    f(A::c);
      ^
    reference to c is ambiguous
      both method c(A,D) in A and method c(D) in A match
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Consider renaming one of the methods to avoid the ambiguity.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AmbiguousMethodReference")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AnnotateFormatMethod<br>
            <small>This method uses a pair of parameters as a format string and its arguments, but the enclosing method wasn't annotated. Doing so gives compile-time rather than run-time protection against malformed format strings.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This method passes a pair of parameters through to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String#format</code>, but the
enclosing method wasn’t annotated <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatMethod</code>. Doing so gives compile-time
rather than run-time protection against malformed format strings. Consider
annotating the format string with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@com.google.errorprone.annotations.FormatString</code> and the method with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatMethod</code> to allow compile-time checking for well-formed format strings.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">format</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Log</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">w</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">format</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">frobnicate</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">a</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Whoops: didn't provide enough format args.</span>
    <span class="n">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"%s &lt; %s"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@FormatMethod</span>
<span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@FormatString</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">format</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Log</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">w</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">format</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>WARNING: There’s a very high chance that manual intervention will be required
after applying this fix, either due to existing uses of the method not passing
in valid format strings, or methods which delegate to this one requiring the
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@FormatMethod</code> annotation as well. Please ensure that everything depending on
this code still compiles after applying.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AnnotateFormatMethod")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ArgumentSelectionDefectChecker<br>
            <small>Arguments are in the wrong order or could be commented for clarity.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>If permuting the arguments of a method call means that the argument names are a
better match for the parameter names than the original ordering then this might
indicate that they have been accidentally swapped. There are also legitimate
reasons for the names not to match such as when rotating an image (swap width
and height). In this case we suggest annotating the names with a comment to make
the deliberate swap clear to future readers of the code. Argument names
annotated with a comment containing the parameter name will not generate a
warning.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ArgumentSelectionDefectChecker")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ArrayRecordComponent<br>
            <small>Record components should not be arrays.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>There are two main problems with having a component of a record be an array.</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>By default, the generated <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> will just call <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> or
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> on the array. Two distinct arrays are never considered equal by
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> even if their contents are the same. The generated <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">toString</code> is
similarly not useful, since it will be something like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">[B@723279cf</code>.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Arrays are mutable, but records should not be mutable. A client of a record
with an array component can change the contents of the array.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<p>Instead of an array component, consider something like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableList&lt;String&gt;</code>,
or, for primitive arrays, something like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteString</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableIntArray</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            AssertEqualsArgumentOrderChecker<br>
            <small>Arguments are swapped in assertEquals-like call</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>JUnit’s assertEquals (and similar) are defined to take the expected value first
and the actual value second. Getting these the wrong way round will cause a
confusing error message if the assertion fails.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AssertEqualsArgumentOrderChecker")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>
