    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AssertThrowsMinimizer<br>
            <small>Minimize the amount of logic in assertThrows</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer to minimize the amount of logic in a lambda passed to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows</code>.</p>

<p>An <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows</code> assertion will pass if any code in the provided lambda throws
the given exception. If the lambda contains multiple expressions that may throw,
the test may incorrectly pass if an earlier expression unexpectedly throws. For
example, consider:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="nc">IllegalArgumentException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span>
        <span class="nc">EncodingUtil</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">convertAudioFormatToMp3Configuration</span><span class="o">(</span>
            <span class="nc">AudioEncoding</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">newBuilder</span><span class="o">()</span>
                <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setAudioFormat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">AudioFormat</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">AUDIO_FORMAT_MP3</span><span class="o">)</span>
                <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setAudioQuality</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">AudioQuality</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">UNRECOGNIZED</span><span class="o">)</span>
                <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">build</span><span class="o">()));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This assertion is intended to check that
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">convertAudioFormatToMp3Configuration()</code> throws <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">IllegalArgumentException</code>, but
the assertion will always pass because the setup logic in
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">setAudioQuality(AudioQuality.UNRECOGNIZED)</code> is incorrect and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">build()</code> will
throw <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">IllegalArgumentException</code>.</p>

<p>Instead, you should minimize the amount of logic inside of your <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows</code>:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">AudioEncoding</span> <span class="n">audioEncoding</span> <span class="o">=</span>
    <span class="nc">AudioEncoding</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">newBuilder</span><span class="o">()</span>
        <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setAudioFormat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">AudioFormat</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">AUDIO_FORMAT_MP3</span><span class="o">)</span>
        <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setAudioQuality</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">AudioQuality</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">UNRECOGNIZED</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="c1">// BOOM goes the dynamite!</span>
        <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">build</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="nc">IllegalArgumentException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">EncodingUtil</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">convertAudioFormatToMp3Configuration</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">audioEncoding</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The test above now (correctly) fails and exposes the setup issue.</p>

<h2 id="var">Variable types and names</h2>

<p>This check tries to pick a reasonable name for the extracted variable, but there
may be a better name. If the extracted variable seems verbose, consider renaming
it to improve readability.</p>

<p>In some cases a judicious use of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">var</code> could improve readability, following the
<a href="https://openjdk.java.net/projects/amber/guides/lvti-style-guide">guidelines for usage of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">var</code></a>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AssertThrowsMinimizer")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AssertThrowsMultipleStatements<br>
            <small>The lambda passed to assertThrows should contain exactly one statement</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>If the body of the lambda passed to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows</code> contains multiple statements,
execution of the lambda will stop at the first statement that throws an
exception and all subsequent statements will be ignored.</p>

<p>This means that:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Any set-up logic in the lambda will cause the test to incorrectly pass if it
throws the expected exception.</li>
  <li>Any assertions that run after the statement that throws will never be
executed.</li>
</ul>

<p>Don’t do this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="nc">UnsupportedOperationException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span> <span class="n">list</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span><span class="o">();</span>
        <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span>
        <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">);</span>
        <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">containsExactly</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">});</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Do this instead:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span> <span class="n">list</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="nc">UnsupportedOperationException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">));</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">containsExactly</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AssertThrowsMultipleStatements")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AssertionFailureIgnored<br>
            <small>This assertion throws an AssertionError if it fails, which will be caught by an enclosing try block.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>LikelyError</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>JUnit’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*</code> methods throw an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AssertionError</code>, so using the
try/fail/catch pattern to test for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AssertionError</code> (or any of its super-types)
is incorrect. The following example will never fail:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">doSomething</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">fail</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"expected doSomething to throw AssertionError"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">AssertionError</span> <span class="n">expected</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// expected exception</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To avoid this issue, prefer JUnit’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows()</code> API:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">static</span> <span class="n">com</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">google</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">common</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">truth</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Truth</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">assertThat</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">static</span> <span class="n">org</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">junit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Assert</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">assertThrows</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">testFailsWithAssertionError</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">AssertionError</span> <span class="n">thrown</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span>
      <span class="nc">AssertionError</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span>
      <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="n">doSomething</span><span class="o">();</span>
      <span class="o">});</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">thrown</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasMessageThat</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"something went terribly wrong"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AssertionFailureIgnored")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AssignmentExpression<br>
            <small>The use of an assignment expression can be surprising and hard to read; consider factoring out the assignment to a separate statement.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using the result of an assignment expression can be quite unclear, except for
simple cases where the result is used to initialise another variable, such as
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x = y = 0</code>.</p>

<p>Consider a common pattern of lazily initialising a field:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Lazy</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">abstract</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">create</span><span class="o">();</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">get</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">create</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Lazy</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">abstract</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">create</span><span class="o">();</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">get</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="n">t</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">create</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>At the cost of another line, it’s now clearer what’s happening. (Note that
neither the before nor the after are thread-safe; this particular example would
be better served with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Suppliers.memoizing</code>.)</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AssignmentExpression")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>

          </dl>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using @AssistedInject and @Inject on the same constructor is a runtimeerror in
Guice.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AssistedInjectAndInjectOnSameConstructor")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            AttemptedNegativeZero<br>
            <small>-0 is the same as 0. For the floating-point negative zero, use -0.0.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Because <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code> is an integer constant, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-0</code> is an integer, too. Integers have no
concept of “negative zero,” so it is the same as plain <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code>.</p>

<p>The value is then widened to a floating-point number. And while floating-point
numbers have a concept of “negative zero,” the integral <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code> is widened to the
floating-point “positive” zero.</p>

<p>To write a negative zero, you have to write a constant that is a floating-point
number. One simple way to do that is to write <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-0.0</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AttemptedNegativeZero")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            AutoValueBoxedValues<br>
            <small>AutoValue instances should not usually contain boxed types that are not Nullable. We recommend removing the unnecessary boxing.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>AutoValue classes reject <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code> values, unless the property is annotated with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Nullable</code>. For this reason, the usage of boxed primitives (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Long</code>) is
discouraged, except when annotated as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Nullable</code>. Otherwise they can be
replaced with the corresponding primitive. There could be some cases where the
usage of a boxed primitive might be intentional to avoid boxing the value again
after invoking the getter.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>Suppress violations by using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AutoValueBoxedValues")</code> on the
relevant <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">abstract</code> getter and/or setter.</p>

<h2 id="suppression-1">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AutoValueBoxedValues")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AutoValueFinalMethods<br>
            <small>Make toString(), hashCode() and equals() final in AutoValue classes, so it is clear to readers that AutoValue is not overriding them</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Consider that other developers will try to read and understand your value class
while looking only at your hand-written class, not the actual (generated)
implementation class. If you mark your concrete methods final, they won’t have
to wonder whether the generated subclass might be overriding them. This is
especially helpful if you are underriding equals, hashCode or toString!</p>

<p>Reference:
https://github.com/google/auto/blob/master/value/userguide/practices.md#mark-all-concrete-methods-final</p>

<p>NOTE:
<a href="https://github.com/google/auto/blob/master/value/userguide/howto.md#memoize_hash_tostring">Since <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Memoized</code> methods can’t be final</a>,
the check doesn’t flag them.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AutoValueFinalMethods")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AutoValueImmutableFields<br>
            <small>AutoValue recommends using immutable collections</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: mutable</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><a href="https://github.com/google/auto/tree/master/value">AutoValue</a> instances should
be deeply immutable. Therefore, we recommend using immutable types for fields.
E.g., use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableMap</code> instead of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Map</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableSet</code> instead of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Set</code>, etc.</p>

<p>Read more at:</p>

<ul>
  <li>https://github.com/google/auto/blob/master/value/userguide/practices.md#avoid-mutable-property-types</li>
  <li>https://github.com/google/auto/blob/master/value/userguide/builders-howto.md#-use-a-collection-valued-property</li>
</ul>

<p>Suppress violations by using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AutoValueImmutableFields")</code> on
the relevant <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">abstract</code> getter.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AutoValueSubclassLeaked<br>
            <small>Do not refer to the autogenerated AutoValue_ class outside the file containing the corresponding @AutoValue base class.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>@AutoValue-annotated classes may form part of your API, but the AutoValue_ generated classes should not. The fact that the generated classes are visible to other classes within the same package is an implementation detail, and is best avoided. Ideally, any reference to the AutoValue_-prefixed class should be confined to a single factory method, with other factories delegating to it if necessary.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AutoValueSubclassLeaked")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            AvoidCommonTypeNames<br>
            <small>Never reuse class names from java.lang</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Style</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: JavaLangClash</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Class names from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.lang</code> should never be reused. From
<a href="http://www.javapuzzlers.com/java-puzzlers-sampler.pdf">Java Puzzlers</a>:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Avoid reusing the names of platform classes, and never reuse class names from
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.lang</code>, because these names are automatically imported everywhere.
Programmers are used to seeing these names in their unqualified form and
naturally assume that these names refer to the familiar classes from
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.lang</code>. If you reuse one of these names, the unqualified name will refer
to the new definition any time it is used inside its own package.</p>
</blockquote>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("AvoidCommonTypeNames")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            BadComparable<br>
            <small>Possible sign flip from narrowing conversion</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A narrowing integral conversion can cause a sign flip, since it simply discards
all but the n lowest order bits, where n is the number of bits used to represent
the target type (JLS 5.1.3). In a compare or compareTo method, this can cause
incorrect and unstable sort orders.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("BadComparable")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            BadInstanceof<br>
            <small>instanceof used in a way that is equivalent to a null check.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Simplification</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Flags <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code> checks where the expression can be determined to be a
supertype of the type it is compared to.</p>

<p><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.28">JLS 15.28</a>
specifically calls <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code> out as <em>not</em> being a compile-time constant
expression, so the usage of this pattern can lead to unreachable code that won’t
be flagged by the compiler:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomething</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="k">this</span> <span class="k">instanceof</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="c1">// BAD: always true</span>
      <span class="k">return</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="n">interestingProcessing</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>In general, an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code> comparison against a superclass is equivalent to a
null check:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">foo</span> <span class="k">instanceof</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="kc">null</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Pattern-matching <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code>s introduce some extra complexity into this. It may
be tempting to use an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code> check to define a narrowly-scoped local
variable which gets reused within an expression, for example,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getSubMessage</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="k">instanceof</span> <span class="nc">SubMessage</span> <span class="n">sm</span>
    <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">sm</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getForename</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"John"</span><span class="o">)</span>
    <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">sm</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getSurname</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Smith"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>We feel this urge should be resisted. While this is a clever trick to avoid an
extra line, it is not a true <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code> check, and declaring a variable
normally is clearer:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">SubMessage</span> <span class="n">sm</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getSubMessage</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">sm</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getForename</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"John"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">sm</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getSurname</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Smith"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("BadInstanceof")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

            BigDecimalEquals<br>
            <small>BigDecimal#equals has surprising behavior: it also compares scale.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">BigDecimal</code>’s equals method compares the scale of the representation as well as
the numeric value, which may not be expected.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">BigDecimal</span> <span class="n">a</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">BigDecimal</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"1.0"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="nc">BigDecimal</span> <span class="n">b</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">BigDecimal</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"1.00"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="n">a</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">b</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// false!</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("BigDecimalEquals")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            BigDecimalLiteralDouble<br>
            <small>new BigDecimal(double) loses precision in this case.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>BigDecimal’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">double</code> can lose precision in surprising ways.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="c1">// these are the same:</span>
  <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">BigDecimal</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">0.1</span><span class="o">)</span>
  <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">BigDecimal</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625"</span><span class="o">)</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prefer the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">BigDecimal.valueOf(double)</code> method or the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">new BigDecimal(String)</code>
constructor.</p>

<p>NOTE <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">BigDecimal.valueOf(double)</code> does not suffer from the same problem; it is
equivalent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">new BigDecimal(Double.valueOf(double))</code>, and while <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0.1</code> is not
exactly representable, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Double.valueOf(0.1)</code> yields <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">"0.1"</code>. As long as
<a href="./FloatingPointLiteralPrecision">FloatingPointLiteralPrecision</a> doesn’t
generate a warning, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">BigDecimal.valueOf</code> is safe.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("BigDecimalLiteralDouble")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            BoxedPrimitiveConstructor<br>
            <small>valueOf or autoboxing provides better time and space performance</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Performance</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Constructors of primitive wrapper objects (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">new Boolean(true)</code> will be
<a href="https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8145468">deprecated</a> in Java 9. The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">valueOf</code> factory methods (e.g.
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Boolean.valueOf(true)</code>) should always be preferred. Those methods are called
implicitly by autoboxing, which is often more convenient than an explicit call.
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer x = Integer.valueOf(23);</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer x = 23;</code> are equivalent.</p>

<p>The explicit constructors always return a fresh instance, resulting in
unnecessary allocations. The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">valueOf</code> methods return cached instances for
frequently requested values, offering significantly better space and time
performance.</p>

<p>Relying on the unique reference identity of the instances returned by the
explicit constructors is extremely bad practice. Primitives should always be
treated as identity-less value types, even in their boxed representations.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("BoxedPrimitiveConstructor")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            ByteBufferBackingArray<br>
            <small>ByteBuffer.array() shouldn't be called unless ByteBuffer.arrayOffset() is used or if the ByteBuffer was initialized using ByteBuffer.wrap() or ByteBuffer.allocate().</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer</code> provides a view of an underlying bytes storage. The two most common
implementations are the non-direct byte buffers, which are backed by a bytes
array, and direct byte buffers, which usually are off-heap directly mapped to
memory. Thus, not all <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer</code> implementations are backed by a bytes array,
and when they are, the beginning of the array returned by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.array()</code> may not
necessarily correspond to the beginning of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer</code>.</p>

<p>Since it’s so finicky, <strong>use of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.array()</code> is discouraged. Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.get(...)</code> to
copy the underlying data instead.</strong></p>

<p>But, if you <em>absolutely must</em> use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.array()</code> to look behind the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer</code>
curtain, check all of the following:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Ensure there is a backing array with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.hasArray()</code></li>
  <li>Check the start position of the backing array by calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.arrayOffset()</code></li>
  <li>Check the end position of the backing array with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.remaining()</code></li>
</ul>

<p>If you know that the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer</code> was created locally with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer.wrap(...)</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ByteBuffer.allocate(...)</code>, it’s safe, you can use the
backing array normally, without checking the above.</p>

<p>Do this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// Use `.get(...)` to copy the byte[] without changing the current position.</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">foo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="kt">byte</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">bytes</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="kt">byte</span><span class="o">[</span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remaining</span><span class="o">()];</span>
   <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">get</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">bytes</span><span class="o">);</span>
   <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">position</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">position</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-</span> <span class="n">bytes</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">length</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Restores the buffer position</span>
   <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// Use `.array()` only if you also check `.hasArray()`, `.arrayOffset()`, and `.remaining()`.</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">foo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hasArray</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">startIndex</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">arrayOffset</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">curIndex</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">arrayOffset</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">position</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">endIndex</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">curIndex</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remaining</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="c1">// Access elements of `.array()` with the above indices ...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// No checking necessary when the buffer was constructed locally with `allocate(...)`.</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">foo</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span> <span class="n">buffer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">allocate</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">SIZE</span> <span class="o">/</span> <span class="nc">Byte</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">SIZE</span><span class="o">);</span>
      <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">putLong</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1L</span><span class="o">);</span>
      <span class="c1">// ...</span>
      <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">array</span><span class="o">();</span>
      <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// No checking necessary when the buffer was constructed locally with `wrap(...)`.</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">foo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">byte</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">bytes</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span> <span class="n">buffer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">wrap</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">bytes</span><span class="o">);</span>
   <span class="c1">// ...</span>
   <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">array</span><span class="o">();</span>
   <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Not this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">foo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="kt">byte</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">dataAsBytesArray</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">buffer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">array</span><span class="o">();</span>
   <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ByteBufferBackingArray")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            CanonicalDuration<br>
            <small>Duration can be expressed more clearly with different units</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer to express durations using the largest possible unit, e.g.
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Duration.ofDays(1)</code> instead of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Duration.ofSeconds(86400)</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("CanonicalDuration")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            CatchAndPrintStackTrace<br>
            <small>Logging or rethrowing exceptions should usually be preferred to catching and calling printStackTrace</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Discarding an exception after calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">printStackTrace</code> should usually be
avoided.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">logger</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">INFO</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"something has gone terribly wrong"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">UncheckedIOException</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// New in Java 8</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">IOException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">printStackTrace</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("CatchAndPrintStackTrace")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            CatchFail<br>
            <small>Ignoring exceptions and calling fail() is unnecessary, and makes test output less useful</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Ignoring an exception and calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> is unnecessary, since an uncaught
exception will already cause a test to fail. It also makes the test output less
useful, since the exception’s message and stack trace is lost.</p>

<p>Do this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">testFoo</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">();</span> <span class="c1">// the test fails if this throws</span>
   <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isEqualTo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">testFoo</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="kd">throws</span> <span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">;</span>
   <span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
     <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">();</span>
   <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
     <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">AssertionError</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"the test failed"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// wraps the exception with additional context</span>
   <span class="o">}</span>
   <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isEqualTo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Not this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">testFoo</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
   <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">;</span>
   <span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
     <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">foos</span><span class="o">();</span>
   <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Exception</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
     <span class="n">fail</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"the test failed"</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// the exception message and stack trace is lost</span>
   <span class="o">}</span>
   <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isEqualTo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("CatchFail")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ChainedAssertionLosesContext<br>
            <small>Inside a Subject, use check(...) instead of assert*() to preserve user-supplied messages and other settings.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Assertions made <em>inside the implementation of another <a href="https://github.com/google/truth">Truth</a> assertion</em> should
use <a href="https://google.github.io/truth/api/latest/com/google/common/truth/Subject.html#check-java.lang.String-java.lang.Object...-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">check</code></a>, not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat</code>.</p>

<p>Before:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>class MyProtoSubject extends Subject {
  ...

  public void hasFoo(Foo expected) {
    assertThat(actual.foo()).isEqualTo(expected);
  }
}
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>After:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>class MyProtoSubject extends Subject {
  ...

  public void hasFoo(Foo expected) {
    check("foo()").that(actual.foo()).isEqualTo(expected);
  }
}
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Benefits of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">check</code> include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>When the assertion fails, the failure message includes more context: The
message specifies that the assertion was performed on <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myProto.foo()</code>, and
it includes the full value of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myProto</code> for reference.</li>
  <li>If the user of the assertion called <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertWithMessage</code>, that message, which
is lost in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat</code> version, is shown by the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">check</code> version.</li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">check</code> makes it possible to test the assertion with <a href="https://google.github.io/truth/api/latest/com/google/common/truth/ExpectFailure.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ExpectFailure</code></a> and
to use <a href="https://google.github.io/truth/api/latest/com/google/common/truth/Expect.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Expect</code></a> or <a href="https://google.github.io/truth/api/latest/com/google/common/truth/TruthJUnit.html#assume--"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assume</code></a>. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat</code>, by contrast, overrides any
user-specified failure behavior.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ChainedAssertionLosesContext")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            CharacterGetNumericValue<br>
            <small>getNumericValue has unexpected behaviour: it interprets A-Z as base-36 digits with values 10-35, but also supports non-arabic numerals and miscellaneous numeric unicode characters like ㊷; consider using Character.digit or UCharacter.getUnicodeNumericValue instead</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.getNumericValue</code> has unexpected behaviour: it interprets A-Z as
base-36 digits with values 10-35, but also supports non-arabic numerals and
miscellaneous numeric unicode characters like ㊷. For example:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.getNumericValue('V' /* ASCII V */) == 31</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.getNumericValue('Ⅴ' /* U+2164, Roman numeral 5 */) == 5</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.getNumericValue('௧' /* U+0BF2, Tamil Digit One */) == 1</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.getNumericValue('௲' /* U+0BF2, Tamil Number One Thousand */) ==
1000</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.getNumericValue('㊷' /* U+32B7, Circled Number Forty Two */) ==
42</code></li>
</ul>

<p><a href="https://unicode-org.github.io/icu-docs/apidoc/released/icu4j/com/ibm/icu/lang/UCharacter.html#getNumericValue-int-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">UCharacter.getNumericValue</code></a>
has the same behavior.</p>

<p>Consider using:</p>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://unicode-org.github.io/icu-docs/apidoc/released/icu4j/com/ibm/icu/lang/UCharacter.html#getUnicodeNumericValue-int-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">UCharacter.getUnicodeNumericValue</code></a>:
Handles all unicode codepoints with numeric values including fractions,
roman numerals, and other miscellaneous numeric characters. Returns the
value as a double. Does not assign a value to A-Z.</li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Character.html#digit-char-int-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Character.digit</code></a>:
Handles unicode codepoints in the “decimal digit” category and the letters
A-Z which are interpreted as base-36 digits with values 10-35. Does not
handle characters like roman numerals and ㊷. You can use a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">radix</code> value of
10 or less to avoid interpreting A-Z as digits.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("CharacterGetNumericValue")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ClassCanBeStatic<br>
            <small>Inner class is non-static but does not reference enclosing class</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Style, Performance</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: InnerClassMayBeStatic</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>An inner class should be static unless it references members of its enclosing
class. An inner class that is made non-static unnecessarily uses more memory and
does not make the intent of the class clear.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ClassCanBeStatic")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ClassInitializationDeadlock<br>
            <small>Possible class initialization deadlock</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>To avoid deadlocks, class initializers should not reference subtypes of the
current class.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="no">INSTANCE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>There is a circular reference between the class initializers for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code> and
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code>: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code> depends on <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code> in the initializer for a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static</code> field, and
initializing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code> requires initializing its supertype <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code>. If one thread
starts initializing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code> and another thread simultaneously starts initializing
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code>, it will result in a deadlock.</p>

<h2 id="suggested-fixes">Suggested fixes</h2>

<p>The best solution is to refactor to break the cycle, by defining the constant
field in a separate class from the supertype of the field.</p>

<p>For example, using this approach to fix the sample above would result in
something like:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foos</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="no">INSTANCE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>That refactoring may be too invasive (say the code is part of an API, and there
are many references to the current structure).</p>

<p>If the subclass is never referenced outside the current file (i.e. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code> is
never used outside of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code>, it is only referenced via <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo.INSTANCE</code>), making
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Bar</code> <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code> makes deadlocks less likely (see caveats below in the discussion
about <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code> classes):</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="no">INSTANCE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If the subclass <em>is</em> referenced outside the current field, deadlocks can be
avoided by ensuring that the subclass has only private constructors (or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static</code>
factory methods), so that the only way to initialize the subclass is to first
initialize the containing class:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="no">INSTANCE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="nf">Bar</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If the subclass needs to be directly created by code outside the current file, a
static factory can be added as a member of the outer class, for example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="no">INSTANCE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">();</span>

  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="nf">Bar</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="nf">createBar</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">Bar</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<hr />

<h2 id="autovalue">AutoValue</h2>

<p>AutoValue implementation classes are necessarily non-<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code>, since they are
generated into separate files. However examples like the following can’t
deadlock as long as the only reference to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AutoValue_Base</code> class is inside
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Base</code>, since there is no way for a thread to cause <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AutoValue_Base</code> to be
initialized without first having initialized <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Base</code>:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@AutoValue</span>
<span class="kd">abstract</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Base</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">abstract</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="nf">bar</span><span class="o">();</span>

  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="no">DEFAULT</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="n">AutoValue_Base</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"bar"</span><span class="o">);</span>

  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Base</span> <span class="nf">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">bar</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">AutoValue_Base</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">bar</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>There is a separate Error Prone check, https://errorprone.info/bugpattern/AutoValueSubclassLeaked, to
prevent <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AutoValue_</code> classes from being accessed outside the file containing the
corresponding <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@AutoValue</code> base class.</p>

<h2 id="private-member-classes">Private member classes</h2>

<p>The check ignores references that cross from a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code> inner class (or any
class inside it) to its immediately enclosing class, e.g.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">A</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">benignCycle</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="no">B</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">C</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">B</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">C</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="no">A</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>There is a cycle <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A</code> -&gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A.B.C</code> -&gt; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A</code>, but (without reflection) it’s not
possible to access <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A.B.C</code> in a way that causes initialization until after A is
initialized.</p>

<p>There are situations where deadlocks involving <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code> classes can still
occur, but the heuristic of ignoring paths cycles from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code> members is good
enough for most real-world examples of deadlocks that have been observed.</p>

<p>In the following, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">A.C</code> can trigger initialization of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">B</code>, despite <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">B</code> being
private.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">A</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">bad_cycle</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="no">B</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">B</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="no">A</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">C</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="no">B</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ClassInitializationDeadlock")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ClassNewInstance<br>
            <small>Class.newInstance() bypasses exception checking; prefer getDeclaredConstructor().newInstance()</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The documentation for <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html#newInstance"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class#newInstance</code></a> includes the following
warning:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>Note that this method propagates any exception thrown by the nullary
constructor, including a checked exception. Use of this method effectively
bypasses the compile-time exception checking that would otherwise be performed
by the compiler. The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Constructor.newInstance</code> method avoids this problem by
wrapping any exception thrown by the constructor in a (checked)
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InvocationTargetException</code>.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>Always prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myClass.getConstructor().newInstance()</code> to calling
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myClass.newInstance()</code> directly. The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class#newInstance</code> method is slated for
<a href="https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-6850612">deprecation in JDK 9</a>.</p>

<p>Note that migrating to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Class#getConstructor()</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Constructor#newInstance</code>
requires handling three new exceptions: <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IllegalArgumentException.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">IllegalArgumentException</code></a>,
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/NoSuchMethodException.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NoSuchMethodException</code></a>, and <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/reflect/InvocationTargetException.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InvocationTargetException</code></a>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ClassNewInstance")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>
