    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            EqualsGetClass<br>
            <small>Prefer instanceof to getClass when implementing Object#equals. Note that this may be a behaviour change.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Requiring the argument to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> to be of a specific concrete type is
incorrect, because it precludes any subtype of this class from obeying the
<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liskov_substitution_principle">substitution principle</a>.
Such code should be modified to use an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code> test instead of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass</code>.</p>

<h2 id="extending-a-value-class-to-add-attributes">Extending a value class to add attributes</h2>

<p>TL;DR: use composition rather than inheritance to add fields to value types.</p>

<p>The most common objection to this rule arises from a scenario like the
following:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>class Point {
  double x() {...}
  double y() {...}
}

class ColoredPoint {
  double x() {...}
  double y() {...}
  Color color() {...}
}
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>It’s reasonable to think first of modeling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint</code> as a subclass of
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code>. First, because on a conceptual level, there is a clear “is-a”
relationship between the two, which we have been taught to model as inheritance.
But also because of a few concrete advantages:</p>

<ol>
  <li>You get the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">y</code> fields/accessors for free.</li>
  <li>You get any other methods defined on <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code> for free.</li>
  <li>Users can pass a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint</code> to anything that expects a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code>. (This is
by far the primary advantage, since the first two are just one-time-only
implementation helpers for the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code> authors themselves.)</li>
</ol>

<p>Although these same advantages <em>can</em> be achieved via composition, it’s no longer
quite “for free”; the frequent need to call <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">myColoredPoint.asPoint()</code> is a pain
that feels unjustified, and thus subclassing is often chosen.</p>

<p>Unfortunately, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> now creates a big problem. Two <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Points</code> should be seen
as interchangeable whenever they have the same <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">y</code> coordinates. But two
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoints</code> are only equivalent if their coordinates <em>and</em> color are the
same. This, plus the general contract of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> (e.g. symmetry), ends up
forcing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point(1, 2)</code> to respond <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> if asked whether it is equal to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint(1, 2, BLUE)</code>.</p>

<p>This can be achieved by changing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> to be based on <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass</code> instead of
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">instanceof</code>. But do we even want to do that? Recall the main advantage we cited
for using subtyping: so that we “can pass <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint</code> to anything that
expects a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code>”, we said. Yet we are in fact <em>not</em> achieving that after all.
Put simply, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint</code> is incapable of functioning properly <em>as a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code></em>
because it cannot participate in equality checks with other <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code>s.</p>

<p>The composition approach may be annoying (the frequent need for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.asPoint()</code>),
but aside from that annoyance, it at least achieves the three advantages
correctly.</p>

<p>In summation, while it is true <em>conceptually</em> that a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint</code> “is-a”
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code>, a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ColoredPoint</code> is nevertheless unable to properly <em>function</em> as a
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code>, and modeling it with subtyping is not a good idea for that reason.</p>

<h2 id="what-about-final-or-effectively-final-classes">What about final or effectively-final classes?</h2>

<p>In this case there is no disadvantage to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass</code> trick - but there’s no
great advantage to it either. Most unsafe idioms have circumstances in which
they are safe, but this doesn’t change the fact that they are <em>generally</em> unsafe
and not worth propagating and legitimizing.</p>

<h2 id="more-information">More information</h2>

<p>See <a href="https://books.google.com/books?id=BIpDDwAAQBAJ">Effective Java 3rd Edition §10</a> (“Obey the general contract when
overriding equals”).</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsGetClass")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            EqualsIncompatibleType<br>
            <small>An equality test between objects with incompatible types always returns false</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Consider the following code:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"42"</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="nc">Integer</span> <span class="n">y</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">42</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">y</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"What is this, Javascript?"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">else</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Types have meaning here."</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>We understand that no <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer</code> will be equal to any <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code>. However, the
signature of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> method accepts any Object, so the compiler will
happily allow us to pass an Integer to the equals method. That method will
always return false, which is probably not what we intended.</p>

<p>This check detects circumstances where the equals method is called when the two
objects in question can <em>never</em> be equal to each other. We check the following
equality methods:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.lang.Object.equals(Object)</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Objects.equals(Object, Object)</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.common.base.Objects.equal(Object, Object)</code></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="im-trying-to-test-to-make-sure-my-equals-method-works">I’m trying to test to make sure my equals method works</h2>

<p>Good! Many tests of equals methods neglect to test that equals on an unrelated
object return false.</p>

<p>We recommend using Guava’s <a href="https://www.javadoc.io/doc/com.google.guava/guava-testlib/latest/com/google/common/testing/EqualsTester.html">EqualsTester</a> to perform tests of your
equals method. Simply give it a collection of objects of your class, broken into
groups that should be equal to each other, and EqualsTester will ensure that:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Each object is equal to each other object in the same group as that object</li>
  <li>Each object is equal to itself</li>
  <li>Each object is unequal to all of the other objects not in the group</li>
  <li>Each object is unequal to an unrelated object (Relevant to this check)</li>
  <li>Each object is unequal to null</li>
  <li>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> of each object in a group is the same as the hash code of
each other member of the group</li>
</ul>

<p>Which should exhaustively check all of the properties of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> and
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code>.</p>

<h2 id="but-im-doing-something-funky-with-my-equals-method">But I’m doing something funky with my equals method!</h2>

<p>The javadoc of <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Object.html#equals(java.lang.Object)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.equals(Object)</code></a> defines object equality very
precisely:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>The equals method implements an equivalence relation on non-null object
references:</p>

  <p>It is reflexive: for any non-null reference value x, x.equals(x) should return
true.</p>

  <p>It is symmetric: for any non-null reference values x and y, x.equals(y) should
return true if and only if y.equals(x) returns true.</p>

  <p>It is transitive: for any non-null reference values x, y, and z, if
x.equals(y) returns true and y.equals(z) returns true, then x.equals(z) should
return true.</p>

  <p>It is consistent: for any non-null reference values x and y, multiple
invocations of x.equals(y) consistently return true or consistently return
false, provided no information used in equals comparisons on the objects is
modified.</p>

  <p>For any non-null reference value x, x.equals(null) should return false.</p>
</blockquote>

<p>TIP: <a href="https://www.javadoc.io/doc/com.google.guava/guava-testlib/latest/com/google/common/testing/EqualsTester.html">EqualsTester</a> validates each of these properties.</p>

<p>For most simple value objects (e.g.: a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Point</code> containing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">y</code>
coordinates), this generally means that the equals method will only return true
if the other object has the exact same class, and each of the components is
equal to the corresponding component in the other object. Here, there are
numerous tools in the Java ecosystem to generate the appropriate <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> and
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> method implementations, including <a href="https://github.com/google/auto/blob/main/value/userguide/index.md">AutoValue</a>.</p>

<p>Another pattern often seen is to declare a common supertype with a defined
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> method (like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List</code>, which defines equality by having equal elements in
the same order). Then, different subclasses of that supertype (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> and
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayList</code>) can be equal to other classes with that supertype, since the
concrete class of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List</code> is irrelevant. This checker will allow these types
of equality, as we detect when two objects share a common supertype with an
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> implementation and allow that to succeed.</p>

<p>Outside of these two general groups of equals methods, however, it’s very
difficult to produce correctly-behaving equals methods. Most of the time, when
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> is implemented in a non-obvious manner, one or more of the properties
above isn’t satisfied (generally the symmetric property). This can result in
subtle bugs, explained below.</p>

<h3 id="a-bad-example-of-equals">A bad example of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals()</code></h3>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// Some property</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">other</span> <span class="k">instanceof</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// We want to be able to call equals with a String</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">other</span> <span class="k">instanceof</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="o">((</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Simplified, avoid null checks</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">hashCode</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hashCode</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Here, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code>’s equals method is defined to accept a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code> value in addition to
other <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Foo</code>’s. This may appear to work at first, but you end up with some
complex situations:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="n">a</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="n">b</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">hi</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">b</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"yes"</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Is printed, expected</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">b</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hi</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"yes"</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Is printed, abusing equals</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hi</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">b</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"no"</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Isn't printed, since String doesn't equals() Foo</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="nc">Set</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">set</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">HashSet</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&gt;();</span>
<span class="n">set</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="n">set</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">b</span><span class="o">);</span>

<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">set</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hi</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// Maybe? Depends on which way HashSet decides to call .equals()</span>
  <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"contained"</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="c1">// Is it removed? It's not guaranteed to be, since the .equals() method could</span>
  <span class="c1">// be called the other way in the remove path. Object.equals documentation</span>
  <span class="c1">// specifies it's supposed to be symmetric, so this could work.</span>
  <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="n">removed</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">set</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">hi</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsIncompatibleType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            EqualsUnsafeCast<br>
            <small>The contract of #equals states that it should return false for incompatible types, while this implementation may throw ClassCastException.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Implementations of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#equals</code> should return <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> for different types, not
throw.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Data</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="nd">@Override</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">Data</span> <span class="n">that</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Data</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="n">other</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// BAD: This may throw ClassCastException.</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">a</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">that</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">a</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsUnsafeCast")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            EqualsUsingHashCode<br>
            <small>Implementing #equals by just comparing hashCodes is fragile. Hashes collide frequently, and this will lead to false positives in #equals.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Don’t implement <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#equals</code> using just a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> comparison:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyClass</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">c</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="o">...</span>

  <span class="nd">@Override</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@Nullable</span> <span class="nc">Object</span> <span class="n">o</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">o</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hashCode</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">hashCode</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="nd">@Override</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">hashCode</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">Objects</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hashCode</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">c</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The number of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object</code>s with randomly distributed <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> required to give a
50% chance of collision (and therefore, with this pattern, erroneously correct
equality) is only ~77k.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("EqualsUsingHashCode")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ErroneousThreadPoolConstructorChecker<br>
            <small>Thread pool size will never go beyond corePoolSize if an unbounded queue is used</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Whenever a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ThreadPoolExecutor</code> is constructed with an unbounded <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">workQueue</code>,
the pool size will never go beyond <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">corePoolSize</code>. Using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">maximumPoolSize</code>
greater than <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">corePoolSize</code> in such case will not have any impact on the maximum
bound of pool size.</p>

<p>Bad:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ThreadPoolExecutor</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="cm">/* corePoolSize= */</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="cm">/* maximumPoolSize= */</span> <span class="mi">10</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="cm">/* keepAliveTime= */</span> <span class="mi">60</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="nc">TimeUnit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">SECONDS</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">LinkedBlockingQueue</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;());</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Good:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ThreadPoolExecutor</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="cm">/* corePoolSize= */</span> <span class="mi">10</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="cm">/* maximumPoolSize= */</span> <span class="mi">10</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="cm">/* keepAliveTime= */</span> <span class="mi">60</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="nc">TimeUnit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">SECONDS</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">LinkedBlockingQueue</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;());</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ThreadPoolExecutor</span><span class="o">(</span>
    <span class="cm">/* corePoolSize= */</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="cm">/* maximumPoolSize= */</span> <span class="mi">10</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="cm">/* keepAliveTime= */</span> <span class="mi">60</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="nc">TimeUnit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">SECONDS</span><span class="o">,</span>
    <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">LinkedBlockingQueue</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;(</span><span class="no">QUEUE_CAPACITY</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ErroneousThreadPoolConstructorChecker")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ExpensiveLenientFormatString<br>
            <small>String.format is passed to a lenient formatting method, which can be unwrapped to improve efficiency.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: PreconditionsExpensiveString</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Lenient format strings, such as those accepted by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Preconditions</code>, are often
constructed lazily. The message is rarely needed, so it should either be cheap
to construct or constructed only when needed. This check ensures that these
messages are not constructed using expensive methods that are evaluated eagerly.</p>

<p>Prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">checkNotNull</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"hello %s"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>instead of this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">checkNotNull</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">format</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello %s"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ExpensiveLenientFormatString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ExposedPrivateType<br>
            <small>Private member classes should not be referenced in signatures of non-private members.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Classes referenced in signatures of non-private APIs should usually also be
non-private.</p>

<p>For example, consider:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="n">record</span> <span class="nf">Person</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">printMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Person</span> <span class="n">person</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">printf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello %s\n"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">person</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">name</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Because <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Person</code> is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code>, clients outside the current compilation unit will
be unable to create an instance of it to pass to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">printMessage</code>.</p>

<p>Prefer to make classes referenced in APIs at least as visible as the API, or
else if the API is only intended to be used in the current compilation unit it
should also be <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">private</code>.</p>

<p>That is, prefer:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="n">record</span> <span class="nf">Person</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">printMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Person</span> <span class="n">person</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">printf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello %s\n"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">person</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">name</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="n">record</span> <span class="nf">Person</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">printMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Person</span> <span class="n">person</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">out</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">printf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello %s\n"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">person</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">name</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ExposedPrivateType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ExtendsObject<br>
            <small>`T extends Object` is redundant (unless you are using the Checker Framework).</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">T extends Object</code> is redundant; both <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;T&gt;</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;T extends Object&gt;</code> compile to
identical class files.— unless you are using the Checker Framework.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ExtendsObject")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            FallThrough<br>
            <small>Switch case may fall through</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: fallthrough</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <a href="https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html#s4.8.4.2-switch-fall-through">Google Java Style Guide §4.8.4.2</a> requires that within a switch
block, each statement group either terminates abruptly (with a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">break</code>,
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">continue</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">return</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">throw</code> statement), or is marked with a comment to
indicate that execution will or might continue into the next statement group.
This special comment is not required in the last statement group of the switch
block.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">switch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">input</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">:</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="o">:</span>
    <span class="n">prepareOneOrTwo</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="c1">// fall through</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="o">:</span>
    <span class="n">handleOneTwoOrThree</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="k">break</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="k">default</span><span class="o">:</span>
    <span class="n">handleLargeNumber</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">input</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FallThrough")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            Finalize<br>
            <small>Do not override finalize</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Do not override <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.finalize</code>.</p>

<p>Starting in JDK 18, the method is deprecated for removal, see
<a href="https://openjdk.org/jeps/421">JEP 421: Deprecate Finalization for Removal</a>.</p>

<p>The <a href="https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html#s6.4-finalizers">Google Java Style Guide §6.4</a> states:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>It is extremely rare to override <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.finalize</code>.</p>

  <p>Tip: Don’t do it. If you absolutely must, first read and understand
<a href="https://books.google.com/books?id=BIpDDwAAQBAJ">Effective Java Item 8</a>, “Avoid finalizers and cleaners” very
carefully, and then don’t do it.</p>
</blockquote>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation to the enclosing
element:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@SuppressWarnings</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Finalize"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="c1">// TODO(user): remove overrides of finalize</span>
</code></pre></div></div>


    </div>

          <h1>
            Finally<br>
            <small>If you return or throw from a finally, then values returned or thrown from the try-catch block will be ignored. Consider using try-with-resources instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: finally, ThrowFromFinallyBlock</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Terminating a finally block abruptly preempts the outcome of the try and catch
blocks, and will cause the result of any previously executed return or throw
statements to be ignored. Finally blocks should be written so they always
complete normally.</p>

<p>Consider the following code. In the case where <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">doWork</code> throws <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SomeException</code>,
the finally block will still be executed. If closing the input stream <em>also</em>
fails, then the exception that was thrown in the catch block will be preempted
by the exception thrown by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">close()</code>, and the first exception will be lost.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">InputStream</span> <span class="n">in</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">openInputStream</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">doWork</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">in</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">SomeException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">SomeError</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">in</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">close</span><span class="o">();</span> <span class="c1">// exception could be thrown here</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This code is easily fixed using try-with-resources. Below, the input stream will
always be closed, and if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">doWork</code> fails and an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">IOException</code> is thrown, then the
try-with-resources uses the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Throwable.addSuppressed()</code> method added in Java 7
to propagate both exceptions back to the caller.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">InputStream</span> <span class="n">in</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">openInputStream</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">doWork</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">in</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">SomeException</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">SomeError</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If Java 7 is not available, we recommend Guava’s
<a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/io/Closer.html">Closer API</a>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Closer</span> <span class="n">closer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Closer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">create</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">InputStream</span> <span class="n">in</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">closer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">register</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">openInputStream</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="n">doWork</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">in</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Throwable</span> <span class="n">e</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="n">closer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">rethrow</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">closer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">close</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("Finally")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            FloatCast<br>
            <small>Use parentheses to make the precedence explicit</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Casts have higher precedence than binary expressions, so <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">(int) 0.5f * 100</code> is
equivalent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">((int) 0.5f) * 100</code> = <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0 * 100</code> = <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0</code>, not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">(int) (0.5f * 100)</code> =
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">50</code>.</p>

<p>To avoid this common source of error, add explicit parentheses to make the
precedence explicit. For example, instead of this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">long</span> <span class="no">SIZE_IN_GB</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">long</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="mf">1.5</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1024</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1024</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1024</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// this is 1GB, not 1.5GB!</span>

<span class="c1">// this is 0, not a long in the range [0, 1000000000]</span>
<span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">rand</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">long</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Random</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">nextDouble</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1000000000</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prefer:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">long</span> <span class="no">SIZE_IN_GB</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">long</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">1.5</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1024</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1024</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1024</span><span class="o">);</span>

<span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">rand</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">long</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Random</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">nextDouble</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="mi">1000000000</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloatCast")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            FloatingPointAssertionWithinEpsilon<br>
            <small>This fuzzy equality check is using a tolerance less than the gap to the next number. You may want a less restrictive tolerance, or to assert equality.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Simplification</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Both JUnit and Truth allow for asserting equality of floating point numbers with
an absolute tolerance. For example, the following statements are equivalent,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">double</span> <span class="no">EPSILON</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">actualValue</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isWithin</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">EPSILON</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">PI</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="n">assertEquals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">PI</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">actualValue</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">EPSILON</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>What’s not immediately obvious is that both of these assertions are checking
exact equality between <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Math.PI</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">actualValue</code>, because the next <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">double</code>
after <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Math.PI</code> is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Math.PI + 4.44e-16</code>.</p>

<p>This means that using the same tolerance to compare several floating point
values with different magnitude can be prone to error,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">float</span> <span class="no">TOLERANCE</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="n">e</span><span class="o">-</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">pressure</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isWithin</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">TOLERANCE</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// GOOD</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">pressure</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isWithin</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">TOLERANCE</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// GOOD</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">pressure</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isWithin</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">TOLERANCE</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// BAD -- misleading equals check</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>A larger tolerance should be used if the goal of the test is to allow for some
floating point errors, or, if not, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isEqualTo</code> makes the intention more clear.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloatingPointAssertionWithinEpsilon")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            FloatingPointLiteralPrecision<br>
            <small>Floating point literal loses precision</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Style</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">double</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code> literals that can’t be precisely represented should be
avoided.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">double</span> <span class="n">d</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.9999999999999999999999999999999</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">err</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">d</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// prints 2.0</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloatingPointLiteralPrecision")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            FloggerArgumentToString<br>
            <small>Use Flogger's printf-style formatting instead of explicitly converting arguments to strings. Note that Flogger does more than just call toString; for instance, it formats arrays sensibly.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer to let Flogger transform your arguments to strings, instead of calling
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">toString()</code> explicitly.</p>

<p>For example, prefer the following:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">logger</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">atInfo</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello '%s'"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">world</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>instead of this, which eagerly calls <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">world.toString()</code> even if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">INFO</code> level
logging is disabled.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">logger</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">atInfo</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello '%s'"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">world</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">toString</span><span class="o">());</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloggerArgumentToString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            FloggerStringConcatenation<br>
            <small>Prefer string formatting using printf placeholders (e.g. %s) instead of string concatenation</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer string formatting to concatenating format arguments together, to avoid
work at the log site.</p>

<p>That is, prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">logger</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">atInfo</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"processing: %s"</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">request</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>to this, which calls <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">request.toString()</code> even if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">INFO</code> logging is disabled:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">logger</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">atInfo</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"processing: "</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">request</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>More information: https://google.github.io/flogger/formatting</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloggerStringConcatenation")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            FormatStringShouldUsePlaceholders<br>
            <small>Using a format string avoids string concatenation in the common case.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>It usually hurts performance to eagerly generate error messages with +, as you pay the cost of the string conversion whether or not the condition fails. It’s usually more efficient to use %s as a placeholder and to pass the additional variables as further arguments.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FormatStringShouldUsePlaceholders")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            FutureReturnValueIgnored<br>
            <small>Return value of methods returning Future must be checked. Ignoring returned Futures suppresses exceptions thrown from the code that completes the Future.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Methods that return <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.concurrent.Future</code> and its subclasses generally
indicate errors by returning a future that eventually fails.</p>

<p>If you don’t check the return value of these methods, you will never find out if
they threw an exception.</p>

<p>Nested futures can also result in missed cancellation signals or suppressed
exceptions - see
<a href="https://github.com/google/guava/wiki/ListenableFutureExplained#avoid-nested-futures">Avoiding Nested Futures</a>
for details.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>In certain scenarios like tests, there might be a need of not using the future
values. One can suppress such false positives by either suppressing the check
directly or by saving the future in variables named with prefix <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">unused</code>. For
example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@SuppressWarnings</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"FutureReturnValueIgnored"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">futureInvocation_noMemoryLeak</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">functionReturningFuture</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">futureInvocation_noMemoryLeak</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">Future</span><span class="o">&lt;?&gt;</span> <span class="n">unusedFuture</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">functionReturningFuture</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>


    </div>

          <h1>
            FutureTransformAsync<br>
            <small>Use transform instead of transformAsync when all returns are an immediate future.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The usage of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">transformAsync</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">callAsync</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">submitAsync</code> is not necessary
when all the return values of the transformation function are immediate futures.
In this case, the usage of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">transform</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">call</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">submit</code> is preferred.</p>

<p>Note that <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">transform</code> cannot be used if the body of the transformation function
throws checked exceptions.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FutureTransformAsync")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            GetClassOnEnum<br>
            <small>Calling getClass() on an enum may return a subclass of the enum type</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Enum values that declare methods are a subclass of the actual enum type, so
calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getClass()</code> returns a synthetic subclass of the enum. To retrieve the
type of the enum, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getDeclaringClass()</code>.</p>

<p>In the following example, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Binop.MULT.getClass()</code> returns the anonymous class
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Binop$2</code>, while <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Binop.MULT.getDeclaringClass()</code> returns the class <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Binop</code>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">enum</span> <span class="nc">Binop</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="no">MULT</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nd">@Override</span>
    <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">apply</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">},</span>
  <span class="no">ADD</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nd">@Override</span>
    <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">apply</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">};</span>

  <span class="kd">abstract</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="nf">apply</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Test</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">printEnumClass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Enum</span> <span class="n">theEnum</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">err</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">theEnum</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getClass</span><span class="o">());</span>
    <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">err</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">println</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">theEnum</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getDeclaringClass</span><span class="o">());</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">[]</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">printEnumClass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Binop</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">ADD</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prints:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>class Binop$2
class Binop
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("GetClassOnEnum")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            HidingField<br>
            <small>Hiding fields of superclasses may cause confusion and errors</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: hiding, OvershadowingSubclassFields</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>If a class has a field of the same name as any field visible to it on any of its
superclasses or superinterfaces, the subclass’ field is said to
“<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/java/IandI/hidevariables.html">hide</a>”
the superclass’ field.</p>

<p>When this circumstance occurs, users of the class declaring the hiding field
can’t interact with the fields from the superclass.</p>

<p>Let’s take a look at how field hiding might cause problems:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Super</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">"bar"</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Sub</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Super</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// the same name, so this hides `Super`'s `foo`</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Main</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">stringFn</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">s</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="cm">/*...*/</span> <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Looking at the API of `Super`, I should be able to access a string `foo`</span>
    <span class="c1">// on any object of type `Super` or its subclasses, right?</span>
    <span class="n">stringFn</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Sub</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">foo</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Oops! `foo` is not visible, and the wrong type!</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("HidingField")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            ICCProfileGetInstance<br>
            <small>This method searches the class path for the given file, prefer to read the file and call getInstance(byte[]) or getInstance(InputStream)</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Performance</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ICC_Profile.getInstance(String)</code> searches the entire classpath, which is often
unnecessary and can result in slow performance for applications with long
classpaths. Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getInstance(byte[])</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">getInstance(InputStream)</code> instead.</p>

<p>See also https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8191622.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ICCProfileGetInstance")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>
