        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Some JDK APIs are obsolete and have preferred alternatives.</p>

<h2 id="linkedlist"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code></h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> almost never out-performs <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayList</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayDeque</code><sup id="fnref:1" role="doc-noteref"><a href="#fn:1" class="footnote" rel="footnote">1</a></sup>. If you
are using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> as a list, prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayList</code>. If you are using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> as a stack or queue/deque, prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayDeque</code>.</p>

<p>Migration gotcha: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> permits <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code> elements; <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayDeque</code> rejects
them. The documentation for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deque</code> strongly discourages users from inserting
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">null</code>, even into implementations that permit it. So, if you are using a
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> for this purpose, you should likely stop, and you will <em>need</em> to
stop in order to migrate to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayDeque</code>.</p>

<h2 id="vector"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Vector</code></h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Vector</code> performs synchronization that is usually unnecessary; prefer
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayList</code>.</p>

<p>If a synchronized collection is necessary, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Collections.synchronizedList</code> or
a data structure from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.concurrent</code>.</p>

<h2 id="hashtable-and-dictionary"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Hashtable</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Dictionary</code></h2>

<p>This is a nonstandard class that predates the Java Collections Framework; prefer
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedHashMap</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">HashMap</code>.</p>

<p>If synchronization is necessary, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap</code> is
usually a good choice.</p>

<h2 id="javautilstack"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Stack</code></h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Stack</code> is a nonstandard class that predates the Java Collections Framework;
prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayDeque</code>.</p>

<p>If a synchronized collection is necessary, use a data structure from
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.concurrent</code>.</p>

<p>When migrating from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Stack</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deque</code>, note that the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Stack</code> methods
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">push</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">pop</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">peek</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">add</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">iterator</code> correspond to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Deque</code> methods
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">addFirst</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">removeFirst</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">peekFirst</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">addFirst</code>/<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">descendingIterator</code>.</p>

<h2 id="stringbuffer"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">StringBuffer</code></h2>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">StringBuffer</code> performs synchronization that is rarely necessary and has
significant performance overhead. Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">StringBuilder</code>, which does not do
synchronization.</p>

<p>If synchronization is necessary, consider creating an explicit lock object and
using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> blocks.</p>

<h2 id="enumeration"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Enumeration</code></h2>

<p>An ancient precursor to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterator</code>.</p>

<h2 id="sortedset-and-sortedmap"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SortedSet</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SortedMap</code></h2>

<p>Replaced by <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NavigableSet</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">NavigableMap</code> in Java 6.</p>

<h2 id="matcherhitend-and-matcherrequireend"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Matcher#hitEnd()</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Matcher#requireEnd()</code></h2>

<p>The methods [<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Matcher#hitEnd()</code>][hitEnd] and
[<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Matcher#requireEnd()</code>][requireEnd] are mainly intended for implementing
scanning functionalities (like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Scanner</code>), where you need to decide
whether to read more input from a stream to find a longer match.</p>

<p>If you are not implementing your own scanning or streaming parser, and the input
being matched against is already fully loaded in memory, using these methods is
likely a mistake.</p>

<h3 id="check-end-of-match">Check End of Match</h3>

<p>If you want to check if a match extends to the end of the input, you can simply
compare the match end index with the length of the input string:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// Instead of:</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">matcher</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">find</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">matcher</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hitEnd</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">...</span> <span class="o">}</span>

<span class="c1">// Use:</span>
<span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">matcher</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">find</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="n">matcher</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">end</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="n">input</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">length</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">...</span> <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h3 id="use-javautilscanner">Use java.util.Scanner</h3>

<p>If you are implementing a scanner or streaming parser, consider using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Scanner</code> directly, which already encapsulates this logic correctly.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Scanner</span> <span class="n">scanner</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Scanner</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">input</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="k">while</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">scanner</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hasNext</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">pattern</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">match</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">scanner</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">next</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">pattern</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JdkObsolete")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>
<div class="footnotes" role="doc-endnotes">
  <ol>
    <li id="fn:1" role="doc-endnote">
      <p>People generally choose <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> because they want fast insertion and
removal. However, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> has slow traversal, and typically you need
to traverse the list to find the place to insert/remove. It turns out that
the cost of traversing to a location in a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code> is approximately 4x
the cost of copying an element in an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ArrayList</code>. Thus, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code>’s
traversal cost dominates and results in poorer performance. More info:
https://stuartmarks.wordpress.com/2015/12/18/some-java-list-benchmarks/
[hitEnd]: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/regex/Matcher.html#hitEnd()
[requireEnd]: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/regex/Matcher.html#requireEnd() <a href="#fnref:1" class="reversefootnote" role="doc-backlink">&#8617;</a></p>
    </li>
  </ol>
</div>

          <h1>
            JodaDateTimeConstants<br>
            <small>Using the `_PER_` constants in `DateTimeConstants` is problematic because they encourage manual date/time math.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Manual date/time math leads to overflows, unit mismatches, and weak typing. Prefer to use strong types (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.time.Duration</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.time.Instant</code>) and their APIs to perform date/time math.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JodaDateTimeConstants")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            JodaDurationWithMillis<br>
            <small>Use of duration.withMillis(long) is not allowed. Please use Duration.millis(long) instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Joda-Time’s ‘duration.withMillis(long)’ method is often a source of bugs because it doesn’t mutate the current instance but rather returns a new immutable Duration instance. Please use Duration.millis(long) instead. If your Duration is better expressed in terms of other units, use standardSeconds(long), standardMinutes(long), standardHours(long), or standardDays(long) instead.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JodaDurationWithMillis")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            JodaInstantWithMillis<br>

          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">

*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Joda-Time’s ‘instant.withMillis(long)’ method is often a source of bugs because it doesn’t mutate the current instance but rather returns a new immutable Instant instance. Please use Instant.ofEpochMilli(long) instead.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JodaInstantWithMillis")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            JodaPlusMinusLong<br>
            <small>Use of JodaTime's type.plus(long) or type.minus(long) is not allowed (where <type> = {Duration,Instant,DateTime,DateMidnight}). Please use type.plus(Duration.millis(long)) or type.minus(Duration.millis(long)) instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>JodaTime’s type.plus(long) and type.minus(long) methods are often a source of bugs because the units of the parameters are ambiguous. Please use type.plus(Duration.millis(long)) or type.minus(Duration.millis(long)) instead.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("JodaPlusMinusLong")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ListRemoveAmbiguous<br>
            <small>Ambiguous call to List.remove; clarify if index-based or value-based removal was intended by adding a comment</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>There are two overloads of the method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List.remove</code>:
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/List.html#remove(int)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">remove(int index)</code></a> removes an element at the specified index, and
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/util/List.html#remove(java.lang.Object)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">remove(Object element)</code></a> removes the specified element. When used
with a list of integers (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List&lt;Integer&gt;</code>), the overload resolution can be
confusing and may lead to bugs if the wrong overload is selected or if the
code’s intent is not clear to readers.</p>

<p>Consider the following code:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">list</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>
<span class="c1">// ...</span>
<span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>In this case, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">list.remove(1)</code> calls <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">remove(int index)</code>, removing the element
at index 1. If the intention was to remove the element with value 1, this code
is incorrect.</p>

<p>To make the intent explicit and avoid ambiguity, add a comment before the
argument:</p>

<p>If you meant to remove by value (element):</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="cm">/* element */</span> <span class="n">ii</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you meant to remove by index:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="cm">/* index */</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you need to change the type to select the correct overload, you can use
explicit boxing/unboxing:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">valueOf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">));</span> <span class="c1">// remove by element</span>
<span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">ii</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">intValue</span><span class="o">());</span>      <span class="c1">// remove by index</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><a href="https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8384074">JDK-8384074</a> discusses adding a
new <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List::removeAtIndex</code> method to the JDK to avoid this potential overload
confusion.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ListRemoveAmbiguous")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            LiteEnumValueOf<br>
            <small>Instead of looking up a lite enum by name, use its numeric value since that is the stable part of the protocol defined by the enum.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Byte code optimizers can change the implementation of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">toString()</code> in lite
runtime and thus using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">valueOf(String)</code> is discouraged. Instead of converting
enums to string and back, its numeric value should be used instead as it is the
stable part of the protocol defined by the enum.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LiteEnumValueOf")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            LiteProtoToString<br>
            <small>toString() on lite protos will not generate a useful representation of the proto from optimized builds. Consider whether using some subset of fields instead would provide useful information.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>After bytecode optimization, Lite protos do not generate a meaningful
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#toString()</code>. This can be acceptable for debugging, as development builds will
typically not be optimized, but can pose a problem if the default lite
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#toString</code> finds its way into production code as part of an important error
message.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">validate</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProto</span> <span class="n">myProto</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="n">myProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hasFrobnicator</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="c1">// MyProto missing frobnicator: asf@6531767b</span>
      <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">IllegalArgumentException</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"MyProto missing frobnicator: "</span> <span class="o">+</span> <span class="n">myProto</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The fix will be highly dependent on the case at hand. There may be an identifier
associated with the message that would be useful to log, or even some serialized
version of the entire proto.</p>

<p>NOTE: Logging fields of a proto will force those fields to be retained after
optimization. This is not an issue if they’re already being used, but writing a
comprehensive <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#toString</code> method for a proto which is otherwise largely unused
would increase code size.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LiteProtoToString")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            LockNotBeforeTry<br>
            <small>Calls to Lock#lock should be immediately followed by a try block which releases the lock.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Wherever possible, calls to Lock#lock should be immediately followed by a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code>
block with a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">finally</code> clause which releases the lock,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">lock</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">frobnicate</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">unlock</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Placing the call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">lock</code> <em>inside</em> the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> block is suboptimal. The
documentation for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Lock</code> allows for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Lock#lock</code> to throw an unchecked exception
if, for example, it determines that the program will deadlock. In this
situation, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#unlock</code> will be called even if <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#lock</code> throws,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">lock</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">frobnicate</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">unlock</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Doing work between the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">lock</code> invocation and the start of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> block is
potentially very bad, as the lock will go unreleased if the intermediate work
throws,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">lock</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="n">checkState</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">frobnicator</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">ready</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">frobnicator</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">frobnicate</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">lock</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">unlock</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">frobnicator.ready()</code> should either be moved before the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#lock</code> call or inside
the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> block, depending on whether the lock must be acquired before calling
it.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LockNotBeforeTry")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            LockOnNonEnclosingClassLiteral<br>
            <small>Lock on the class other than the enclosing class of the code block can unintentionally prevent the locked class being used properly.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Having a lock on a class, other than the enclosing class of the code block, can
unintentionally prevent the locked class from being used properly when other
classes effectively lock on the same resource. From a maintainability
perspective, it can be time-consuming to ensure the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> blocks are
working as expected. Hence, locking on a class other than the enclosing class of
the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> code block is discouraged by Error Prone. Locking on the
enclosing class or an instance is a preferred practice.</p>

<p>For example, a lock on <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Other.class</code> rather than <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Example.class</code> will trigger an
Error Prone warning:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Example</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">method</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Other</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>A lock on the instance or the enclosing class of the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> code block
will not trigger the warning:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Example</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">method</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Example</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
    <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="k">this</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LockOnNonEnclosingClassLiteral")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            LogicalAssignment<br>
            <small>Assignment where a boolean expression was expected; use == if this assignment wasn't expected or add parentheses for clarity.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>LikelyError</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When an assignment expression is used as the condition of a loop, it isn’t clear
to the reader whether the assignment was deliberate or it was intended to be an
equality test. Parenthesis should be used around assignments in loop conditions
to make it clear to the reader that the assignment is deliberate.</p>

<p>That is, instead of this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">while</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">checkSomething</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// ...</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">while ((x = checkSomething())) {</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">while (x == checkSomething()) {</code>.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LogicalAssignment")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            LongDoubleConversion<br>
            <small>Conversion from long to double may lose precision; use an explicit cast to double if this was intentional</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A cast from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">long</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">double</code> may lose precision. Prefer an explicit cast to an
implicit conversion if this was intentional.</p>

<p>Consider
<a href="https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/java/com/google/protobuf/util/Values"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.protobuf.util.Values</code></a>
which has a method <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">of(double value)</code>, and the following example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// Values.of receives a long, which is implicitly converted to double:</span>
<span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">value</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">123L</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="nc">Values</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">value</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prefer this (to make existing behavior explicit):</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">value</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">123L</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="nc">Values</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">((</span><span class="kt">double</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="n">value</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>From <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se11/html/jls-5.html#jls-5.1.2">JLS §5.1.2</a>:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>A widening primitive conversion from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">int</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code>, or from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">long</code> to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code>, or from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">long</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">double</code>, may result in loss of precision - that
is, the result may lose some of the least significant bits of the value. In
this case, the resulting floating-point value will be a correctly rounded
version of the integer value, using IEEE 754 round-to-nearest mode</p>
</blockquote>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LongDoubleConversion")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            LongFloatConversion<br>
            <small>Conversion from long to float may lose precision; use an explicit cast to float if this was intentional</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A cast from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">long</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code> may lose precision. Prefer an explicit cast to an
implicit conversion if this was intentional.</p>

<p>Consider
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.desktop/java/awt/Color.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.awt.Color</code></a>
which has constructors <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Color(float r, float g, float b)</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Color(int r, int
g, int b)</code>, and the following example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// Math.round returns a double, which is implicitly converted to float:</span>
<span class="k">new</span> <span class="nf">Color</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Prefer this (to make existing behavior explicit):</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Color</span><span class="o">((</span><span class="kt">float</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">float</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">float</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or this (if this implicit conversion to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code> was unintentional):</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Color</span><span class="o">((</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">round</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>From <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se11/html/jls-5.html#jls-5.1.2">JLS §5.1.2</a>:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>A widening primitive conversion from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">int</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code>, or from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">long</code> to
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">float</code>, or from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">long</code> to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">double</code>, may result in loss of precision - that
is, the result may lose some of the least significant bits of the value. In
this case, the resulting floating-point value will be a correctly rounded
version of the integer value, using IEEE 754 round-to-nearest mode</p>
</blockquote>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LongFloatConversion")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            LoopOverCharArray<br>
            <small>toCharArray allocates a new array, using charAt is more efficient</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html#toCharArray\(\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String#toCharArray</code></a>
allocates a new array. Calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">charAt</code> is more efficient, because it avoids
creating a new array with a copy of the character data.</p>

<p>That is, prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">isDigits</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">for</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">i</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="n">i</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">length</span><span class="o">();</span> <span class="n">i</span><span class="o">++)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kt">char</span> <span class="n">c</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">charAt</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="nc">Character</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isDigit</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">c</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>to this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">isDigits</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// this allocates a new char[]</span>
  <span class="k">for</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">char</span> <span class="n">c</span> <span class="o">:</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">toCharArray</span><span class="o">())</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(!</span><span class="nc">Character</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isDigit</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">c</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Note that many loops over characters can be expressed using streams with
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html#chars()"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String#chars</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html#codePoints()"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String#codePoints</code></a>, for example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">isDigits</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">codePoints</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">allMatch</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nl">Character:</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="n">isDigit</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LoopOverCharArray")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            LoopToTestParameter<br>
            <small>Migrate loops in tests to use github.com/google/TestParameterInjector. Test parameterization executes each input case in strict isolation, ensuring that a single failure doesn't halt the rest of your test case while providing clear, per-case reporting without the need for manual loops.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>

<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("LoopToTestParameter")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            MathAbsoluteNegative<br>
            <small>Math.abs() does not always give a non-negative result. Please consider other methods for positive numbers, such as IntMath.saturatedAbs() or Math.floorMod().</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: MathAbsoluteRandom</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Math.html#abs-long-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Math.abs</code></a>
returns a negative number when called with the largest negative number.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">veryNegative</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">abs</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">MIN_VALUE</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">veryNegativeLong</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Math</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">abs</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">MIN_VALUE</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>When trying to generate positive random numbers or fingerprints by using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Math.abs</code> around a random positive-or-negative integer (or long), there will a
rare edge case where the returned value will be negative.</p>

<p>This is because there is no positive integer with the same magnitude as
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer.MIN_VALUE</code>, which is equal to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1</code>. Floating point
numbers don’t suffer from this problem, as the sign is stored in a separate bit.</p>

<p>Instead, one should use random number generation functions that are guaranteed
to generate positive numbers:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Random</span> <span class="n">r</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">Random</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">positiveNumber</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">nextInt</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">MAX_VALUE</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or map negative numbers onto the non-negative range:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">lng</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">nextLong</span><span class="o">();</span>

<span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">bestForHashCodes</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">lng</span> <span class="o">&amp;</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">MAX_VALUE</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">bestForMath</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">LongMath</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">saturatedAbs</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">lng</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MathAbsoluteNegative")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            MissingCasesInEnumSwitch<br>
            <small>Switches on enum types should either handle all values, or have a default case.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Consider a switch statement that doesn’t handle all possible values and doesn’t
have a default:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">enum</span> <span class="nc">Colors</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="no">RED</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">GREEN</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">BLUE</span> <span class="o">}</span>

<span class="k">switch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">RED:</span>
  <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">GREEN:</span>
    <span class="n">paint</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="k">break</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The author’s intent isn’t clear. There are three possibilities:</p>

<ol>
  <li>
    <p>The default case is known to be impossible. This could be made clear by
adding: <br />
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">default: throw new AssertionError(color);</code></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>The code intentionally ‘falls out’ of the switch on the default case, and
execution continues below. This could be made clear by adding: <br />
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">default: // fall out</code></p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>The code has a bug, and the missing cases should have been handled.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<p>To avoid this ambiguity, the Google Java Style Guide <a href="https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html#s4.8.4.3-switch-default">requires</a> each
switch statement on an enum type to either handle all values of the enum, or
have a default statement group.</p>

<h2 id="library-skew">Library skew</h2>

<p>If libraries are compiled against different versions of the same enum it’s
possible for the switch statement to encounter an enum value despite it
otherwise being thought to be exhaustive. If there is no default branch code
execution will simply fall out of the switch statement.</p>

<p>Since developers may have assumed this to be impossible, it may be helpful to
add a default branch when library skew is a concern, however, you may not want
to give up checking to ensure that all cases are handled. Therefore if a default
branch exists with a comment containing “skew”, the default will not be
considered for exhaustiveness. For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">enum</span> <span class="nc">TrafficLightColour</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="no">RED</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">GREEN</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="no">YELLOW</span> <span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">approachIntersection</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">TrafficLightColour</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">switch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">state</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">GREEN:</span>
      <span class="n">proceed</span><span class="o">();</span>
      <span class="k">break</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">YELLOW:</span>
    <span class="k">case</span> <span class="nl">RED:</span>
      <span class="n">stop</span><span class="o">();</span>
      <span class="k">break</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="k">default</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="c1">// In case of skew we may get an unknown value, always stop.</span>
      <span class="n">stop</span><span class="o">();</span>
      <span class="k">break</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>In this case the default branch is providing runtime safety for unknown enum
values while also still enforcing that all known enum values are handled.</p>

<p>Note: The <a href="/bugpattern/UnnecessaryDefaultInEnumSwitch.html">UnnecessaryDefaultInEnumSwitch</a>
check will not classify the default as unnecessary if it has the “skew” comment.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MissingCasesInEnumSwitch")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            MissingFail<br>
            <small>Not calling fail() when expecting an exception masks bugs</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<p><em>Alternate names: missing-fail</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When testing for exceptions in JUnit, it is easy to forget the call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code>:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">someOperationThatShouldThrow</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="c1">// forget to call Assert.fail()</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">SomeException</span> <span class="n">expected</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">expected</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Operation failed"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This is better:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">static</span> <span class="n">org</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">junit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Assert</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">fail</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">someOperationThatShouldThrow</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">fail</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">SomeException</span> <span class="n">expected</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">expected</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Operation failed"</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>But using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows</code> is preferable and the least error prone:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">static</span> <span class="n">org</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">junit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Assert</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">assertThrows</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="nc">SomeException</span> <span class="n">expected</span> <span class="o">=</span>
    <span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">SomeException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="n">someOperationThatShouldThrow</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">expected</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"Operation failed"</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Without the call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code>, the test is broken: it will pass if the exception
is never thrown <em>or</em> if the exception is thrown with the expected message.</p>

<p>If the try/catch block is defensive and the exception may not always be thrown,
then the exception should be named ‘tolerated’.</p>

<h2 id="detection">Detection</h2>

<p>This checker uses heuristics that identify as many occurrences of the problem as
possible while keeping the false positive rate low (low single-digit
percentages).</p>

<h2 id="heuristics">Heuristics</h2>

<p>Five methods were explored to detect missing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> calls, triggering if no
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail()</code> is used in a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try/catch</code> statement within a JUnit test class:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Cases in which the caught exception is called “expected”.</li>
  <li>Cases in which there is a call to an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code> method in the catch block.</li>
  <li>Cases in which “expected” shows up in a comment inside the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> block.</li>
  <li>Cases in which the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> block is empty.</li>
  <li>Cases in which the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> block contains only a single statement.</li>
</ul>

<p>Only the first three yield useful results and also required some more refinement
to reduce false positives. In addition, the checker does not trigger on comments
in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> block due to implementation complexity.</p>

<p>To reduce false positives, no match is found if any of the following is true:</p>

<ul>
  <li>Any method with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">fail</code> in its name is present in either catch or try block.</li>
  <li>A <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">throw</code> statement or synonym (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertTrue(false)</code>, etc.) is present in
either <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> block.</li>
  <li>The occurrence happens inside a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">setUp</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">tearDown</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Before</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@After</code>,
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">suite</code> or<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">main</code> method.</li>
  <li>The method returns from the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> block or immediately after.</li>
  <li>The exception caught is of type <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">InterruptedException</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AssertionError</code>,
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">junit.framework.AssertionFailedError</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Throwable</code>.</li>
  <li>The occurrence is inside a loop.</li>
  <li>The try block contains a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">while(true)</code> loop.</li>
  <li>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> block contains a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">continue;</code> statement.</li>
  <li>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try/catch</code> statement also contains a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">finally</code> statement.</li>
  <li>A logging call is present in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">catch</code> block.</li>
</ul>

<p>In addition, for occurrences which matched because they have a call to an
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code> method in the catch block, no match is found if any of the following
characteristics are present:</p>

<ul>
  <li>A field assignment in the catch block.</li>
  <li>A call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertTrue/False(boolean variable or field)</code> in the catch block.</li>
  <li>The last statement in the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">try</code> block is an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assert*()</code> (that is not a
noop): <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertFalse(false)</code>, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertTrue(true))</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Mockito.verify()</code> call.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MissingFail")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            MissingOverride<br>
            <small>method overrides method in supertype; expected @Override</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Style</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <a href="https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html#s6.1-override-annotation">Google Java Style Guide §6.1</a> requires that a method is marked with
the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Override</code> annotation whenever it is legal. This includes a class method
overriding a superclass method, a class method implementing an interface method,
and an interface method respecifying a superinterface method.</p>

<p>Exception: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Override</code> may be omitted when the parent method is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Deprecated</code>.
If the flag <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepOpt:MissingOverride:IgnoreInterfaceOverrides=true</code> is used,
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Override</code> can be omitted for an interface method respecifying a superinterface
method.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MissingOverride")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            MissingRefasterAnnotation<br>
            <small>The Refaster template contains a method without any Refaster annotations</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>LikelyError</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A Refaster template consists of multiple methods. Typically, each method in the
class has an annotation. If a method has no annotation, this is likely an
oversight.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MethodLacksBeforeTemplateAnnotation</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@BeforeTemplate</span>
  <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">before1</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">equals</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">""</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="c1">// @BeforeTemplate is missing</span>
  <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">before2</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">length</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">==</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="nd">@AfterTemplate</span>
  <span class="nd">@AlsoNegation</span>
  <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="nf">after</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isEmpty</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MissingRefasterAnnotation")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            MixedMutabilityReturnType<br>
            <small>This method returns both mutable and immutable collections or maps from different paths. This may be confusing for users of the method.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>It is dangerous for a method to return a mutable instance in some circumstances,
but immutable in others. Doing so may lead users of your API to make incorrect
assumptions about the mutability of the return type. For example, consider this
method:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">primeFactors</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">n</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">isPrime</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">))</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">Collections</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">singletonList</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">factors</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>
  <span class="k">for</span> <span class="o">(...)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">factors</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">factors</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If someone were to add another method to include the trivial factor <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">1</code>, a bug
will be introduced.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">primeFactorsAndOne</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">n</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">primeFactors</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">primeFactors</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">primeFactors</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">primeFactors</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">primeFactorsAndOne</code> will behave as intended for composite numbers, but throw an
exception for primes.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("MixedMutabilityReturnType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            ModifiedButNotUsed<br>
            <small>A collection or proto builder was created, but its values were never accessed.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Collections and proto builders which are created and mutated but never used may
be a sign of a bug, for example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nc">MyProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Builder</span> <span class="n">builder</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">MyProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">newBuilder</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="k">if</span> <span class="o">(</span><span class="n">field</span> <span class="o">!=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">MyProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">NestedField</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Builder</span> <span class="n">nestedBuilder</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">MyProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">NestedField</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">newBuilder</span><span class="o">();</span>
    <span class="n">nestedBuilder</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setValue</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">field</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="c1">// Oops--forgot to do anything with nestedBuilder.</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">builder</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">build</span><span class="o">();</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Likewise, converting a proto to a builder and modifying it is a no-op unless
something is done with the return value:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProto</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">toBuilder</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">build</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>As protos are immutable, either the return value must be used:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="nd">@CheckReturnValue</span>
  <span class="nc">MyProto</span> <span class="nf">withFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProto</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">proto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">toBuilder</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">build</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>or the Builder modified in place:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProto</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Builder</span> <span class="n">protoBuilder</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">protoBuilder</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">setFoo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ModifiedButNotUsed")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>
