    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            TruthIncompatibleType<br>
            <small>Argument is not compatible with the subject's type.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This assertion using Truth is guaranteed to be true or false based on the types
being passed to it. For example,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isNotEqualTo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Optional</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">2L</span><span class="o">));</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">xs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">of</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1L</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="mi">2L</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">doesNotContain</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>These will always be true, given <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Integer</code> is not comparable to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Long</code>. This
isn’t such a big issue for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isEqualTo</code> assertions, given the test will fail.
However, it can be insidious for <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">isNotEqualTo</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">doesNotContain</code>, given the
assertion will be vacuously true without providing any test coverage.</p>

<h2 id="testing-equals-methods">Testing equals methods</h2>

<p>One false positive for this is where the goal is to test the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code>
implementation of the type under test, i.e. that comparison to a different type
is <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> and does not throw:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">myCustomType</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">isNotEqualTo</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">""</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>For such cases, consider whether your type can be implemented using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AutoValue</code>
to remove the need to implement <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> by hand. If it can’t, consider
<a href="https://javadoc.io/doc/com.google.guava/guava-testlib/latest/com/google/common/testing/EqualsTester.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EqualsTester</code></a>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">EqualsTester</span><span class="o">()</span>
    <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addEqualityGroup</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyCustomType</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">create</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">),</span> <span class="nc">MyCustomType</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">create</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">))</span>
    <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">addEqualityGroup</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">""</span><span class="o">)</span>
    <span class="o">.</span><span class="na">testEquals</span><span class="o">();</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Although consider omitting an explicit comparison with a different type, as
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">EqualsTester</code> does this already by default.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TruthIncompatibleType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            TypeEquals<br>
            <small>TypeMirror should be compared using Types#isSameType, not equality operators or equals().</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.compiler/javax/lang/model/type/TypeMirror.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">TypeMirror</code></a>
doesn’t override <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.equals</code> and instances are not interned by javac, so
testing types for equality should be done with
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.compiler/javax/lang/model/util/Types.html#isSameType\(javax.lang.model.type.TypeMirror,javax.lang.model.type.TypeMirror\)"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Types#isSameType</code></a>
instead.</p>

<p>If you’re implementing an Error Prone <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">BugChecker</code>, you can get a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Types</code>
instance from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">VisitorState</code>.</p>

<p>If you’re implementing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">AnnotationProcessor</code>, you can get the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Types</code> instance
from <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">javax.annotation.processing.ProcessingEnvironment</code>.</p>

<p>For more discussion of preferred APIs for comparing types, see
https://errorprone.info/bugpattern/TypeToString</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TypeEquals")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            TypeNameShadowing<br>
            <small>Type parameter declaration shadows another named type</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Style</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When declaring type parameters, it’s possible to declare a type parameter with
the same name as another type in scope, “shadowing” that type and potentially
causing confusing or unintended behavior.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomething</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">object</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Here, object is the static class T in this file</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doSomethingElse</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">object</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Here, object is a generic T</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">T</span> <span class="o">{...}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This checker warns when a type parameter shadows another type and suggests a
possible renaming for the type parameter.</p>

<p>Note, however, that in some cases it may be preferable to rename or delete the
shadowed type rather than the type parameter shadowing it, such as in cases
where the type parameter is always instantiated with the same type.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TypeNameShadowing")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            TypeParameterShadowing<br>
            <small>Type parameter declaration overrides another type parameter already declared</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>Style</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When declaring type parameters, it’s possible to declare a type parameter with
the same name as another type parameter in scope causing unintended
incompatibilities when trying to use them together.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">instanceMethod</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">genericMethod</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="n">instanceMethod</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">t</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// FAIL: T declared in this method doesn't correspond to Foo&lt;T&gt;'s T</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>In some cases, the type variable being declared has no relation to the type
variable being shadowed. It may be appropriate to rename the shadowing type
variable:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Logger</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">log</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
  <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">logOther</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">...</span> <span class="o">}</span> <span class="c1">// Really should be &lt;O&gt; void logOther(O o), since this T is unrelated.</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Depending on the nature of the surrounding code, you might be able to remove the
generic declaration on a method, or convert the generic method into a static
method that doesn’t inherit the surrounding type parameter:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Holder</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">held</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">fooIt</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nf">fooify</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">held</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">fooify</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">t</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span> <span class="o">...</span> <span class="o">}</span> <span class="c1">// Could be static, or non-generic</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If an inner class declaration shadows a type variable, you may be able to remove
the type variable, make it a static inner class, or rename the type variable:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">BoxingBox</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// Works if you make the class static.</span>
  <span class="c1">// If you remove the type parameter, you'll need to update stuff to List&lt;Container&gt;</span>
  <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Container</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="no">T</span> <span class="n">held</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Container</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="no">T</span><span class="o">&gt;&gt;</span> <span class="n">stuff</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">ArrayList</span><span class="o">&lt;&gt;();</span>

  <span class="no">T</span> <span class="nf">get</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">index</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">stuff</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">get</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">index</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">held</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TypeParameterShadowing")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
</nav>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            TypeParameterUnusedInFormals<br>
            <small>Declaring a type parameter that is only used in the return type is a misuse of generics: operations on the type parameter are unchecked, it hides unsafe casts at invocations of the method, and it interacts badly with method overload resolution.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A method’s type parameters should always be referenced in the declaration of one
or more formal parameters. Type parameters that are only used in the return type
are a source of type-unsafety. First, operations on the type will be unchecked
after the type parameter is erased. For example:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>static &lt;T&gt; T doCast(Object o) {
  return (T) o; // this will always succeed, since T is erased
}
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The ‘doCast’ method would be better implemented as:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>static &lt;T&gt; T doCast(Class&lt;T&gt; clazz, Object o) {
  return clazz.cast(o); // has the expected behaviour
}
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Second, this pattern causes unsafe casts to occur at invocations of the method.
Consider the following snippet, which uses the first (incorrect) implementation
of ‘doCast’:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>this.&lt;String&gt;doCast(42); // succeeds
String s = doCast(42); // fails at runtime
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Finally, relying on the type parameter to be inferred can have surprising
results, and interacts badly with overloaded methods. Consider:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>&lt;T&gt; T getThing()
void assertThat(int a, int b)
void assertThat(Object a, Object b)
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This invocation will be ambiguous:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>// both method assertThat(int,int) and method assertThat(Object,Object) match
assertThat(42, getThing());
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("TypeParameterUnusedInFormals")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            URLEqualsHashCode<br>
            <small>Avoid hash-based containers of java.net.URL--the containers rely on equals() and hashCode(), which cause java.net.URL to make blocking internet connections.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hashCode</code> methods of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.net.URL</code> make blocking network
calls. When you place a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">URL</code> into a hash-based container, the container invokes
those methods.</p>

<p>Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.net.URI</code>. Or, if you must use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">URL</code> in a
collection, prefer to use a non-hash-based container like a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List&lt;URL&gt;</code>, and
avoid calling methods like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">contains</code> (which calls <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code>) on it.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("URLEqualsHashCode")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UndefinedEquals<br>
            <small>This type is not guaranteed to implement a useful equals() method.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>This code uses <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Object.equals</code> (or similar method) with a type that does not
have well-defined <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> behavior: <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Collection</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Iterable.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterable</code></a>, <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/Multimap.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Multimap</code></a>,
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Queue.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Queue</code></a>, or <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CharSequence</code></a>. Such a call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> may return <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">false</code> in
cases where equality was expected. <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/SparseArray"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SparseArray</code></a> and <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/LongSparseArray"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LongSparseArray</code></a> do
not implement <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code>, so will fall back to reference equality.</p>

<h2 id="for-collection-or-iterable">For <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Collection</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Iterable.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterable</code></a></h2>

<p>Your code might be working correctly, but only if there is some <em>subtype</em> of
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterable</code> which <em>does</em> have well-defined equals behavior, and you are certain
that both operands are definitely of that type at runtime. (The common examples
of such types are [<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List</code>], [<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Set</code>], and <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/Multiset.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Multiset</code></a>, or any subtypes of
those.)</p>

<p>If this describes your situation, congratulations: you don’t have a bug. To make
this warning go away, change the references in your code to be of that more
specific static type, not <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Collection</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Iterable.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterable</code></a>. This lets the bug
checker (and human readers) <em>know</em> that there is no risk of a false negative.</p>

<p>The minimal solution is to cast or copy “just in time” before calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code>,
but ideally you can make broader changes, to adopt the proper interface more
widely in your code.</p>

<p>On the other hand, if you might be mixing a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List</code> and a non-<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List</code>, etc., you
are at risk. If you can’t correct that situation, one alternative solution is to
use <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/Iterables.html#elementsEqual-java.lang.Iterable-java.lang.Iterable-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterables.elementsEqual</code></a> (which checks for <em>order-dependent</em> equality,
like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">List.equals</code>).</p>

<h2 id="for-multimap">For <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/Multimap.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Multimap</code></a></h2>

<p>The discussion above generally applies in this case as well; the well-behaved
subtypes to choose from are <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/ListMultimap.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ListMultimap</code></a> and <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/SetMultimap.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SetMultimap</code></a>.</p>

<p>There is no equivalent to <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/Iterables.html#elementsEqual-java.lang.Iterable-java.lang.Iterable-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Iterables.elementsEqual</code></a> in this case, however.</p>

<h2 id="for-queue">For <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Queue.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Queue</code></a></h2>

<p>All known <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Queue</code> implementations besides <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/LinkedList.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LinkedList</code></a> use reference equality
instead of value-based equality. <em>Some</em> of the workarounds discussed above may
apply.</p>

<h2 id="for-charsequence">For <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CharSequence</code></a></h2>

<p>When comparing a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code> to a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CharSequence</code>, prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String#contentEquals</code>.
When comparing the content of two <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">CharSequence</code>s, you may want to compare the
string representation: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">lhs.toString().contentEquals(rhs)</code>.</p>

<h2 id="for-sparsearray-and-longsparsearray">For <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/SparseArray"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">SparseArray</code></a> and <a href="https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/LongSparseArray"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">LongSparseArray</code></a></h2>

<p>These must be iterated over and compared manually, element by element.</p>

<h2 id="for-javautildate">For <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Date</code></a></h2>

<p>Subtypes of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Date</code> (like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.sql.Timestamp</code>) break substitutability, so
comparing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Date</code>s with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code> is unreliable.</p>

<p>TIP: <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.Date</code> is a legacy, bug-prone API. Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.time.Instant</code> or
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.time.LocalDateTime</code>.</p>

<h2 id="for-immutablecollection">For <a href="https://guava.dev/releases/snapshot-jre/api/docs/com/google/common/collect/ImmutableCollection.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableCollection</code></a></h2>

<p>Prefer subtypes such as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableSet</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ImmutableList</code>, which have
well-defined <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">equals</code>.</p>

<h2 id="for-future">For <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/Future.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Future</code></a></h2>

<p>Prefer calling <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#get</code> and checking the result, or using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat(...).isSameInstanceAs()</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThat(...).isNotSameInstanceAs()</code>
for cases where the same/different instance is expected.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UndefinedEquals")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UnicodeEscape<br>
            <small>Using unicode escape sequences for printable ASCII characters is obfuscated, and potentially dangerous.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using unicode escapes in Java for printable characters is obfuscated. Worse,
given the compiler allows unicode literals outside of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">String</code> literals, it can
be potentially unsafe.</p>

<p>Prefer using literal characters for printable characters.</p>

<p>For an example of malicious code, consider:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Evil</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">...</span> <span class="n">args</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// Don't run this, it would be really unsafe!</span>
    <span class="c1">// \u000d Runtime.exec("rm -rf /");</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\u000d</code> encodes a newline character, so <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Runtime.exec</code> appears on its own line
and will execute.</p>

<p>NOTE: Unicode escapes are defined as a preprocessing step in the Java compiler
(see <a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se11/html/jls-3.html#jls-3.3">JLS §3.3</a>). After compilation, there is no runtime difference whatsoever
between a Unicode escape and using the equivalent character in source. That is,
writing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">"hello \u0077\u006f\u0072\u006c\u0064"</code> is equivalent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">"hello
world"</code> in the compiled <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.class</code> file and at runtime.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnicodeEscape")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            UnnamedVariable<br>
            <small>Consider renaming unused variables and lambda parameters to `_`</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer using an unnamed variable (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">_</code>) to denote variables and patterns that are
intentionally unused.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnamedVariable")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            UnnecessaryAssignment<br>
            <small>Fields annotated with @Inject/@Mock/@TestParameter should not be manually assigned to, as they should be initialized by a framework. Remove the assignment if a framework is being used, or the annotation if one isn't.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Mock</code> annotation is used to automatically initialize mocks using
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MockitoAnnotations.initMocks</code>, or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">MockitoJUnitRunner</code>.</p>

<p>Variables annotated this way should not be explicitly initialized, as this will
be overwritten by automatic initialization.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryAssignment")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

          <h1>
            UnnecessaryBreakInSwitch<br>
            <small>This break is unnecessary, fallthrough does not occur in -> switches</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The newer arrow (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-&gt;</code>) syntax for switches does not permit fallthrough between
cases. A <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">break</code> statement is allowed to break out of the switch, but including
a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">break</code> as the last statement in a case body is unnecessary.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryBreakInSwitch")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UnnecessaryCopy<br>
            <small>This collection is already immutable (just not ImmutableList/ImmutableMap); copying it is unnecessary.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The collections returned by the protobuf API are unmodifiable: attempts to
modify them will result in an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">UnsupportedOperationException</code>.</p>

<p>The protobuf collections are not implemented using Guava’s immutable
collections, so copying them as a Guava collection isn’t free.</p>

<p>This check suggests omitting copies of unmodifiable protobuf collections as
Guava immutable collections in places where a Guava immutable collection is not
required, for example to replace this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">foos</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProtoMessage</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">copyOf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">message</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getFoos</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>with this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">List</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">foos</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProtoMessage</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getFoos</span><span class="o">();</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Note that the check will not report diagnostics if the result of the copy is
being used somewhere that requires a Guava Immutable collection, for example it
is returned from the current method, or passed to an API that expects a Guava
immutable collection:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">foos</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">MyProtoMessage</span> <span class="n">message</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">ImmutableList</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">copyOf</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">message</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getFoos</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The check will suggest refactoring local variables, if the local variable is
never used in a context that requires a Guava immutable collection. Using
Guava’s collections has some benefit in this case, since it makes the
immutability of the collection clear and can enable other compile-time static
analysis for accidental attempts to modify the collection. But this value is
limited if it is only used as a local variable that never escapes the current
method, and there is some runtime cost from making the copy.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryCopy")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UnnecessaryLambda<br>
            <small>Returning a lambda from a helper method or saving it in a constant is unnecessary; prefer to implement the functional interface method directly and use a method reference instead.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer method references to constant lambda expressions, or to a helper method
that does nothing but return a lambda.</p>

<p>That is, prefer this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span> <span class="nf">getBar</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Foo</span> <span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nc">BarService</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">lookupBar</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">defaultCredentials</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="o">...</span>

<span class="k">return</span> <span class="nf">someStream</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">map</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nl">MyClass:</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="n">getBar</span><span class="o">)....;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>to this:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">Function</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Bar</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="no">GET_BAR_FUNCTION</span> <span class="o">=</span>
    <span class="n">foo</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">BarService</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">lookupBar</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">foo</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="n">defaultCredentials</span><span class="o">());</span>

<span class="o">...</span>

<span class="k">return</span> <span class="nf">someStream</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">map</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="no">GET_BAR_FUNCTION</span><span class="o">)....;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Advantages of using a method include:</p>

<ul>
  <li>It avoids hardcoding a named dependency on the functional interface type
(e.g., is it a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">com.google.common.base.Function</code> or a
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">java.util.function.Function</code>?)</li>
  <li>It is easier to name the method than the constant.</li>
  <li>It is more natural to test the method than the constant.</li>
  <li>If the behavior is nontrivial, it’s more natural to write javadoc for the
method.</li>
</ul>

<p>Be aware that this change is not purely syntactic: it affects the semantics of
your program in some small ways. In particular, evaluating the same method
reference twice is not guaranteed to return an identical object.</p>

<p>This means that, first, inlining the reference instead of storing a lambda may
cause additional memory allocations - usually this very slight performance cost
is worth the improved readability, but use your judgment if the performance
matters to you.</p>

<p>Secondly, if the correctness of your program depends on reference equality of
your lambda, inlining it may break you. Ideally, you should <em>not</em> depend on
reference equality for a lambda, but if you are doing so, consider not making
this change.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryLambda")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            UnnecessaryMethodReference<br>
            <small>This method reference is unnecessary, and can be replaced with the variable itself.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Using a method reference to refer to the abstract method of the target type is
unnecessary. For example,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Stream</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">filter</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Stream</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Predicate</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">predicate</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">filter</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nl">predicate:</span><span class="o">:</span><span class="n">test</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Stream</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="nf">filter</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Stream</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Predicate</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">predicate</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">xs</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">filter</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">predicate</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryMethodReference")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UnnecessaryQualifier<br>
            <small>A qualifier annotation has no effect here.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Qualifier</code> or a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@BindingAnnotation</code> has no effect here, and can be removed.
Its presence may be misleading.</p>

<p>For example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">final</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyInjectableClass</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@Username</span> <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">username</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="nd">@Inject</span>
  <span class="nc">MyInjectableClass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@Username</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">username</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">this</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">username</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">username</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>The annotation on the constructor parameter is important, but the field
annotation is redundant.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">final</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyInjectableClass</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">username</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="nd">@Inject</span>
  <span class="nc">MyInjectableClass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nd">@Username</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">username</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">this</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">username</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">username</span><span class="o">;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>There are a couple of ways this check can lead to false positives:</p>

<ul>
  <li>
    <p>You’re using a custom framework we don’t know about which makes the location
of the finding an injection point. File a bug, and we’ll happily incorporate
it.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <p>Your annotation is annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Qualifier</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@BindingAnnotation</code> but
isn’t actually used as a qualifier (perhaps you have a framework that just
uses it reflectively). Try removing those annotations from the <em>annotation</em>.</p>
  </li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnnecessaryQualifier")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

          <h1>
            UnsafeFinalization<br>
            <small>Finalizer may run before native code finishes execution</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When invoking <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static native</code> methods from objects that override
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/9/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html#finalize--"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">finalize</code></a>,
the finalizer may run before the native method finishes execution.</p>

<p>Consider the following example:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">GameRunner</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// Pointer to some native resource, stored as a long</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="c1">// Allocates the native resource that this object "owns"</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">native</span> <span class="kt">long</span> <span class="nf">doNativeInit</span><span class="o">();</span>

  <span class="c1">// Releases the native resource</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">native</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">cleanUpNativeResources</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span><span class="o">);</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nf">GameRunner</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">doNativeInit</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="nd">@Override</span>
  <span class="kd">protected</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">finalize</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">cleanUpNativeResources</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span>
    <span class="kd">super</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">finalize</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">run</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="nc">GameLibrary</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">playGame</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// Bug!</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>

<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">GameLibrary</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="c1">// Plays the game using the native resource</span>
  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kd">native</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">playGame</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kt">long</span> <span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>During the execution of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">GameRunner.run</code>, the call to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">playGame</code> may not hold
the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">this</code> reference live, and its finalizer may run, cleaning up the native
resources while the native code is still executing.</p>

<p>You can fix this by making the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static native</code> method not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static</code>, or by
changing the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">static native</code> method so that it is passed the enclosing instance
and not the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">nativeResourcePtr</code> value directly.</p>

<p>If you can use Java 9, the new method
<a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/9/docs/api/java/lang/ref/Reference.html#reachabilityFence-java.lang.Object-"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Reference.reachabilityFence</code></a>
will keep the reference passed in live. Be sure to call it in a finally block:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code> <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">run</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="k">try</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="n">playAwesomeGame</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">nativeResourcePtr</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">}</span> <span class="k">finally</span> <span class="o">{</span>
      <span class="nc">Reference</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">reachabilityFence</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="k">this</span><span class="o">);</span>
    <span class="o">}</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Note: This check doesn’t currently detect this problem when passing fields from
objects other than “this”. That is equally unsafe. Consider passing the Java
object instead.</p>

<h2 id="references">References</h2>

<ul>
  <li><a href="https://www.hpl.hp.com/techreports/2002/HPL-2002-335.html">Boehm, “Destructors, finalizers, and synchronization.” POPL 2003.</a>
Section 3.4 discusses this problem.</li>
  <li><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se9/html/jls-12.html#jls-12.6.2">Java Language Specification 12.6.2, “Interaction with the Memory Model.”</a></li>
</ul>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnsafeFinalization")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UnsafeReflectiveConstructionCast<br>
            <small>Prefer `asSubclass` instead of casting the result of `newInstance`, to detect classes of incorrect type before invoking their constructors. This way, if the class is of the incorrect type, it will throw an exception before invoking its constructor.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Prefer <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">asSubclass</code> instead of casting the result of <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">newInstance</code> to detect
classes of incorrect type before invoking their constructors. This way, if the
class is of the incorrect type, it will throw an exception before invoking its
constructor.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="nc">Class</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">forName</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">someString</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">getDeclaredConstructor</span><span class="o">(...).</span><span class="na">newInstance</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">args</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Should be written as</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nc">Class</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">forName</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">someString</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">asSubclass</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Foo</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">getDeclaredConstructor</span><span class="o">(...).</span><span class="na">newInstance</span><span class="o">();</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This has caused issues in the past:</p>

<p>CVE-2014-7911 - https://seclists.org/fulldisclosure/2014/Nov/51</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnsafeReflectiveConstructionCast")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    <div class="container">
      <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized<br>
            <small>Unsynchronized method overrides a synchronized method.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            <dt>Tags</dt><dd>FragileCode</dd>
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Thread-safe methods should never be overridden by methods that are not
thread-safe. Doing so violates behavioural subtyping, and can result in bugs if
the subtype is used in contexts that rely on the thread-safety of the supertype.</p>

<p>Overriding a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> method with a method that is not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> can
be a sign that the thread-safety of the supertype is not being preserved.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Counter</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">count</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">synchronized</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">increment</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">count</span><span class="o">++;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="c1">// MyCounter is not thread safe!</span>
<span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyCounter</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Counter</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">count</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">increment</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">count</span><span class="o">++;</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Note that there are many ways to implement a thread-safe method without using
the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> modifier (e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> statements using explicit
locks, or other locking constructs). When overriding a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> method
with a method that is thread-safe but does not have the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">synchronized</code> modifier,
consider adding <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized")</code> and
an explanation.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyCounter</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">Counter</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="nc">AtomicInteger</span> <span class="n">count</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">AtomicInteger</span><span class="o">();</span>

  <span class="nd">@SuppressWarnings</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized"</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="c1">// AtomicInteger is thread-safe</span>
  <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">increment</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="n">count</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getAndIncrement</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

<p><em>Alternate names: Unused, unused, UnusedParameters</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The presence of an unused method may indicate a bug. This check highlights
<em>private</em> methods which are unused and can be safely removed without considering
the impact on other source files.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>Methods and fields which are used by reflection can be annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Keep</code> to
suppress the warning.</p>

<p>This annotation can also be applied to annotations, to suppress the warning for
any member annotated with that annotation:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">com.google.errorprone.annotations.Keep</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="nd">@Keep</span>
<span class="nd">@Retention</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">RetentionPolicy</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">RUNTIME</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nd">@interface</span> <span class="nc">Field</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

<span class="o">...</span>

<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Data</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@Field</span> <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// no warning.</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>All false positives can be suppressed by annotating the method with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("unused")</code> or prefixing its name with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">unused</code>.</p>

<p><em>Alternate names: unused, UnusedParameters</em></p>

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>The presence of an unused variable may indicate a bug. This check highlights
private fields, and parameters of private methods, which are unused and can be
safely removed without considering the impact on other source files. “Private”
in this context also includes effectively-private members, like public members
of private classes.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>

<p>False positives on fields and parameters can be suppressed by prefixing the
variable name with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">unused</code>, e.g.:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">authenticate</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">User</span> <span class="n">user</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Application</span> <span class="n">unusedApplication</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="n">checkState</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">user</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">isAuthenticated</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Fields which are used by reflection can be annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Keep</code> to suppress
the warning.</p>

<p>This annotation can also be applied to annotations, to suppress the warning for
any member annotated with that annotation:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">com.google.errorprone.annotations.Keep</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="nd">@Keep</span>
<span class="nd">@Retention</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">RetentionPolicy</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">RUNTIME</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nd">@interface</span> <span class="nc">Field</span> <span class="o">{}</span>

<span class="o">...</span>

<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">Data</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nd">@Field</span> <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kt">int</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="o">;</span> <span class="c1">// no warning.</span>
  <span class="o">...</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>All false positives can be suppressed by annotating the variable with
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("unused")</code>.</p>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            UseBinds<br>
            <small>@Binds is a more efficient and declarative mechanism for delegating a binding.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>A @Provides or @Produces method that returns its single parameter has long been
Dagger’s only mechanism for delegating a binding. Since the delegation is
implemented via a user-defined method there is a disproportionate amount of
overhead for such a conceptually simple operation. @Binds was introduced to
provide a declarative way of delegating from one binding to another in a way
that allows for minimal overhead in the implementation. @Binds should always be
preferred over @Provides or @Produces for delegation.</p>

<p>For instance, the following <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Provides</code> method</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Provides</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">Heater</span> <span class="nf">provideHeater</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">ElectricHeater</span> <span class="n">heater</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="n">heater</span><span class="o">;</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>is equivalent to the following preferred <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Binds</code> method.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Binds</span> <span class="kd">abstract</span> <span class="nc">Heater</span> <span class="nf">bindHeater</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">ElectricHeater</span> <span class="n">impl</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("UseBinds")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            VariableNameSameAsType<br>
            <small>variableName and type with the same name would refer to the static field instead of the class</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>When a field/variable name is the same as the field/variable type, it is
difficult to determine which to use at which time.</p>

<p>For example,</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>This would cause future use of String.something within this class to refer to
the static field String, instead of the class String.</p>

<p>This is worth calling out to avoid confusion and is a violation of
<a href="https://google.github.io/styleguide/javaguide.html#s5.2.7-local-variable-names">Google Java style naming conventions</a></p>

<p>Instead of this naming style, the correct way would be:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">static</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="n">string</span><span class="o">;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("VariableNameSameAsType")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="chrome=1">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>WaitNotInLoop</title>
  <link href="/stylesheets/bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
  <link href="/stylesheets/styles.css" rel="stylesheet">
  <link href="/stylesheets/syntax.css" rel="stylesheet">

  <body>
    <nav id="common-nav" class="navbar navbar-inverse navbar-fixed-top">

    <button type="button" class="navbar-toggle collapsed" data-toggle="collapse" data-target="#bs-example-navbar-collapse-1">

  <div class="collapse navbar-collapse" id="bs-example-navbar-collapse-1">
