          <h1>
            ExpectedExceptionChecker<br>
            <small>Prefer assertThrows to ExpectedException</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Any additional statements after the statement that is expected to throw will
never be executed in a passing test. This can lead to inappropriately passing
tests where later incorrect assertions are skipped by the thrown exception. For
instance, the final assertion in the following example will never be executed if
the call throws as expected.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">testRemoveFails</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span> <span class="n">list</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">thrown</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">expect</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">UnsupportedOperationException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">thrown</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">expectMessage</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// throws</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasSize</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span> <span class="c1">// never executed</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To avoid this issue, prefer JUnit’s <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">assertThrows()</code> API:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">static</span> <span class="n">org</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">junit</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">Assert</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">assertThrows</span><span class="o">;</span>

<span class="nd">@Test</span>
<span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">testRemoveFails</span><span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">{</span>
  <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span> <span class="n">list</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nc">AppendOnlyList</span><span class="o">();</span>
  <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">add</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="s">"a"</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="nc">UnsupportedOperationException</span> <span class="n">thrown</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">assertThrows</span><span class="o">(</span>
      <span class="nc">UnsupportedOperationException</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">class</span><span class="o">,</span>
      <span class="o">()</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="o">{</span>
        <span class="n">list</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">remove</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="o">);</span>
      <span class="o">});</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">thrown</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasMessageThat</span><span class="o">().</span><span class="na">contains</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"hello"</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="n">assertThat</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">list</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">hasSize</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("ExpectedExceptionChecker")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

            FloggerMessageFormat<br>
            <small>Invalid message format-style format specifier ({0}), expected printf-style (%s)</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Flogger uses printf-style format specifiers, such as %s and %d. Message format-style specifiers like {0} don’t work.</p>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloggerMessageFormat")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

-->

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FloggerRedundantIsEnabled")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-10">
          <h1>
            FunctionalInterfaceClash<br>
            <small>Overloads will be ambiguous when passing lambda arguments.</small>
          </h1>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-1 col-md-2">
          <dl>
            <dt>Severity</dt><dd>WARNING</dd>
            
          </dl>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!--
*** AUTO-GENERATED, DO NOT MODIFY ***
To make changes, edit the @BugPattern annotation or the explanation in docs/bugpattern.
-->

<h2 id="the-problem">The problem</h2>
<p>Passing lambdas to an overloaded method may be ambiguous if two overloads have
parameters that are functional interfaces with equivalent methods.</p>

<p>Prefer to avoid ambiguous overloads, and consider renaming one of the methods.</p>

<p>For example <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Function&lt;String, Integer&gt;</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">IntFunction&lt;String&gt;</code> are both
compatible with the lambda <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">x -&gt; x.hashCode()</code>.</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Function</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">f</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">IntFunction</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>error: reference to f is ambiguous
    f(x -&gt; x.hashCode());
    ^
  both method f(Function&lt;String,Integer&gt;) in Test and method f(IntFunction&lt;String&gt;) in Test match
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>To avoid the ambiguity, callers will have to use an explicit cast:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">f</span><span class="o">((</span><span class="nc">IntFunction</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;)</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hashCode</span><span class="o">());</span>
<span class="n">f</span><span class="o">((</span><span class="nc">Function</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">Integer</span><span class="o">&gt;)</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="n">x</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">hashCode</span><span class="o">());</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="expression-bodied-lambdas">Expression-bodied lambdas</h2>

<p>The situation is more complicated with expression-bodied lambdas. Consider:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doIt</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Function</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">f</span><span class="o">);</span>
<span class="kt">void</span> <span class="nf">doIt</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">Consumer</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">&gt;</span> <span class="n">c</span><span class="o">);</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><a href="https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.12.2.1">JLS 15.12.2.1</a>
says that lambdas whose body is a statement expression are compatible with
functional interfaces whose function type is void-returning <em>or</em> value
returning:</p>

<blockquote>
  <p>A lambda expression (§15.27) is potentially compatible with a functional
interface type (§9.8) if all of the following are true:</p>

  <ul>
    <li>
      <p>The arity of the target type’s function type is the same as the arity of
the lambda expression.</p>
    </li>
    <li>
      <p>If the target type’s function type has a void return, then the lambda body
is either a statement expression (§14.8) or a void-compatible block
(§15.27.2).</p>
    </li>
    <li>
      <p>If the target type’s function type has a (non-void) return type, then the
lambda body is either an expression or a value-compatible block
(§15.27.2).</p>
    </li>
  </ul>
</blockquote>

<p>So, if you have:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="n">doIt</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">System</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">gc</span><span class="o">());</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>it’s an implicitly typed statement-expression-bodied lambda that’s compatible
with both overloads.</p>

<p>Any of the following disambiguate the overloads:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>doIt((String x) -&gt; x.toString()); // explicitly typed, calls f(Function)
doIt(x -&gt; (x.toString())); // non-statement expression body, calls f(Function)
doIt(x -&gt; {x.toString();}); // statement body, calls f(Consumer)
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="suppression">Suppression</h2>
<p>Suppress false positives by adding the suppression annotation <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@SuppressWarnings("FunctionalInterfaceClash")</code> to the enclosing element.</p>

    </div>

        <div class="col-lg-10 col-md-9 col-sm-9">
          <h1>Command-line flags</h1>
          <h3 id="severity">Severity</h3>

<p>Error Prone lets the user enable and disable specific checks as well as override
their built-in severity levels (warning vs. error) by passing options to the
Error Prone compiler invocation.</p>

<p>A valid Error Prone command-line option looks like:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">-Xep</span>:&lt;checkName&gt;[:severity]
</code></pre></div></div>

<p><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">checkName</code> is required and is the canonical name of the check, e.g.
“ReferenceEquality”. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">severity</code> is one of {“OFF”, “WARN”, “ERROR”}. Multiple
flags must be passed to enable or disable multiple checks. The last flag for a
specific check wins.</p>

<p>Examples of usage follow:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality  <span class="o">[</span>turns on ReferenceEquality check with the severity level from its BugPattern annotation]
<span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality:OFF  <span class="o">[</span>turns off ReferenceEquality check]
<span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality:WARN  <span class="o">[</span>turns on ReferenceEquality check as a warning]
<span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality:ERROR  <span class="o">[</span>turns on ReferenceEquality check as an error]
<span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality:OFF <span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality  <span class="o">[</span>turns on ReferenceEquality check]
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>There are also a few blanket severity-changing flags:</p>

<ul>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepAllErrorsAsWarnings</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepAllSuggestionsAsWarnings</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepAllDisabledChecksAsWarnings</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepDisableAllChecks</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepDisableAllWarnings</code></li>
  <li><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepDisableWarningsInGeneratedCode</code> : Disables warnings in classes
annotated with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@Generated</code></li>
</ul>

<p>With any of the blanket flags, you can pass additional flags afterward to tweak
the level of individual checks. E.g., this flag combination disables all checks
except for ReferenceEquality:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">-XepDisableAllChecks</span> <span class="nt">-Xep</span>:ReferenceEquality:ERROR
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Additionally, you can completely exclude certain paths from any Error Prone
checking via the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepExcludedPaths</code> flag. The flag takes as an argument a
regular expression that is matched against a source file’s path to determine
whether it should be excluded. So, to exclude files in any sub-directory of a
path containing <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">build/generated</code>, use the option:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">-XepExcludedPaths</span>:.<span class="k">*</span>/build/generated/.<span class="k">*</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>If you pass a flag that refers to an unknown check name, by default Error Prone
will throw an error. You can allow the use of unknown check names by passing the
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepIgnoreUnknownCheckNames</code> flag.</p>

<p>We no longer support the old-style Error Prone disabling flags that used the
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Xepdisable:&lt;checkName&gt;</code> syntax.</p>

<h3 id="patching">Patching</h3>

<p>There are a couple of flags for configuration of patching in suggested fixes,
e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepPatchChecks:VALUE</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepPatchLocation:VALUE</code>. See the
<a href="https://errorprone.info/docs/patching">patching docs</a> for more info.</p>

<h3 id="pass-additional-info-to-bugcheckers">Pass Additional Info to BugCheckers</h3>

<p>To configure checks, you can use custom flags to pass info directly to
BugCheckers. A valid custom flag looks like this:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">-XepOpt</span>:[Namespace:]FlagName[<span class="o">=</span>Value]
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>By convention, if a flag is only relevant to one check or a group of checks, to
prevent name collision, you should prefix your flag’s name with an optional
namespace and a colon, e.g. <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepOpt:JUnit4TestNotRun:ExpandedHeuristic=true</code>.</p>

<p>If a flag is set with no value provided, that flag is set to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">true</code>, e.g.
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepOpt:MakeAwesome</code> is equivalent to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-XepOpt:MakeAwesome=true</code>.</p>

<p>Some examples:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">-XepOpt</span>:FlagName<span class="o">=</span>SomeValue        <span class="o">(</span>flags[<span class="s2">"FlagName"</span><span class="o">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"SomeValue"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nt">-XepOpt</span>:BooleanFlag               <span class="o">(</span>flags[<span class="s2">"BooleanFlag"</span><span class="o">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"true"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nt">-XepOpt</span>:ListFlag<span class="o">=</span>1,2,3            <span class="o">(</span>flags[<span class="s2">"ListFlag"</span><span class="o">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"1,2,3"</span><span class="o">)</span>
<span class="nt">-XepOpt</span>:Namespace:SomeFlag<span class="o">=</span>AValue <span class="o">(</span>flags[<span class="s2">"Namespace:SomeFlag"</span><span class="o">]</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"AValue"</span><span class="o">)</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>These flags can be accessed in a BugChecker just by adding a one-argument
constructor that takes an <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">ErrorProneFlags</code> object, like so:</p>

<div class="language-java highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">class</span> <span class="nc">MyChecker</span> <span class="kd">extends</span> <span class="nc">BugChecker</span> <span class="kd">implements</span> <span class="nc">SomeTreeMatcher</span> <span class="o">{</span>

  <span class="kd">private</span> <span class="kd">final</span> <span class="kt">boolean</span> <span class="n">coolness</span><span class="o">;</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nf">MyChecker</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="nc">ErrorProneFlags</span> <span class="n">flags</span><span class="o">)</span> <span class="o">{</span>
    <span class="c1">// The ErrorProneFlags get* methods return an Optional&lt;*&gt;, use</span>
    <span class="c1">// Optional.orElse(...) and related methods to get with default, etc.</span>
    <span class="k">this</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">coolness</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">flags</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="na">getBoolean</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="s">"ErrorProne:IsCool"</span><span class="o">).</span><span class="na">orElse</span><span class="o">(</span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="o">);</span>
  <span class="o">}</span>

  <span class="kd">public</span> <span class="nc">Description</span> <span class="nf">matchSomething</span><span class="o">(...)</span> <span class="o">{...}</span>
<span class="o">}</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<h2 id="configuration-file">Configuration file</h2>

<p>All arguments that are passed as <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Xep*</code> after <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Xplugin:ErrorProne</code> can also be
passed through a configuration file using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@</code>.</p>

<p>This allows easier sharing of errorprone configurations between various build
systems (cli, maven, gradle, bazel, etc) and works around platform-dependent
line wrapping rules.</p>

<p>The configuration file allows <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#</code> as comment, both full line and inline.</p>

<p>Example:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>-XepAllErrorsAsWarnings
-XepAllSuggestionsAsWarnings
-XepDisableWarningsInGeneratedCode
# This library back-ports `java.time`, so we need the old APIs
-Xep:JavaUtilDate:OFF
# Bug #123
-Xep:JUnit4TestNotRun:OFF
# Indends and trailing spaces are OK:
   -Xep:MisusedDayOfYear:WARN
   -Xep:MisusedWeekYear:WARN
# Several flags in one single line are OK:
-Xep:EffectivelyPrivate:OFF -Xep:ReturnValueIgnored:OFF   -Xep:EmptyBlockTag:OFF
# Empty lines are OK

-Xep:ReturnValueIgnored:WARN # Inline comments are OK
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Using it in command line:</p>

<div class="language-bash highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>@~/project/errorprone.cfg
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>NOTE: The <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">~</code> in the example above will not work in Windows, or Gradle, or
Maven, as it is expanded by the shell. You will need to use the methods specific
to your platform and build system.</p>

<p>NOTE: It is supported to pass a mixture of flags and several arguments files.
The final value of a flag will be the one set that last time, regardless of
whether that was done directly or in an arguments file.</p>

<h2 id="maven">Maven</h2>

<p>To pass Error Prone flags to Maven, use the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">compilerArgs</code> parameter in the
plugin’s configuration. The flags must be appended to the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">arg</code> entry containing
<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">-Xplugin:ErrorProne</code>. To enable warnings, the <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">showWarnings</code> parameter must
also be set:</p>

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">&lt;project&gt;</span>
  <span class="nt">&lt;build&gt;</span>
    <span class="nt">&lt;plugins&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;plugin&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;artifactId&gt;</span>maven-compiler-plugin<span class="nt">&lt;/artifactId&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;configuration&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;showWarnings&gt;</span>true<span class="nt">&lt;/showWarnings&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;compilerArgs&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-XDcompilePolicy=simple<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>--should-stop=ifError=FLOW<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
            <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-Xplugin:ErrorProne -Xep:DeadException:WARN -Xep:GuardedBy:OFF<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
          <span class="nt">&lt;/compilerArgs&gt;</span>
        <span class="nt">&lt;/configuration&gt;</span>
      <span class="nt">&lt;/plugin&gt;</span>
    <span class="nt">&lt;/plugins&gt;</span>
  <span class="nt">&lt;/build&gt;</span>
<span class="nt">&lt;/project&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>Be aware that when running on JDK 8 the flags cannot be wrapped across multiple
lines. JDK 9 and above do allow the flags to be separated by newlines. That is,
the second <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;arg&gt;</code> element above can also be formatted as follows on JDK 9+, but
<em>not</em> on JDK 8:</p>

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>
  -Xplugin:ErrorProne \
  -Xep:DeadException:WARN \
  -Xep:GuardedBy:OFF
<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>NOTE: using multi-line <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;arg&gt;</code>s does not work on Windows when <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&lt;fork&gt;</code> is
enabled, see https://github.com/google/error-prone/issues/4256</p>

<p>NOTE: using an argument file (with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">@</code>) allows bypassing this line wrapping bug:</p>

<div class="language-xml highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="nt">&lt;compilerArgs&gt;</span>
  ...
  <span class="nt">&lt;arg&gt;</span>-Xplugin:ErrorProne @${project.basedir}/errorprone.cfg<span class="nt">&lt;/arg&gt;</span>
<span class="nt">&lt;/compilerArgs&gt;</span>
</code></pre></div></div>

<p>And move the flags to <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">errorprone.cfg</code>:</p>

<div class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code>-Xep:DeadException:WARN
-Xep:GuardedBy:OFF
</code></pre></div></div>
